Julian Beaudion, the Democratic candidate who was challenging Republican Sen. Mike Rounds of South Dakota, announced he is dropping his election bid, a move that leaves independent candidate Brian Bengs going head-to-head against the incumbent lawmaker.

"As many of you know, we experienced a devastating house fire while continuing to navigate significant personal financial hardship," Beaudion explained in part of a lengthy statement issued Tuesday. "Through it all, my wife, Inkka, and our daughters have shown incredible strength. They have sacrificed more than anyone should ever be asked to sacrifice for a campaign. Today, my first responsibility is to them.

"After the fire, an opponent and those associated with the opponent, hit my family and I with intimidating threats to drop out of this race,' he said in the statement.

"Those attacks were personal and never about politics. The mental and physical safety of my family is my priority and for this reason alone, I step aside. This is a time for my family to heal and for South Dakota voters to choose a Senator. Not a time for me to talk of specific threats and attacks. But rest assured that time will come."

GOP GOVERNOR SURVIVES CHALLENGE FROM BITCOIN EVANGELIST IN GUBERNATORIAL RUNOFF

U.S. Senate candidate Julian Beaudion speaks during the McGovern Day Dinner hosted by the Democratic Party June 5, 2026, at the Ramkota Exhibit Hall in Sioux Falls, S.D. (USA Today Network via Reuters Connect)

Beaudion said he will not back either of the remaining candidates in the contest.

"Let me be clear, I will not be endorsing or supporting Brian Bengs in this race," he noted. "Likewise, I cannot support Senator Mike Rounds."

TRUMP ENDORSES GOP SENATOR YEARS AFTER ASSERTING 'I WILL NEVER ENDORSE THIS JERK AGAIN'

Sen. Mike Rounds, R-S.D., during votes in the U.S. Capitol June 17, 2026. (Tom Williams/CQ-Roll Call, Inc via Getty Images)

Bengs, who ran for U.S. Senate as a Democrat in 2022 but lost to GOP Sen. John Thune, said in a post on X, "I commend Julian Beaudion’s patriotic decision to make this a two-person race and put South Dakota first. Now South Dakotans who want to vote against Washington's cost-raising agenda and corruption can come together regardless of party. Let’s look forward to November and retiring Big Money Mike Rounds."

South Dakota Democratic Party Chair Shane Merrill said in a statement, "Julian would have made an outstanding U.S. Senator for South Dakota."

REPUBLICAN WHO REPORTEDLY DROPPED OUT DEFEATS TRUMP'S PICK IN KEY SWING-DISTRICT PRIMARY

U.S. Senate candidate Brian Bengs speaks during a Democratic rally Nov. 7, 2022, at the Washington Pavilion in Sioux Falls. (USA Today Network via Reuters Connect)

"Every city, town, and reservation he's visited, people truly felt like they were being heard. Julian is the kind of leader we need in Congress. He is fair, understanding and open minded. That is why he would have won in November. While I am saddened that he is leaving the race, I respect his decision to focus on his family. Thank you Julian for your dedication to the people of South Dakota," Merrill noted.

title: Cambridge announces investigation into professor accused of plagiarism
excerpt:
University says it has ‘new information’ about academic career of Jason Arday, the youngest black professor in its history

Jason Arday, the Cambridge professor accused of plagiarism and embellishment...
body_text:
University says it has ‘new information’ about academic career of Jason Arday, the youngest black professor in its history

Jason Arday, the Cambridge professor accused of plagiarism and embellishment, is to face investigation by the university after it said it received “new information” about his qualifications and career.

Cambridge initially defended Arday – the youngest black professor appointed in the university’s history, with a compelling life story of educational disadvantage – as “the victim of a vile campaign”. But as questions mounted over Arday’s own claims, the university’s leaders felt that Cambridge’s reputation was in danger.

The Guardian published its own investigation uncovering discrepancies in Arday’s public accounts involving prodigious fundraising feats as well as claims he had been targeted by knife-wielding masked intruders.

Arday first faced allegations that he plagiarised parts of his PhD thesis and other academic research late last year, and has rejected the claims. An investigation by Liverpool John Moores University, which awarded his PhD in 2015, did not uphold the charges of plagiarism but said they were probably caused by “honest and reasonable error”.

Arday has denied plagarism, telling the Guardian last week: “There have been multiple thorough investigations across several institutions as a result of the allegations, and immense scrutiny, including with an academic misconduct panel who concluded that there was no plagiarism or academic misconduct.”

The statement from the university on Wednesday evening said: “The University of Cambridge has begun an investigation following new information about Prof Arday’s academic qualifications and honorary appointments. In order to ensure a fair process, we will not comment further until this has concluded.

“Separately, there remains a number of ongoing complaints regarding academic misconduct, which are being handled in line with our misconduct in research policy. This is consistent with our previous statement on the matter.

“While we are fully aware of the public commentary and concerns around this matter, it remains vital that any process is thorough and adheres to both university policies and employment law.

“We also fully recognise that there is a person at the centre of this situation, and we continue to provide support to him.”

A spokesperson for Jesus College, Cambridge, said it was launching its own parallel “process”. “Prof Arday’s college fellowship is linked to his university role and we will fully support the university.

“Prof Arday remains a fellow during this process. We recognise that this is a very difficult time for him and his family, and ask that they are treated with compassion and respect.”

The new investigations may have been triggered by Arday’s claims that he held a string of prestigious visiting fellowships and professorships at other universities, including statements in published biographies dating back to 2018 that he was a visiting fellow or visiting professor at Ohio State University in the US. Ohio State has denied that Arday was ever employed in any role.

Biographies linked to Arday have also claimed he had visiting professorships at Durham, Glasgow, Coventry and London Metropolitan universities as well as Nelson Mandela University in South Africa.

Arday’s appointment as professor of sociology at Cambridge, at the comparatively young age of 37, received wide publicity through Arday’s life story, which includes a diagnosis of autism at the age of three, being unable to speak until he was 11, or read or write until he was 18.

Despite those factors, Arday went on to university and swiftly climbed the academic ladder. After receiving his PhD in 2015 he held academic posts at Leeds Beckett, Roehampton and Durham universities, including a brief stint at Warwick University, before being appointed professor of sociology of education at Glasgow University in 2021. By early 2023 he had sought and won appointment to a professorship at Cambridge.

Arday also claimed to have completed 30 marathons in 35 days as well as running 600 miles in six days, and raising £5m for charity over several years. After facing questions he has revised some of those claims, and instead says he was part of a funding raising group that he cannot name for legal reasons.

Arday told the Guardian he had been the target of multiple threats after his Cambridge appointment, including having a severed pig’s head delivered to his parents’ home. Subsequent investigations found no evidence to support this claim.

The controversy comes as Simon & Schuster prepares to publish Arday’s memoir later this month, entitled Great and Unfortunate Things.

title: El-Sayed campaign backed by over $100,000 from dozens of members of group with alleged terror ties
excerpt: Rep. Chip Roy, R-Texas, discusses Gov. Greg Abbott’s decision to declare CAIR and the Muslim Brotherhood as a terrorist organization and investigations into Sharia courts in the Lone Star State on ‘Th...
body_text:
Rep. Chip Roy, R-Texas, discusses Gov. Greg Abbott’s decision to declare CAIR and the Muslim Brotherhood as a terrorist organization and investigations into Sharia courts in the Lone Star State on ‘The Will Cain Show.’

FIRST ON FOX: GRAND RAPIDS, MI - Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed's campaign has collected more than $115,000 from individuals who work for or have held leadership roles with the Council on American-Islamic Relations (CAIR), which has been designated a terrorist organization by the United Arab Emirates and formally designated or labeled as such in Florida and Texas.

A Fox News Digital review found that El-Sayed, who has made getting "money out of politics" a central campaign rallying cry, has accepted donations from at least 41 individuals who either work for CAIR, formerly worked for CAIR, or have served in leadership positions with the organization.

The donor list includes several of CAIR's highest-ranking officials, including national Board Chair Manal Fakhoury, national Board Treasurer Eyas Abdeen, national Vice Chair Emad Sabbah, and CAIR-Michigan board member Jukaku Tayeb, El-Sayed's father-in-law.

Tayeb has been one of the largest financial backers of the super PAC supporting El-Sayed's campaign and is also part of the founding committee of the Islamic Society of North America (ISNA), a group linked to Hamas and Muslim Brotherhood funding, Washington Free Beacon first reported.

DEMS CLASH OVER AIPAC MONEY, ‘OGRE’ ATTACK AND ELECTABILITY DURING CRUCIAL SENATE DEBATE

Abdul El-Sayed speaks during a Democratic primary election-night event in his race against Haley Stevens on Wednesday, Aug. 5, 2026, at the Majestic Theatre in Detroit. (Julia Demaree Nikhinson/AP Photo)

One donor, CAIR Executive Director Nihad Awad, listed in FEC records under the name Nehad Hammad, drew national condemnation after saying he was "happy" to see Hamas break out of Gaza on Oct. 7, 2023, and arguing Israel "does not have the right to self-defense" as an occupying power.

The contributions were not limited to Michigan. Fox News Digital identified donations from CAIR national leaders and officials affiliated with chapters in California, Arizona, Texas, Georgia, Washington, Illinois, Minnesota and Ohio, among other states, illustrating the breadth of support El-Sayed received from within the organization's leadership ranks.

Other names on the donor list include CAIR-California Governance Board Treasurer Rubina Alvi, CAIR-California Governance Board Chair Asaad Traina, CAIR-Michigan board member Muzammil Ahmed, who contributed $11,600 to El-Sayed's campaign, CAIR-California Governance Board member Atef Ibrahim, CAIR-California Governance Board member Dina Ezzeddine, and former CAIR National Board Chair Roula Allouch.

EL-SAYED PALS AROUND WITH FAR-LEFT STREAMER HASAN PIKER THE DAY BEFORE CRUCIAL MICHIGAN SENATE ELECTION

Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed poses for a portrait in Grand Rapids, Michigan, on Saturday, Feb. 21, 2026. (Evan Cobb for The Washington Post via Getty Images)

El-Sayed has maintained ties to CAIR beyond campaign fundraising. In 2022, he appeared at a CAIR event and was paid for a speaking engagement, where he criticized Oklahoma's ban on Sharia law and compared it to the Trail of Tears, Washington Free Beacon reported.

CAIR has long been the subject of controversy over its alleged ties to Hamas. In 2007, federal prosecutors named the organization an unindicted co-conspirator in the Holy Land Foundation terrorism financing case, the largest terrorism financing prosecution in U.S. history.

Although CAIR was never charged with a crime, federal prosecutors argued the organization was part of a network created to support Hamas in the United States. CAIR has denied the allegations and has challenged its inclusion as an unindicted co-conspirator.

In recent years, Florida and Texas have formally designated or labeled CAIR a terrorist organization, while the United Arab Emirates designated the group a terrorist organization in 2014 which is widely understood to stem from the UAE's view that CAIR has ties to the Muslim Brotherhood.

In response to Fox News Digital's request for comment, CAIR denied allegations that it has ties to terrorism, citing its "Dispelling Rumors About CAIR" webpage and a memorandum stating it has "repeatedly condemned antisemitism throughout our 30 years of existence" and has "for decades" maintained a statement condemning "terrorist attacks committed by Hamas and other designated terrorist groups."

CAIR also highlighted a previous statement "has appeared on CAIR’s website since 2009" saying, "We unequivocally condemn all acts of terrorism, whether carried out by al-Qa’ida, the Real IRA, FARC, Hamas, ETA, or any other group designated by the U.S. Department of State as a ‘Foreign Terrorist Organization."

Additionally, CAIR cited a National Board statement condemning antisemitism and the Oct. 7, 2023, attacks, along with a 2023 editorial in which National Executive Director Nihad Awad said he agreed with the organization's condemnation of attacks on civilians.

Fox News Digital reached out to the El-Sayed campaign for comment.

Hussam Ayloush, an executive director of CAIR, speaks during a press conference. (Marc Martin/Los Angeles Times via Getty Images)

El-Sayed has repeatedly drawn criticism from Republicans and pro-Israel advocates over his associations and comments related to the Middle East, including campaigning with far-left streamer Hasan Piker, his response to an attack targeting a Detroit synagogue, and declining to comment on the death of Iran's supreme leader, citing constituents in Dearborn who were mourning.

El-Sayed defeated Dem. Rep. Haley Stevens in the Democratic Senate primary on Tuesday night in a race that was much closer than most pundits expected. El-Sayed will face off against Republican Mike Rogers, a former congressman, in November.

Andrew Mark Miller is a reporter at Fox News. Find him on Twitter @andymarkmiller and email tips to AndrewMark.Miller@Fox.com.

title: Schumer claims victory as Senate moves to avert shutdown; GOP says he got played
excerpt:
Tensions rise in Washington over a potential government shutdown by Oct. 1.

The Senate quietly moved its solution to halt a government shutdown through another key step as the tenuous truce between R...
body_text:
Tensions rise in Washington over a potential government shutdown by Oct. 1.

The Senate quietly moved its solution to halt a government shutdown through another key step as the tenuous truce between Republicans and Democrats continues to hold.

In the midst of a hectic, albeit open-ended and uncertainty-laden schedule, the upper chamber advanced its continuing resolution (CR) unanimously on Wednesday.

While not the final vote, it’s a strong sign that neither side wants to thrust the federal government into uncertainty as the midterms near.

It marks a sharp departure from the shutdown politics of the last year and follows Senate Republicans' hand-wringing for months that Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., would once again lead his caucus to the brink and shut the government down for political gain.

DEMOCRATS BLINK AS SCHUMER HELPS GOP CLEAR KEY SHUTDOWN HURDLE

Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., speaks during a news conference after Senate Democratic policy luncheons at the U.S. Capitol in Washington, D.C., June 23, 2026. (Daniel Heuer/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

And Schumer is saying that Democrats have wanted to keep the lights on in a bipartisan manner all along.

He contended that the CR, negotiated between the top Republican and Democrat on the Senate Appropriations Committee, was a major victory for Democrats, particularly for its design to "stave off Trump's disgraceful effort to withhold federal grants from vital projects."

"I mean, what kind of country is this? You have two identical projects, one in a red state and one in a blue state funded the same way, same clean record," Schumer said. "He cancels the blue state one and says the red state one is OK."

TRUMP ADMIN PAUSING OVER $1B IN MEDICAID PAYMENTS TO MINNESOTA, CALIFORNIA OVER FRAUD, COMPLIANCE CONCERNS

The Office of Management and Budget (OMB) and the Trump administration are pushing for more control over federal grants, which critics like Schumer and others warn could be used as a political cudgel to dictate which states do and don’t get a flow of federal dollars.

If the CR passes and is signed by Trump, it will pause that rule change until Dec. 11, when the stopgap expires.

But Republicans say it’s not quite the victory Schumer thinks it is.

BOMB-THROWER DEM MAKES SHOCKING PROMISE TO KICK SCHUMER TO CURB DURING SENATE DEBATE

Sen. John Kennedy, R-La., is urging the Senate to craft the SAVE America Act into a budget reconciliation bill passable by a simple majority instead of the 60-vote filibuster. (Anna Moneymaker/Pool/AFP)

Sen. John Kennedy, R-La., countered that Schumer may think he won with the deal, but, in reality, it just delayed the inevitable for the White House’s plans for grant-funded projects.

"I think he's going to go back to his base and say, ‘I got the OMB rule killed,’" Kennedy said. "Well, he didn’t. I mean, I've talked to [OMB Director] Russ Vought, and the president this morning about that, and the rule can be ready by Dec. 11. So, no harm, no foul."

Alex Miller is a writer for Fox News Digital covering the U.S. Senate.

title: New York City transit auctions off last MetroCard machines: ‘Wild home decor idea’
excerpt:
MTA to sell remaining machines – which weigh up to 1,050lbs – as it transitions to contactless fare system

The Metropolitan Transportation Authority (MTA) of New York City has begun auctioning off it...
body_text:
MTA to sell remaining machines – which weigh up to 1,050lbs – as it transitions to contactless fare system

The Metropolitan Transportation Authority (MTA) of New York City has begun auctioning off its final MetroCard vending machines, offering New Yorkers the chance to own one of the transit system’s most recognizable fixtures as the agency continues its transition to Omny.

The auction opened on Wednesday morning and will run through 19 August, according to the MTA. The agency is offering a limited number of retired MetroCard Vending Machines (MVM) and MetroCard Express Machines (MEM), which have served subway riders for decades.

“First installed in 1999, the colorful metal MVM and MEM are familiar to the millions of riders who take the subway each day,” the MTA said in a news release.

The MTA’s media liaison, Joana Flores, confirmed the agency was auctioning off the very last of the machines.

“Today, we began auctioning off the last MetroCard vending machines. There are a total of 60,” Flores said. The last remaining public-facing machine is located in Greenwich Village’s Mulry Square, she said, and now displays a QR code for commuters to scan should they be interested in making a bid.

The larger MetroCard vending machines, first installed in 1999, allowed riders to buy and reload MetroCards using cash, credit and debit cards. Each machine measures 80in long, 42in wide and 36in deep (203cm x 107cm x 91cm), and weighs 1,050lbs (476kg).

The smaller MetroCard express machines, introduced later to ease congestion at busy stations by accepting only credit and debit card payments, measure 21in long, 14in wide and 42in, and weigh about 210lb.

The MTA said the machines were being sold as-is in non-operational condition after their electronic and payment processing components were removed. Successful bidders will be required to pay in full on the day they are notified and arrange pickup within 10 days. Buyers are responsible for loading and transporting the heavy machines.

Flores said the MTA was also holding a public sweepstake in conjunction with the auction. Fifteen people will be selected in a random draw that allows the winners to skip the line at the agency’s annual transit memorabilia pop-up sale in October, along with a 20% discount on purchases.

She added that any remaining vending machines not sold through the auction will be sold online through GovDeals. But the agency does not anticipate any will be left by then, Flores said: “Usually, these things are hot-ticket items – they tend to go fast.”

The MetroCard, once synonymous with being a New York subway commuter, was also a popular vehicle for promotions, with the city issuing several commemorative editions, including one to mark baseball’s home-team World Series between the Mets and the Yankees in 2000.

Many famous musicians graced the card over the years, such as David Bowie, Olivia Rodrigo, the Wu-Tang Clan, the Notorious BIG and LL Cool J, as did New York-centric TV shows such as Seinfeld and Law & Order.

Some social media users have already expressed interest in placing bids, with commenters responding “Wild home decor idea” and “So tempted by this”.

The NPR gameshow host Peter Sagal wrote: “I haven’t been a New Yorker since 1998 but I really, really want one.”

The auction comes as the MTA continues replacing MetroCards with Omny, its contactless fare payment system.

“We’re no longer selling MetroCards, but we are accepting MetroCards,” Flores said. There is no date yet for when the transit system plans to fully convert to contactless payments and stop accepting the classic yellow cards, but Flores said there will come a day when the agency will “transition fully over to the tap and ride system”.

title: Hasan Piker unloads on 'Islamophobic pieces of s---' Democrats as El-Sayed faces party unity test
excerpt:
Hasan Piker accused Abdul El-Sayed’s Democratic critics of Islamophobia and demanded they "lock the f--- in," even as the Michigan Senate nominee pledged to "mend fences" after winning the primary.

L...
body_text:
Hasan Piker accused Abdul El-Sayed’s Democratic critics of Islamophobia and demanded they "lock the f--- in," even as the Michigan Senate nominee pledged to "mend fences" after winning the primary.

Left-wing Twitch streamer Hasan Piker rejected calls for Abdul El-Sayed to repair relationships with skeptical Democrats during the candidate’s Tuesday night election event at the Majestic Theatre in Detroit, even as El-Sayed promised reconciliation ahead of the general election against Republican Mike Rogers.

"Like everyone being like, Abdul has a f--- ton of work to do mending bridges. Here's the f---ing take nuke for you, OK? You are all unbelievably Islamophobic pieces of s---, OK?" Piker said.

El-Sayed struck a conciliatory tone before the race was called, telling supporters his campaign would begin reconciling with Democrats who backed Rep. Haley Stevens, D-Mich., in the bitter primary.

In his victory speech on Wednesday, he praised Stevens as a dedicated public servant.

Hasan Piker lashed out at Democrats who opposed Abdul El-Sayed during the Senate candidate’s election night event in Detroit. (Fox News Digital/Paul Steinhauser)

DEM PRIMARY ERUPTS AS ESTABLISHMENT FAVORITE DISMISSES RIVAL AS ‘CELEBRITY CANDIDATE’

Piker accused El-Sayed’s critics of spending months branding the former Wayne County health director a terrorist, misogynist and fake doctor before demanding that he win them over.

"Like, what are you talking about? Do you want to f---ing win or not? Lock the f--- in, OK? Lock the f--- in," Piker said.

Piker also framed questions about whether El-Sayed could unite Democrats as a test of whether pro-Israel organizations, consultants and voters would stop attacking the nominee long enough to defeat Rogers.

"And that question is just can El-Sayed get the pro-Israel vote? Can El-Sayed win over, not even the vote necessarily, but like can El-Sayed get the people and the group," Piker said.

Piker accused El-Sayed’s primary critics of Islamophobia and demanded Democrats unite behind the nominee against Republican Mike Rogers. (Sportsfile via Getty Images)

EL-SAYED PALS AROUND WITH FAR-LEFT STREAMER HASAN PIKER THE DAY BEFORE CRUCIAL MICHIGAN SENATE ELECTION

"Groups and the NGOs and the consultants that have worked extensively for pro-Israel candidates to shut the f--- up about El-Sayed being a terrorist for a long enough timeline so that you know we can consolidate the base and defeat the f---ing Republican."

Moms Demand Action founder Shannon Watts highlighted Piker’s message to Democrats who supported Stevens or another primary candidate.

"Hasan Piker’s message to Dems who didn’t vote for El-Sayed: ‘You are all unbelievably Islamophobic pieces of s---,’" Watts said on X.

Rob Flaherty, ex-White House digital strategy director for former President Joe Biden, urged El-Sayed to disregard Piker as the nominee pivoted toward the general election.

El-Sayed called for Democrats to mend fences after winning the primary, and Hasan Piker’s remarks drew criticism from across the political spectrum. (Sarah Rice/Getty Images)

REPUBLICANS GET THE DEMOCRAT THEY WANTED AS SOCIALIST ABDUL EL-SAYED WINS MICHIGAN SENATE PRIMARY

"I am not a Hasan-doomer, and I think he has an important place in the ecosystem, but I hope he and the pool party crowd head back to LA and let Abdul ignore this very bad advice," Flaherty said.

Conservative commentator Guy Benson characterized Piker as a leading surrogate addressing Democratic voters.

"Dems’ top surrogate to many Dem voters: ‘You are all unbelievably Islamophobic pieces of s---,’" Benson said.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

El-Sayed repeatedly campaigned with Piker, including at college campus rallies and a Detroit pool party Monday for content creators supporting his campaign. Stevens urged El-Sayed to distance himself from the streamer, whose previous remarks about the Sept. 11 attacks, Hamas and Mao Zedong have drawn criticism.

The Associated Press declared El-Sayed the winner Wednesday after he narrowly defeated Stevens in a contest that attracted more than $80 million in spending. He will face Rogers for the seat being vacated by retiring Democratic Sen. Gary Peters.

CJ joined Fox News Digital's team in 2026, which highlights the vital role journalism plays in shaping politics and culture. He has years of experience analyzing and reporting on the news media.

CJ graduated from Long Beach State University in 2025 with a Bachelor of Arts in Political Science and a minor in Journalism.

title: Grocer-turned-lawmaker says Mamdani’s government-run stores 'might not even last a year’
excerpt: Rep. Mike Rulli, R-Ohio, whose family owns Rulli Brothers grocery stores, spoke with Fox News Digital about President Trump's call on stores to lower prices, and New York City's government-run grocery...
body_text:
Rep. Mike Rulli, R-Ohio, whose family owns Rulli Brothers grocery stores, spoke with Fox News Digital about President Trump's call on stores to lower prices, and New York City's government-run grocery stores.

A former grocer is joining the chorus of criticism against New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani's plan for government-run grocery stores, arguing it would harm hundreds of small businesses forced to compete with them.

"That supermarket will just bleed red the entire time it's open, from the first time you turn the key until it closes," Rep. Mike Rulli, R-Ohio, told Fox News Digital. "And I would bet the farm there's no way these grocery stores last more than five years — they might not even last a year."

Rulli grew up with his family's Ohio-based grocery store chain, Rulli Brothers, which is now run by his brothers.

EXPERTS SCORCH MAMDANI'S GROCERY PLAN AS AN 'ILLUSION' THAT WILL HAVE TAXPAYERS FOOTING THE BILL

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani holds up bananas as he speaks at a food distribution center on July 27, 2026 in the Brooklyn borough of New York City. (Spencer Platt/Getty Images)

Rulli said his family's small but thriving two-location business has given him an appreciation for the challenges facing small business owners in New York City, whom he argued would be harmed by competition from Mamdani's city-run stores.

"You will put hundreds of these small businesses out of business. And a lot of these businesses are owned by immigrants," Rulli said. "So I mean, I don't think the mayor could possibly have asked for a worse situation."

NY GOVERNOR HOPEFUL VOWS SHOWDOWN WITH MAMDANI OVER SOCIALIST AGENDA: ‘I WILL STOP HIM’

Mamdani, the Democratic socialist mayor of New York City, unveiled a plan for government-funded grocery stores while on the campaign trail. The city has since committed $70 million to constructing one store in each of the five boroughs, with an aim to open all five by 2030.

Rep. Michael Rulli, R-Ohio, testifies during a House Subcommittee on Railroads, Pipelines, and Hazardous Materials hearing on "Rail safety in the aftermath of the East Palestine, Ohio, derailment" in Washington, District of Columbia, on July 23, 2024. (Samuel Corum/Getty Images)

Mamdani discussed the agreement during a recent news conference, saying, "Once a month, our five city-run grocery stores will set prices for this core set of goods at 30% below typical retail prices."

MAMDANI’S CITY GROCERY PLAN COULD LEAVE TAXPAYERS PAYING FOR EVERY BANANA

While the plan has been cheered by progressives, it has been panned by business groups such as the Multicultural Business Coalition, which the New York Post reported was threatening to sue Mamdani.

Rulli, noting that grocery stores already operate on thin profit margins, said Mamdani's government shops will likely be "operating at a loss the entire time."

"When you think about the grocery industry, [it] runs on about 27% gross. That's before you pay your bills. Once you pay your bills, you're about one-and-a-quarter, one-and-half-percent net," he said.

That, he argued, would make it a drain on taxpayers as long as they remained open.

"This is the biggest mistake the mayor has made," Rulli said.

Elizabeth Elkind is a politics reporter for Fox News Digital leading coverage of the House of Representatives. Previous digital bylines seen at Daily Mail and CBS News.

title: MIKE PENCE: Congress must finish Lindsey Graham’s fight against Putin
excerpt:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy discusses the Russia-Ukraine war and reflects on the late Sen. Lindsey Graham's, R-S.C., support for his country on 'Hannity.'

Freedom has lost one of its fier...
body_text:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy discusses the Russia-Ukraine war and reflects on the late Sen. Lindsey Graham's, R-S.C., support for his country on 'Hannity.'

Freedom has lost one of its fiercest defenders, and I have lost a dear friend.

For more than three decades, South Carolina Republican Sen. Lindsey Graham stood at the center of the great debates over our nation’s security and America’s role in the world. He understood that peace is preserved not by wishful thinking, but by American strength. He knew that dictators are not pacified by concessions, but deterred by unshakable resolve.

History will remember his many accomplishments. The Senate has already taken an important step toward securing one more by overwhelmingly advancing his legislation. Now it must complete its work, and the House must act without delay.

GRAHAM'S FINAL MISSION ADVANCES AS SENATE MOVES TO CRUSH PUTIN'S WAR MACHINE WITH RUSSIA, IRAN SANCTIONS

Congress has an opportunity to ensure that one of his greatest achievements is still to come.

The Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 is more than just another sanctions bill. It is the culmination of Lindsey’s determined effort to deny Russian President Vladimir Putin the money, technology and international support fueling Russia’s brutal and unconscionable war against Ukraine. Passing it would not simply honor his memory. It would advance the cause to which he devoted the final chapter of his public life.

Lindsey Graham understood that half-measures would never change Vladimir Putin’s calculations.

More than four years after Russia launched its unprovoked war of conquest, Putin continues to finance his war machine through energy exports, financial networks and an elaborate system of sanctions evasion. Existing sanctions have imposed real costs, but they have not been enough. Putin and his henchmen have adapted. Russia has built a shadow fleet of ships to move its oil around the world. It has relied on foreign companies to sustain its defense-industrial base. And too many nations continue to purchase Russian energy with their money while condemning Russian aggression with their words.

Lindsey understood that half-measures would never change Putin’s calculations.

REPORT WARNS RUSSIA USING SHADOW FLEET TO PROBE NATO DRONE DEFENSES

His legislation would impose mandatory sanctions on Russia’s political leadership, financial institutions, state-owned energy enterprises and the networks helping Moscow evade existing restrictions. It would target the shadow fleet transporting Russian oil, tighten financial and export controls, and use targeted tariffs to encourage the world’s largest purchasers of Russian energy to end their support for the Kremlin’s war machine. Just as importantly, it preserves presidential waiver authority when a waiver serves America’s national interest, ensuring that strength remains guided by sound judgment.

At its heart, this legislation is about restoring the deterrence that keeps dictators from mistaking American restraint for weakness.

History has taught us repeatedly that unchecked aggression only invites more aggression. Every barrel of oil sold through sanctions evasion, every financial transaction that slips through the cracks and every dollar flowing into the Kremlin’s coffers help finance missiles and drones that rain terror on Ukrainian cities and encourage other authoritarian regimes to test the resolve of the free world.

ZELENSKYY SAYS PUTIN 'LOST THE INITIATIVE' AS UKRAINE'S TECH INDUSTRY RESHAPES THE WAR

Lindsey Graham believed America should never shrink from that challenge. He knew that the United States must lead, our allies must stand together and our adversaries must know that freedom has both the will and the means to defend itself.

One of Lindsey’s last acts in public life was to travel to Kyiv and meet with President Volodymyr Zelenskyy to express America’s continued support for the long-suffering Ukrainian people. He believed this legislation could help bring Putin to the negotiating table and hasten the day when this terrible war finally ends. I believe he was right.

Congress can pay tribute to Lindsey Graham with eloquent speeches and heartfelt memorials. Those are certainly fitting. But the tribute that would matter most to Lindsey would be finishing the work he began.

It’s time for Congress to pass the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026. Let’s complete his final mission.

CLICK HERE TO READ MORE FROM FORMER VICE PRESIDENT MIKE PENCE

Mike Pence is the former vice president of the United States and founder of Advancing American Freedom.

title: FAA investigates air ‘safety incident’ involving Trump’s Marine One
excerpt:
Controllers allegedly failed to halt flights, leading to a ‘loss of separation’ with a departing passenger jet

An air “safety incident” in which Donald Trump’s Marine One helicopter came closer than ...
body_text:
Controllers allegedly failed to halt flights, leading to a ‘loss of separation’ with a departing passenger jet

An air “safety incident” in which Donald Trump’s Marine One helicopter came closer than permitted to another aircraft over Washington DC is under investigation by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA).

Air traffic controllers are believed to have mistakenly failed to halt commercial flights at Ronald Reagan national airport in northern Virginia on Tuesday afternoon when the military helicopter lifted off from the White House with the president on board.

A “loss of separation” incident occurred in which the helicopter and a recently departed passenger jet bound for Florida came closer to each other than regulations allow, a source told Reuters. The aircraft are not believed to have been on a collision course.

The FAA said in a statement that it was “investigating a safety incident involving Marine One but it didn’t appear to be a dangerous close call and the aircraft weren’t apparently converging”.

The episode followed a tightening of proximity rules in the wake of a January 2025 collision between a commercial airliner and an army Black Hawk helicopter over the nation’s capital that killed 67 people. The government eventually admitted negligence in what was the deadliest crash on US soil in more than two decades.

The aircraft involved in Tuesday’s incident was an Embraer E170 jet operated by Envoy ​Air, a wholly owned subsidiary of American Airlines, as flight 3742 to Pensacola. Tracking website Flightaware showed it left its gate at Reagan national at 2.18pm on Tuesday, 34 minutes later than scheduled, and was in the air 16 minutes later at 2.34pm.

Marine One took off from the Ellipse near the White House at 2.33pm to take Trump to Joint Base Andrews and a flight to Los Angeles, according to a pool report.

FAA rules implemented after last year’s tragedy require aircraft to remain separated by at least ​1.5 miles horizontally and 500ft vertically around airports, and the sources told Reuters that it appeared Marine One and the plane did ​not maintain separation. One said it appears they were not converging during the incident.

Marine One and the Envoy jet continued their journeys without incident, with the Embraer landing in Pensacola at 3.33pm CT after a flight of 2hr 16min.

The Guardian has contacted the White House and American Airlines for comment.

Reuters ‌learned from its sources, who were speaking under the condition of anonymity, that the FAA planned to convene a safety review team to investigate the incident.

A third aircraft, regional flight Republic 4700 from North Carolina’s Raleigh-Durham international airport to Washington DC, was three miles (5 km) from Reagan national at the time of the incident and was ordered to fly around before landing at 2.52pm, one of the sources said, confirmed by Flightaware tracking.

The FAA ⁠imposed permanent restrictions on helicopter operations around Reagan national following last year’s mid-air collision. The US government conceded in December in a response to a lawsuit filed by one of the victims’ families that failures of the FAA and army played a role in the crash.

“The United States admits that it owed a duty of care to plaintiffs, which it breached, thereby proximately causing the tragic accident,” it said.

The ​National Transportation Safety Board said in January that a series of systemic failures by the FAA led ​to the collision, ⁠citing its decision to allow helicopters to travel close to the airport with no safeguards to separate them from airplanes.

The FAA has since banned mixed helicopter and jet traffic around the airport, and commercial traffic is typically halted when Marine One is in flight around ⁠the airport.

title: Rand Paul's calls for Fauci to to face imprisonment continue after contentious hearing
excerpt:
Sen. Rand Paul, R-Ky., was asked on MS NOW's "Morning Joe" whether he still believes that Anthony Fauci should be jailed after a recent Senate hearing.

Sen. Rand Paul, R-Ky., has frequently suggested...
body_text:
Sen. Rand Paul, R-Ky., was asked on MS NOW's "Morning Joe" whether he still believes that Anthony Fauci should be jailed after a recent Senate hearing.

Sen. Rand Paul, R-Ky., has frequently suggested that Dr. Anthony Fauci should face prison time, and he was still open to the idea Tuesday when pressed about his past calls on that front.

Paul spoke on MS NOW about his response to the former director of the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases invoking the Fifth Amendment more than 100 times during a Senate hearing chaired by Paul last week.

The Republican senator admitted that he didn't know what to expect from Fauci's testimony, arguing that Fauci likely could have escaped legal culpability under former President Joe Biden's pardon. Geist remarked that Fauci, under the guidance of his lawyers, likely wanted to avoid speaking to Paul, who has advocated for him to be jailed. He followed up by asking if he still believes in that.

CAN FAUCI HIDE BEHIND THE FIFTH? GAME-CHANGING BIDEN PARDON MAY NOT PROVIDE COMPLETE COVER, EXPERTS SAY

Sen. Rand Paul reiterated on "Morning Joe" that Anthony Fauci should face consequences for his role in gain-of-function research. (AP Photo/J. Scott Applewhite)

"That's a good question," Paul said. "Did he lie to Congress? I think he did lie to Congress. And I think, to be fair, that people who lie to Congress should be charged with a felony and, if convicted, go to jail. That’s also a felony crime. So I think both destroying records and lying to Congress are serious crimes."

Paul explained that it was more important to him to learn the truth about the gain-of-function research allegedly connected to Fauci prior to the COVID-19 pandemic.

Geist then asked if anyone else should face a criminal investigation. Paul stopped short of suggesting legal ramifications but added that they "should all apologize" and were culpable in other ways.

Turning back to Fauci, Geist asked Paul if he believed the doctor had some "nefarious" purpose behind his actions.

WATCH: RAND PAUL SAYS THERE'S ONE THING AMERICANS HAVE NEVER HEARD FROM FAUCI

Rand Paul has repeatedly suggested Dr. Anthony Fauci committed a felony. (Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images)

"I would say it's wrongheaded. I'm not sure I would use the word 'nefarious.' I would say that he is of the belief that the common man can't handle the truth, and that people like him who are the science, the elite, and the experts should make decisions," Paul said, pointing to Fauci's shifting comments regarding masks.

He added that Fauci was telling "lies, platonic lies, because he's one of the philosopher kings. So it really is about an attitude, but it is an arrogance, and it is an arrogance that shouldn't go unchallenged."

Fox News Digital reached out to Fauci and Paul's office for further comment.

RAND PAUL SEEKS CONTEMPT CHARGES AFTER FAUCI INVOKES FIFTH AMENDMENT MORE THAN 100 TIMES

In 2021, Paul told "Hannity" that lying about gain-of-function research is a felony "punishable by five years in jail." The controversial method refers to manipulating or altering an organism or virus for purposes of research, which could give it enhanced abilities.

"We’ve referred it to the Department of Justice," Paul said. "I don’t think Biden’s Department of Justice will do anything with it but yes, it is very dangerous to have public officials who we need to have trust in coming and lying to us, but he has lied dozens of times."

Anthony Fauci declined to testify in a Senate committee hearing on his role in the US response to Covid-19, invoking his 5th Amendment rights. (Alex Wroblewski / AFP via Getty Images; Al Drago/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

Paul directly told Fox News' Laura Ingraham in 2024 that Fauci's consequence should be jail.

"I think he lied to Congress, which is a felony. You know, several folks from the Trump administration were accused of lying to Congress and carted off to jail with FBI agents all over the property, host, you know, yanking them out of their house early in the morning," he said. "But Anthony Fauci did lie to Congress. We know that from his own words, not because I say lies, but his private email say he was lying. Virtually everything he said in private contradicted what he was saying in public."

Lindsay Kornick is an associate editor for Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to lindsay.kornick@fox.com and on Twitter: @lmkornick.

title: Nigeria's president orders a 80% salary increase for junior soldiers
excerpt:
Nigerian soldiers are fighting multiple enemies, including Islamist militants, separatists and gangs that kidnap civilians for ransom

Nigerian soldiers are to get a pay increase of up to 80% - their ...
body_text:
Nigerian soldiers are fighting multiple enemies, including Islamist militants, separatists and gangs that kidnap civilians for ransom

Nigerian soldiers are to get a pay increase of up to 80% - their second salary increase in a month - for what President Bola Tinubu says is the government's "deep appreciation" of those battling the nation's enormous security threats.

In July, the defence minister raised the monthly wages for privates, the lowest-ranking soldiers, from $36 (£27) to $73. With the president's intervention they will now receive $132 from September.

It is part of Tinubu's efforts to curb violence from various armed groups, including Islamist militants and criminal kidnap gangs, known locally as "bandits".

Last month, he ordered the recruitment of 28,000 extra soldiers and the creation of four new army divisions.

Continuing insecurity nationwide has become a major political issue ahead of the 2027 elections.

The kidnap gangs, jihadists and separatists wreaking havoc in Nigeria

Nigeria's president approves largest military expansion in recent times

Announcing the salary hikes, the president praised the courage and sacrifices of members of the armed forces confronting "the scourge of banditry, kidnapping and terrorism".

"The men and women who help to keep us safe in our homes must be supported and appreciated in the course of their duties to our nation," he said in a statement.

"I urge our servicemen to take our gesture as a sign of our deep appreciation of the services they render to our fatherland. Together we shall prevail over the enemies intent on destroying the fabric of our nation."

Successive Nigerian governments have struggled to contain insecurity despite increased military deployments and spending.

Islamist insurgents, including Boko Haram and the Islamic State West Africa Province (Iswap), continue to stage attacks in the north-east, while heavily armed criminal gangs - which loot and kidnap for ransom - operate across parts of north-west and north-central areas.

Other security challenges include separatist unrest in the south-east and deadly clashes over land between farmers and herders.

The most junior personnel are to receive the biggest salary hike:

This will see the military's annual wage bill jump from $484m to $678m.

"This is what we have been calling for a long time," military expert Bashir Galma, a retired major general, told the BBC.

Though he expressed concern that future administrations might struggle to sustain such funding, given the significant jump in the military's annual salary bill.

Serving personnel approached for comment have said they will reserve judgment until the new salaries are reflected in their bank accounts.

Galma also argued that other security agencies should receive similar pay reviews, stressing that "keeping the country safe is a joint effort".

Beyond salaries, he said broader welfare issues also required attention including uniforms, boots and, most critically, new rifles to tackle the ongoing crises.

"All these are also important areas," he said.

Tinubu has said his administration will continue to prioritise troop welfare and to modernise the armed forces with the weapons and technology needed to tackle security threats.

Under his recent reforms, the army will have now 12 divisions spread over the whole country to ensure better co-ordination, intelligence sharing and faster response times.

title: Drone carrying explosives found at German airport, police say
excerpt:
A drone carrying an explosive device has been found at a German airport, police say.

A robot was deployed at Leipzig/Halle Airport after the device was spotted in the cargo operation area overnight, ...
body_text:
A drone carrying an explosive device has been found at a German airport, police say.

A robot was deployed at Leipzig/Halle Airport after the device was spotted in the cargo operation area overnight, according to Saxony police. Some reports suggest it was near a Ukrainian aircraft.

Officers said that a second unidentified object also collided with a cargo plane after it had taken off from the airport. The plane was diverted to Hanover, where minor damage was detected.

Flights were initially suspended at the airport after the drone was detected, but one runway has since been cleared for use, while the airport's other runway was not not due to be used on Wednesday.

title: ‘Leicester Square, please guv’: Self-driving taxis cleared for London streets ‘later this summer’
excerpt:
Wayve Uber wins first minicab licence for autonomous cabs from TfL but vehicles will have a safety driver (at first)

The taxi app company Uber and the autonomous technology developer Wayve have been ...
body_text:
Wayve Uber wins first minicab licence for autonomous cabs from TfL but vehicles will have a safety driver (at first)

The taxi app company Uber and the autonomous technology developer Wayve have been granted the first minicab licences in London, allowing them to offer self-driving taxi rides to paying customers – but with a human safety driver in place, for now.

The companies said they would start trips in the UK “later this summer” before the full public launch.

The San Francisco-headquartered Uber and London-based Wayve are racing against the Google-owned Waymo and its Chinese equivalent Baidu’s Apollo Go to launch self-driving taxi services in London. Their progress is being watched closely because the British capital will be one of the first cities in the world to have American and Chinese tech firms operating on the same roads.

Uber and Wayve said more than 100,000 Londoners were on their waiting list for the self-driving taxis.

Transport for London (TfL), the capital’s licensing authority, granted 15 private hire vehicle licences to Ford Mustang Mach-E vehicles equipped with Wayve’s artificial intelligence driving software, as well as surround cameras and radar. The companies said TfL had confirmed they reached the required safety standards.

A TfL-licensed private hire driver will sit in the driver’s seat during trips to intervene if necessary, although the software is expected to control the car.

The next step, of operating the taxis without a driver, will require Uber and Wayve to seek approval via a new process, known as an automated passenger services permit, with the government’s Driver and Vehicle Standards Agency.

TfL said it would monitor the use of the vehicles, and was ready to intervene if passenger safety was compromised.

A TfL spokesperson said: “Safety is our top priority. Any new vehicle licensed to carry passengers on London’s roads must align with our Vision Zero goal of eliminating all deaths and serious injuries from collisions on London’s streets by 2041.”

Wayve, which was co-founded by the New Zealand-born Alex Kendall, has been testing its tech in London since 2018 with safety drivers. In previous demonstrations to the Guardian the car has navigated most of the obstacles of north London’s busy roads, although the safety driver was forced to intervene at one point.

Sarah Gates, Wayve’s vice-president for global affairs and assurance, said: “This licence is an important step towards giving Londoners the chance to experience autonomous driving technology.

“The responsible deployment of these vehicles will bring us safer, cleaner and quieter streets, and we’re proud to continue working alongside regulators, communities and the public as we take the next steps towards making autonomous rides a reality in the capital.”

Driverless taxi services are already operating in several cities around the world, although mainly in the US and China, where most of the software developers are based. However, US companies are essentially blocked from China, and vice versa, meaning they have not had to compete directly.

Uber abandoned its own efforts to develop self-driving technology in 2020, but it is working with several partners around the world who are in turn using different systems. That includes the Chinese company WeRide, which is operating driverless taxis in Abu Dhabi, UAE.

Wayve is also working with the Japanese manufacturer Nissan on integrating its tech in private cars.

Uber’s global head of autonomous mobility operations, Annie Duvnjak, said: “This licence is a key milestone in bringing autonomous rides to London on Uber.

“Our interest list has seen an incredible response from Londoners who are excited to experience Wayve’s British-built autonomous driving technology.”

The news came as Uber reported better than expected second-quarter gross bookings of $58.02bn (£43bn), but said earnings for the next quarter would fall below Wall Street forecasts.

Uber said earnings per share would come in between ​84 cents and 88 cents, compared with analysts’ expectations of 89 cents, with foreign exchange costs trimming booking growth.

The company also outlined ‌plans to spend more than $10bn on autonomous vehicles over the coming years, although it did not provide a specific ‌timeline.

title: GOP Rep Chuck Edwards drops re-election bid after House ethics report recommends censure
excerpt: Rep. Chuck Edwards, R-N.C., announces he and his wife, Teresa, have sold the McDonald's restaurant business they spent decades building, allowing him to dedicate more of his time to representing weste...
body_text:
Rep. Chuck Edwards, R-N.C., announces he and his wife, Teresa, have sold the McDonald's restaurant business they spent decades building, allowing him to dedicate more of his time to representing western North Carolina in Congress. (This video contains AI-assisted content.)

Rep. Chuck Edwards, R-N.C., announced early on Wednesday morning that he was dropping his re-election bid.

"After much prayer and reflection, I’ve decided to withdraw from my re-election campaign. I will complete my current term. Serving Western North Carolina has been the honor of my life. Thank you for your trust, prayers, and support. God bless WNC and America," Edwards noted in a post on X that was published at 3:32 a.m. ET.

The announcement came two days after the House Ethics Committee released a report recommending Edwards' censure.

GOP LAWMAKER'S GIFTS, 'EFFUSIVE AFFECTION' TOWARD YOUNG STAFFERS DETAILED IN EXPLOSIVE ETHICS REPORT

Rep. Chuck Edwards, R-N.C., departs from a House Republican Conference meeting in the U.S. Capitol on July 21, 2026, in Washington, D.C. (Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images)

Fox News Digital reached out to Edwards' congressional office and campaign on Wednesday morning.

Edwards has served in the U.S. House of Representatives since early 2023.

He decisively won the GOP primary in North Carolina's 11th Congressional District earlier this year.

'MCDONALD'S CHANGED THE COURSE OF MY LIFE': CONGRESSMAN SELLS BUSINESS HE BUILT SINCE HIS TEEN YEARS

The sun sets behind the U.S. Capitol on a hot and humid evening on Aug. 4, 2026 in Washington, D.C. (Kevin Carter/Getty Images)

But on Monday, the House Committee on Ethics issued a report finding Edwards "engaged in persistent unprofessional and inappropriate conduct towards two young female staffers."

While Edwards "denied that any of his conduct was intended as a sexual or romantic advance, his pattern of behavior would lead a reasonable observer to interpret it as such, including providing the young women with lavish and recurrent gifts, making comments regarding their appearance and dress, inviting them to intimate dinners and vacations, sending notes regarding his effusive affection, and inviting them to other activities as a way to spend time together," the report says.

The committee said it found "no evidence that Representative Edwards engaged in sexual activity with or explicitly propositioned any individual under his employ."

Edwards "was aware, however, that his excessive attention toward the young women had led to rumors and innuendo in the office," the report says. "Both women were uncomfortable with his behavior (which they attempted to communicate) but were put in an untenable position by virtue of his status as their boss and a Member of Congress. Representative Edwards was at minimum blind to that reality, and at worst, dismissive of the impact his inappropriate conduct had on the careers and wellbeing of two women on his staff."

REPUBLICAN LAWMAKER WELCOMES HOUSE ETHICS PROBE INTO SEXUAL MISCONDUCT ALLEGATIONS AGAINST HIM

Rep. Chuck Edwards, R-N.C., leaves the Capitol Hill Club after a meeting of the House Republican Conference on Tuesday, March 25, 2025. (Tom Williams/CQ-Roll Call, Inc via Getty Images)

"The Committee hereby adopts this Report in this matter and recommends Representative Edwards be censured for his conduct," the document noted.

Alex Nitzberg is a writer for Fox News Digital.

title: Trump's remarks on recruiting LeBron James to women's basketball resurface amid WNBA trans athlete debate
excerpt:
Donald Trump talks about recruiting LeBron James to his women's basketball team in July 2022 remarks. The comments resurfaced on social media in August 2026.

The WNBA is in the midst of a firestorm a...
body_text:
Donald Trump talks about recruiting LeBron James to his women's basketball team in July 2022 remarks. The comments resurfaced on social media in August 2026.

The WNBA is in the midst of a firestorm as sports fans have rallied around Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham and her stance that women and girls shouldn’t have to compete against males.

WNBA coaches, columnists and media pundits have continued to miss the mark on Cunningham’s comments and have said everything from sports should be inclusive to labelling Cunningham "anti-Black" and against transgender people.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

President Donald Trump's 2022 remarks about recruiting LeBron James to a women's basketball team went viral in August 2026. (Getty Images)

In the midst of the heated conversations on social media, President Donald Trump’s comments about being a WNBA coach resurfaced on Tuesday night. Trump was making a speech at the America First Policy Institute in July 2022 and said he would be the greatest women’s basketball coach ever because he’d ask LeBron James if he had any "desire to be a woman."

"I’ll tell you what – I’d be the greatest women’s basketball coach in history. Because, I don’t like LeBron James. I like Michael Jordan much better. But I’d go up to LeBron James, it doesn’t matter, I’d say, ‘LeBron, did you ever have any desire to be a woman? Because what I’d love you to do is star on my team that I’m building up. I’ll have the greatest team in history. They’ll never lose. Nobody will come within 70 points of this team,’ Trump said at the time. "No, we have to change that. We have to make it OK to talk about it."

The clip took new life ahead of the Fever’s game on Wednesday night against the New York Liberty. It will be the Fever’s second home game since her remarks were published in an ESPN feature.

NCAA SOFTBALL PLAYER REVEALS ALLEGED ENCOUNTER WITH PRO-TRANS COUNTERPROTESTERS AT SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM RALLY

Riley Gaines, Sophie Cunningham, and XX-XY Athletics founder Jen Sey pose courtside after an Indiana Fever game with a sign thanking Cunningham. (Riley Gaines/XX-XY Athletics)

Since then, women’s sports activists have rallied around Cunningham and have held events in support of her outside of arenas.

The latest was in Minneapolis ahead of the Fever’s 108-100 loss to the Minnesota Lynx. Pro-tans activists seemingly got wind of the rally and attempted to shout down at those in support of Cunningham.

One man waved a sign with a derogatory message toward those in support of Cunningham.

Still, Cunningham has not backed down from her comments.

"I said what I said. I think it’s kind of common sense," she said back on July 22. "I think I’ll always believe in that. I think it’s really important to protect children and that’s little girls who are also involved in that category. So, I stand on what I said and I’ll always believe that."

Ryan Gaydos is a senior editor for Fox News Digital.

title: Middle East crisis live: US and Iran signal hope for Hormuz deal but terms unclear
excerpt:
While Trump suggests deal could come as soon as today, Iran indicates that ongoing talks with Oman would not lead to its immediate reopening

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of the Middle East....
body_text:
While Trump suggests deal could come as soon as today, Iran indicates that ongoing talks with Oman would not lead to its immediate reopening

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of the Middle East.

US officials, including Donald Trump, have said a deal over the strait of Hormuz could be reached today, with continued diplomatic efforts potentially paving the way for US-Iran talks to resume.

“It could happen. Tomorrow or the next day,” the US president told reporters last night. “A lot of progress has been made.”

That optimism was shared by Iran, which said talks with Oman to reopen the critical shipping route were progressing “positively”.

It followed similar statements by the US’s secretary of state Marco Rubio and treasury secretary Scott Bessent, both of whom said progress had been made in those talks.

It remains to be seen what any agreement would include, as Iran has pushed for greater control of the strait of Hormuz, which carried about a fifth of the world’s oil and gas supply before the war, while the US has firmly rejected those demands. The strait has been effectively shut since 28 February, causing global energy prices to rocket.

A deal also does not guarantee that the strait of Hormuz would be reopened anytime soon, according to Iran’s state media. A central demand from Tehran has been the removal of the US naval blockade on Iranian ports, and it has threatened to keep the strait shut if “the United States continues to threaten Iran”. Both countries have accused each other of breaching the memorandum of understanding signed in June, which held for about a week before fresh hostilities erupted in the Gulf.

Citing an “informed source”, Iran’s state-run Islamic Republic of Iran Broadcasting (IRIB) reported:

double quotation markThe possible agreement between Iran and Oman on arrangements for vessels to pass through the strait of Hormuz has nothing to do with the immediate opening of the strait.
  Negotiations regarding arrangements for vessel traffic through the strait of Hormuz are purely Iranian-Omani and have no connection to the United States.

Brent crude is back above $80 a barrel, rising 1% to $80.2 a barrel.

The cost of filling up a tank of diesel has also reached £100 in the UK while petrol prices hit a new Iran war high – bad news for families heading on their summer getaways.

The average price of a litre of petrol in the UK rose to a new Iran war high of 161.5p on Wednesday, a jump of nearly 11p since its 6 July low, up 7%, the RAC motoring group reports.

Diesel has gone up even more, rising almost 17p a litre to 181.5p – a rise of 10% – since a conflict low point of 164.5p on 9 July.

One idea being floated is for Iran to control the route for ships entering the Gulf, while Oman would be responsible for the exit route. The Associated Press spoke to two regional officials familiar with the Iran-Oman talks who said service fees would be charged for keeping ships safe and protecting the waters.

Iran has repeatedly said the strait of Hormuz will not operate as it did before the war, as it seeks to secure a greater role in managing the critical shipping route. The Trump administration, however, has rejected any deal that would allow Iran such control.

“I’m not going to let them charge,” Donald Trump told reporters on Monday. “Anybody’s going to charge, we’ll charge.”

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of the Middle East.

US officials, including Donald Trump, have said a deal over the strait of Hormuz could be reached today, with continued diplomatic efforts potentially paving the way for US-Iran talks to resume.

“It could happen. Tomorrow or the next day,” the US president told reporters last night. “A lot of progress has been made.”

That optimism was shared by Iran, which said talks with Oman to reopen the critical shipping route were progressing “positively”.

It followed similar statements by the US’s secretary of state Marco Rubio and treasury secretary Scott Bessent, both of whom said progress had been made in those talks.

It remains to be seen what any agreement would include, as Iran has pushed for greater control of the strait of Hormuz, which carried about a fifth of the world’s oil and gas supply before the war, while the US has firmly rejected those demands. The strait has been effectively shut since 28 February, causing global energy prices to rocket.

A deal also does not guarantee that the strait of Hormuz would be reopened anytime soon, according to Iran’s state media. A central demand from Tehran has been the removal of the US naval blockade on Iranian ports, and it has threatened to keep the strait shut if “the United States continues to threaten Iran”. title: Republican Chuck Edwards drops bid for re-election after report finding sexual harassment of staffers
excerpt:

Chuck Edwards announced he would not run for re-election after the US House of Represen...
body_text:
Congressional ethics panel had recommended Edwards face censure over its findings on ‘hostile work environment’

Chuck Edwards announced he would not run for re-election after the US House of Representatives ethics committee determined the US congressman “fostered a hostile work environment and engaged in sexual harassment” by giving gifts and lavishing attention on two young female staffers.

Edwards, a Republican for North Carolina, said he would complete his current term, which is due to end in January.

In a statement posted on social media early on Wednesday morning, Edwards said: “After much prayer and reflection, I’ve decided to withdraw from my re-election campaign. I will complete my current term. Serving sestern North Carolina has been the honor of my life. Thank you for your trust, prayers, and support”

The bipartisan congressional ethics panel recommended on Monday that Edwards face censure over its findings. Should the House agree, he will have to stand in the well of the chamber while the text of a resolution rebuking him is read aloud.

The ethics committee launched an investigation into Edwards earlier this year, after receiving complaints about his conduct. In a report approved by Democratic and Republican committee members, it said there was “substantial reason to believe” that Edwards had broken House rules by singling out the two unidentified aides for special treatment that made them uncomfortable and harmed relations with other employees.

While the investigation uncovered no evidence that Edwards engaged in sexual activity with the staffers or suggested it, his behavior likely violated provisions in the House code of conduct that prohibit sexual harassment and unwanted advances.

The congressman “acknowledged at least some of the behavior at issue could be viewed as inappropriate”, but “has not acknowledged or taken responsibility for the harm he caused”, the committee wrote in its report.

Edwards was already viewed as vulnerable to losing re-election to his western North Carolina district in the November midterm elections. Last week election forecaster Sabato’s Crystal Ball announced it was rating his race a “toss-up”, in a sign of improving Democratic chances.

title: Waste workers help winner find binned €1m lottery ticket in Italy
excerpt:
A lottery player who accidentally binned a €1m (£857,158) winning-ticket may be the luckiest man in Italy after refuse workers found the missing slip.

The anonymous player disposed of the ticket in a...
body_text:
A lottery player who accidentally binned a €1m (£857,158) winning-ticket may be the luckiest man in Italy after refuse workers found the missing slip.

The anonymous player disposed of the ticket in a shop in Bitonto, southern Italy, after checking his numbers and being told it was "non-payable".

The man only realised he threw away a winning ticket after a relative pointed out the numbers he always played had been drawn.

It sparked a two-day search through a "mountain of waste" which had been collected by a bin lorry, the head of the refuse company, Roberto Nicola Toscano, told Italian news agency Ansa.

"This story is nothing short of miraculous," he added.

Recounting the story, he said the mix-up happened because the "non-payable" message appears when the prize is too high to be paid out by the shop.

When the player returned home, his family reportedly pointed out his favourite numbers - 2, 4, 8, 10, and 51 - had been drawn.

"It was then that he realised the misunderstanding. So they all went to the shop together and discovered that the tickets had been thrown away and collected by one our operators," said Toscano, director of SANB who handles waste collection in the area.

After the player made contact with the refuse company, the bin lorry was located before its contents were compacted for disposal.

"Luckily it was a Sunday, otherwise the load would have already ended up in landfill," the boss told Italian broadcaster TGCOM24.

The truck was then escorted to a special site where the search began to find the "small piece of paper hidden in a mountain of waste".

Finally after a two-day search, the winning ticket was reportedly found by a waste worker on Tuesday morning.

"It was in a hole-ridden bag along with other damaged tickets: this was one of the few intact ones," Toscano told Ansa.

The cost of the recovery operation is set to be charged to the winner, who had previously signed a declaration promising to cover the costs associated with the search.

The luck even rubbed off when Toscano and his colleagues bought a scratch card as a joke. They won €50 (£43).

title: Mexican influencer shot dead during livestream
excerpt:

Gast...
body_text:
The government has deployed extra security forces to Sinaloa state among a surge of violence (file photo)

A Mexican influencer, César Gastélum, has been shot dead while livestreaming on TikTok.

Gastélum was filming with two friends outside a fast food restaurant in Tres Ríos, in the northern city of Culiacán, on Tuesday evening when when two men on a motorbike drove up to him and one shot him at close range.

He had more than half a million followers on TikTok and mainly uploaded comedy videos.

It is not the first time a social media influencer has been killed in Mexico. Last year, 23-year-old Valeria Márquez was shot dead at a beauty salon while she was livestreaming on TikTok.

On the livestream, Gastélum and his friends were wearing bright orange coats and bags typically used by delivery drivers.

Local media reported that their outfits originally led police to believe that the victim was a delivery driver, but officials were later alerted to his identity.

Police and forensic experts cordoned off the area and are examining the cartridge casings and CCTV footage for any clues.

No arrests have so far been made and the two people on the motorbike fled the scene.

It is not yet clear whether Gastélum had received any threats.

On his Instagram account he often shared pictures of his travels and nights out, or posing in front of luxury cars.

In one of his posts, he could be seen at the grave of Leobardo Aispuro, an influencer known as "El Gordo Peruci".

Aispuro was shot dead in December 2024, in a killing which police said may have been linked to the rivalry between two warring factions of the Sinaloa cartel.

Violence in the state of Sinaloa, of which Culiacán is the capital, has spiralled since the two factions - Los Chapitos and La Mayiza - fell out in September 2024.

title: Andy Burnham reveals wife’s reaction to third Labour leadership bid
excerpt:
Burnham said his wife, Marie-France van Heel, took some persuading after he ran and lost in contests in 2010 and 2015

Andy Burnham has revealed his wife’s dismayed reaction when he told her he wanted...
body_text:
Burnham said his wife, Marie-France van Heel, took some persuading after he ran and lost in contests in 2010 and 2015

Andy Burnham has revealed his wife’s dismayed reaction when he told her he wanted to make another attempt at becoming Labour leader.

Burnham said that his wife, Marie-France van Heel, had been surprised by his decision to run, having lost contests in 2010 and 2015 to Ed Miliband and Jeremy Corbyn respectively.

“She was like, ‘not again, they’ve told you twice they don’t want you’,” Burnham told Elizabeth Day on the How to Fail podcast.

“She took some persuading to be honest, because I guess she didn’t want to see me go through it all again and then end up the wrong side at the end of it, but she gives me good advice,” he added.

Burnham recalled being an MP in his early 30s and thinking he had done well in interviews, only to find a text message from his wife that said, in capital letters, “ANSWER THE F***ING QUESTION”.

“That’s the kind of feedback I’ve had from her,” Burnham said. “She’s quite forthright, she’s Dutch and they don’t hold back, they’re pretty plain speaking and I’ve been on the receiving end of a lot of that over the years.”

Burnham said his failed leadership bids made him “a much better politician” in the end and that losing in 2015, standing to be the mayor of Greater Manchester and challenging himself “really strengthened” him.

Last week, Burnham promised to work collaboratively with other parties to find a lasting solution to social care. He told Day: “I feel that my generation of politicians is guilty of a shameful dereliction of duty, political cowardice of the worst kind in saying that this issue is too difficult and we’re not going to touch it.

“In fact, social care has gone backwards and doesn’t that just say something how politics has really fallen? It has to be radical, we’d have never created the NHS if we weren’t radical as a country at times.”

The prime minister said there was a need for radicalism in politics now “given where we are”, adding that neoliberalism and trickle down economics had not been kind to a lot of places across Britain, particularly former industrial hubs.

“Sometimes in politics you have to say, ‘I’m going to break out of the consensus and start talking about those things in a different way’, and it’s what I’ve started to do,” he added.

Board of Deputies of British Jews and the Jewish Leadership Council to meet with Tory party but decline meeting with Joshua Bonehill-Paine

Badenoch defends decision to allow man jailed for antisemitism to stand as councillor

The Board of Deputies of British Jews and the Jewish Leadership Council have said they will meet the Conservative Party to discuss the selection of a former neo-Nazi as a council candidate, but declined to meet Joshua Bonehill-Paine himself.

In a joint statement, the two groups said:

double quotation markThe Board of Deputies of British Jews and the Jewish Leadership Council have declined the Conservative party’s invitation to meet with a former neo-Nazi with criminal convictions for antisemitic hatred.

The severity of Joshua Bonehill-Paine’s crimes targeting Luciana Berger and others mean that he still faces ongoing legal restrictions.

Whilst we do believe in the possibility of rehabilitation, this should not in this case entail selection as a candidate for a major political party, and the impact of this decision on the victims ought to be a central consideration.

We have agreed to meet the Conservative party to discuss their decision-making processes and to urge them to rescind this decision.

Bonehill-Paine was jailed in 2016 after he was convicted of racially aggravated harassment of Labour peer Luciana Berger, who is Jewish.

He was previously jailed for producing an advert for a neo-Nazi rally illustrated with a picture of Nazi concentration camp Auschwitz which promised “an absolute gas”.

He has since apologised for his past offending, and said he has now dedicated himself to “challenging the wave of hatred British Jews continue to face”.

Women should not feel pressurised into experiencing an “ideal birth”, the new health secretary, Yvette Cooper, has said, promising a root-and-branch reform of standards after several damning maternity scandals.

Cooper, who returns to the department 27 years after she was the minister for public health under Tony Blair, said maternity and child health would be a major focus in the role, where she will also be expected to implement significant reforms to social care.

In an interview with the Guardian, she said the culture change should address any pressure on women to have a particular kind of birth experience, after families have repeatedly raised the alarm about an unwillingness by some maternity units to escalate interventions because of a desire for more natural births.

“I would worry about any mum feeling pressurised that there is somehow a kind of an ideal birth experience to live up to when it’s always different in every case, and you have to follow the evidence, you have to have informed choice,” she said.

In one of her first acts as health secretary, Cooper said she intended to re-introduce binding national maternity standards, which were dismantled under the early Conservative NHS reforms and replaced with fragmented trust-by-trust practices.
