Jesse Watson is a Fox News Digital production assistant.

title: Socialist House candidate says he agrees with Republicans on 'one issue'
excerpt: Rep. Josh Gottheimer, D-N.J., warns of a growing far-left socialist influence within the Democratic Party. He addresses the rising prominence of the Democratic Socialists of America in key primaries a...
body_text:
Rep. Josh Gottheimer, D-N.J., warns of a growing far-left socialist influence within the Democratic Party. He addresses the rising prominence of the Democratic Socialists of America in key primaries and its potential impact on future elections.

A socialist candidate vying to unseat a sitting House Democrat says there is "one issue" he agrees with Republicans on.

Michigan state lawmaker Donavan McKinney is among the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) members giving establishment Democrats a run for their money across the country ahead of the 2026 midterm elections in November.

Members of the group have shown that they're a potent force among the left's base voters, while also working to appeal to the same working-class, anti-establishment sentiment that helped President Donald Trump get elected in 2016.

DSA MEMBER LEADS DEM PRIMARY IN MIDWEST BATTLEGROUND BUT TRAILS LIKELY GOP NOMINEE: POLL

Michigan state Rep. Donavan McKinney rallied over the weekend in his bid to unseat Rep. Shri Thanedar, D-Mich., on Aug. 2, 2026. (Paul Steinhauser/Fox News Digital)

The latest evidence of that is McKinney's tease in a recent interview with Zeteo News, "I gotta give Republicans — I agree with them on this one issue. The one issue is waste, fraud, and abuse."

But he differed with the GOP on where that's coming from.

"Republicans' analysis is there's waste, fraud, and abuse when it comes to the poor. It's kind of like, you know, voting fraud. There's like .0001%, like very small percentage of folks, poor people, take advantage of the system," McKinney said. "The waste, fraud, and abuse is coming from our taxpayer dollars subsidizing our corporations and the wealthy, so they can get richer and we keep being poor."

SOCIALIST-BACKED MICHIGAN SENATE HOPEFUL CALLS AMERICAN POLITICS A 'DISEASE' AFTER PROFESSING LOVE FOR US

Rep. Shri Thanedar arrives for the vote on the budget resolution at the U.S. Capitol on April 10, 2025. (Bill Clark/CQ-Roll Call, Inc. via Getty Images)

"We're gonna attack the waste, fraud, and abuse, but we're going to attack it for the top 1% earners in this country," he added of his goals if elected to the House.

McKinney is running to unseat Rep. Shri Thanedar, D-Mich., a progressive who split with the DSA over the party's anti-Israel sentiment.

And during a rally over the weekend, McKinney attempted to appeal to voters who feel the strain of high costs in their everyday lives.

HOUSE REPUBLICANS AIM TO TURN DEMOCRATIC CIVIL WAR INTO MIDTERM WEAPON

"All I hear across our communities is that I don't have enough resources to survive. I would define politics, it's pretty simple, it's the redistribution of resources. Well, we have to take our taxpayer money to send it overseas for bombs and weapons, to kill families and children. No more to support genocide. I think that's a damn shame," he said.

"We're in Iran spending billions of dollars a day on average. And you're telling me the people in my district, the seniors, our children, our most vulnerable populations can't get the resources they deserve? I don't think this is America anyone wants us to live in, am I right?"

He also criticized "self-interested" lawmakers in both parties for falling out of touch with what Americans across the country are struggling with.

Items on a table during an election night party held by the Democratic Socialists of America - LA chapter at The Greyhound on Nov. 4, 2025 in Los Angeles. (Eric Thayer/Los Angeles Times via Getty Images)

But on the other side of the aisle, the growing insurgency from the socialist left could provide a boon to Republicans who are fighting an uphill battle to keep control of the House.

GOP leaders across the country are warning that Americans are not interested in socialism or its core beliefs, like the redistribution of wealth and demise of capitalism.

Meanwhile, DSA-linked candidates have already unseated incumbent House Democrats in New York and Colorado.

Elizabeth Elkind is a politics reporter for Fox News Digital leading coverage of the House of Representatives. Previous digital bylines seen at Daily Mail and CBS News.

Follow on Twitter at @liz_elkind and send tips to elizabeth.elkind@fox.com

title: Buffalo music venue bans DJ after 'We Are Charlie Kirk' song played in jest
excerpt: During the Charlie Kirk murder preliminary hearing, etched bullets bearing messages like 'Hey Fascist' and 'Catch' are shown as key evidence. Legal expert Joshua Ritter discusses the intent behind the...
body_text:
During the Charlie Kirk murder preliminary hearing, etched bullets bearing messages like 'Hey Fascist' and 'Catch' are shown as key evidence. Legal expert Joshua Ritter discusses the intent behind these etchings, considering if they were a joke or a serious threat. A witness, Lance Twiggs, details Tyler Robinson's request for a Dremel tool to create these messages.

A Buffalo music venue says it has barred a DJ from performing again after it said a "We Are Charlie Kirk" meme was shown during a recent performance that sparked backlash online, prompting the club to issue a public apology.

In a Facebook statement posted Sunday, live music bar Nietzsche's said it only learned about the incident after it circulated on social media. While the venue said the artist and promoter described the incident as a joke, it apologized to patrons, said the content did not reflect its values, and announced the DJ responsible would not be invited back.

"We want to apologize for a moment that occurred during a show at Nietzsche's last weekend, involving a ‘We are Charlie Kirk’ meme that we just became aware of via social media," the venue said in a post on Facebook. "After speaking with the artist and promoter, we understand it was intended in jest, but it's not something that has any place at Nietzsche's."

BOB IGER BREAKS SILENCE ON DISNEY'S SUSPENSION OF JIMMY KIMMEL OVER CHARLIE KIRK ASSASSINATION COMMENTS

Charlie Kirk was a conservative activist who led Turning Point USA. (Alex Brandon/The Associated Press)

The bar and lounge continued, "We want to reaffirm that Nietzsche's is, has been, and always will be a place of acceptance, respect, and community. We recognize that this moment did not reflect those values, and we sincerely apologize to anyone who was made to feel unwelcome or hurt."

"The DJ who included this content will not be performing at the club again," Nietzsche's added. "We appreciate everyone who brought this to our attention and will continue working to ensure Nietzsche's remains a welcoming space for all."

RHODE ISLAND TEACHER WHO CALLED SLAIN CHARLIE KIRK 'GARBAGE' HONORED IN HIGH SCHOOL YEARBOOK

Turning Point USA founder Charlie Kirk spoke during his "American Comeback Tour" at Utah Valley University on Sept. 10, 2025, in Orem, Utah. Kirk was fatally shot while appearing at the event. (Trent Nelson/The Salt Lake Tribune/Getty Images)

Kirk, the 31-year-old founder of the conservative organization Turning Point USA, was assassinated Sept. 10 while speaking at Utah Valley University during his American Comeback Tour.

Shortly after Kirk’s assassination, a song thought to be AI-generated called "We Are Charlie Kirk" was credited to Spalexma that was released on Sept. 18, 2025. It is in the style of a Christian power ballad, with lyrics like, "He spoke the truth when the cost was high / He lived for Jesus, unafraid to die."

TikTokers and others have used the song in videos to mock Kirk and his death since last year.

TEXAS MAN ALLEGEDLY THREATENED TO BOMB TURNING POINT USA EVENT AND KILL CEO ERIKA KIRK IN ONLINE POSTS

Matthew Robinson (left) has continued running his masonry business as his son, Tyler Robinson (right), faces prosecution in the assassination of Charlie Kirk. (Alec Thornock for Fox News Digital and Rick Egan/The Salt Lake Tribune via Pool)

Fox News Digital reached out to Nietzsche's and Turning Point USA for comment but did not immediately receive a response.

Rachel del Guidice is a culture reporter for Fox News covering the intersection of politics, faith, family, and American culture.

title: College football is finally back after months of NCAA lawsuits, NIL drama and congressional fights
excerpt:
Trey Wallace tells Dan Dakich what the most interesting elements are that could be included in a new college sports bill.

Lost in the kerfuffles over court cases involving the NCAA and the 'Protect C...
body_text:
Trey Wallace tells Dan Dakich what the most interesting elements are that could be included in a new college sports bill.

Lost in the kerfuffles over court cases involving the NCAA and the 'Protect College Sports Act' heading to the Senate floor this that week for a vote is the fact that we will play college football this month after another wild offseason of drama.

As football teams hit the practice field this week for the start of fall camp, the anticipation builds for what is to come in just 25 days after a majority of the headlines over the past seven months have centered around the future.

NCAA ROCKED BY COLORADO JUDGE'S 2022 CLASS ELIGIBILITY RULING THAT COULD RESHAPE COLLEGE SPORTS THIS YEAR

The expansion of the College Football Playoff. Congressional leaders trying to garner enough from SEC and Big Ten leaders to pass legislation that will have major ramifications on the future of college athletics. Court cases involving athletes who feel they were wronged by the NCAA installing a new 5-for-5 eligibility rule that gives athletes five years to play five seasons in all sports.

Bundle all of this together and we once again had an offseason that did not center around what was going to take place on the football field this year.

Indiana head coach Curt Cignetti watches during warm ups before the College Football Playoff national championship game between Miami and Indiana, Monday, Jan. 19, 2026, in Miami Gardens, Florida. (AP Photo/Rebecca Blackwell)

I am not implying that what is taking place off the field is not important, far from it. The NCAA put itself in this spot, and it's having to spend an insane amount of money to defend their decisions in courtrooms across the country.

What I am saying is that the average fan who just wants to cheer on their team, or call into their local postgame show to unload on whomever is coaching their favorite squad after a loss, is tired of hearing about the everyday noise that has overtaken the offseason.

And guess what? I don't blame them one bit. In reality, I agree with them.

We spent college football media days clamoring over the future of college athletics and how much money it's going to take in hopes of competing for a national championship. At the end of the day, fans that pay for tickets, parking, memorabilia, food, hotels and gas just want to sit in their seats to cheer on their team.

THREE INTRIGUING QUARTERBACK BATTLES TO WATCH DURING COLLEGE FOOTBALL OFFSEASON CAMPS

Whether that's inside the stadium or sitting on the couch with their friends, the conversation around what college sports will look like in two or three years has gotten old, quick.

Since the inception of NIL, which was highlighted by Nick Saban and Jimbo Fisher trading jabs about how much money was spent on the Texas A&M roster, the offseason talk has shifted from the on-field product to which lawyer is representing a player in their fight against the NCAA.

Again, that is just the world we live in now. It's not going away any time soon, no matter if Congress passes the 'Protect College Sports Act' or not.

All across the country, players and coaches are preparing for the upcoming season. At the same time, fans are booking hotel rooms or deciding how much money they will need to spend on streaming platforms so they can enjoy a season of college football.

Lawmakers praise bipartisan efforts led by Trump admin to ‘protect college sports for future generations’

We had plenty of drama though, thanks to figures like Brendan Sorsby, Lane Kiffin, the entire Texas Tech athletic department, Ole Miss and even Bill Belichick.

In Austin, there are Texas fans wondering if this is the year in which Steve Sarkisian can get the Longhorns playing for a national championship.

Out in Southern California, USC fans are already preparing to hold a picket line if Lincoln Riley cannot get the Trojans back into the CFP conversation.

Texas Longhorns quarterback Arch Manning warms up before a game against the Texas A&M Aggies at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium in Austin, Texas. (Scott Wachter/Imagn Images)

The list goes on, and on. And, I love it. The local radio stations are getting everything together from a technical standpoint to host postgame shows that are like therapy sessions for fans.

We have also spent this offseason clamoring over who's the best conference in college football.

Is it the Big Ten or SEC? Well, who has won the past three national championships? Curt Cignetti rightfully stood at the podium last week in Chicago and made that point abundantly clear.

Will the ACC make another run at a College Football Playoff title game appearance, and can that team once again be Miami? Is this the final season in which Dabo Swinney will lead Clemson down the hill? How many vacancies will the ACC have after this season comes to an end?

There is a lot of pressure on schools to deliver, and if you aren’t in the CFP conversation when the first weekend of November rolls around, then fans will be prepared to start conversing about how much money was spent on a roster that came up short.

We have entered the most nerve-wracking point of the year in college football. The 'expectation' period, where everyone still has a chance.

This is what we crave. This is what we find ourselves stressing over when life might be kicking us outside the sports realm.

Head Coach Lane Kiffin of the LSU Tigers speaks at SEC Football Kickoff Media Day at Tampa Marriott Water Street in Tampa, Fla., on July 23, 2026. (Getty Images)

And sure, there will be plenty of noise around legislation and court cases that are currently ongoing off the field.

Unfortunately, that's the world we live in right now when it comes to college athletics. But, the beautiful sight of your favorite team running out of the locker room is nearly upon us.

Congratulations to you all. We've made it to another season of college football.

Trey Wallace is the Sr. College Sports Reporter for OutKick.

title: US cyclosporiasis outbreak kills two people in Michigan, officials say
excerpt:
US sees first fatalities due to intestinal illness, though both had significant ​underlying health conditions

Two people have died from cyclosporiasis in Michigan, the state’s health department said ...
body_text:
US sees first fatalities due to intestinal illness, though both had significant ​underlying health conditions

Two people have died from cyclosporiasis in Michigan, the state’s health department said on Monday, marking the first fatalities in the largest US outbreak ⁠of the intestinal illness.

Both ⁠individuals had significant ​underlying health conditions that may have been affected by cyclosporiasis and dehydration, according to medical records.

There are no updates on the investigation, the state ⁠health department told Reuters in an email.

An FDA investigation linked the outbreak that has expanded to nine states to iceberg lettuce sourced from privately held Taylor Farms ⁠operations in central Mexico, but authorities are still looking for other potential sources.

Cyclosporiasis is generally not a ​life-threatening illness.

Michigan health officials reported 11,234 outbreak-linked cases ‌on Monday, up 461 ‌from Friday’s update. The outbreak has resulted in 193 hospitalizations, according to the health department’s latest data.

Wayne ‌county has reported the highest number of cases, with 1,379 infections. Adults aged 30 to 39 years have been the hardest hit, accounting for 2,216 reported cases, state data showed.

Cases of the intestinal illness caused by the Cyclospora parasite have been rising steadily across the United States in recent weeks, according to the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). Symptoms include severe diarrhea, nausea ‌and other gastrointestinal issues.

Nationwide, the CDC has recorded 6,707 laboratory-confirmed cases of cyclosporiasis as of 28 July, with more than 11,500 additional suspected cases still awaiting confirmation ​or further investigation.

The CDC surveillance updates include only laboratory-confirmed cases, while state health departments may also report probable infections, resulting in higher case counts. The agency has said it is working with states to update the national tally as additional cases are confirmed.

Former CDC officials and food safety experts have said cuts across federal ⁠health agencies have complicated the government’s ability to respond to foodborne disease outbreaks.

The ​US Department of Health and ​Human Services said it was aware of ​the deaths in Michigan.

“This development highlights the importance of identifying the source of ​the outbreak and ‌preventing additional illnesses,” said Wade ​Syers, food safety ​specialist at Michigan State University Extension.

Consumers in the US have been steering clear of some restaurant chains and buying less lettuce in grocery stores as the multi-state outbreak of the parasitic disease has fueled confusion over what is safe to eat.

title: Scottish seabird hunt cancelled for first time in 400 years
excerpt:
NatureScot refuses licence for hunt on Hebridean island of Sula Sgeir in which up to 2,000 gannet chicks are killed

A controversial Scottish seabird hunt will not go ahead for the first time in 400 y...
body_text:
NatureScot refuses licence for hunt on Hebridean island of Sula Sgeir in which up to 2,000 gannet chicks are killed

A controversial Scottish seabird hunt will not go ahead for the first time in 400 years, in what campaigners have called a “victory for common sense”.

In the annual guga hunt, up to 2,000 gannet chicks are killed over a 10-day period on the uninhabited Hebridean island of Sula Sgeir, 40 miles north of Lewis and Harris.

NatureScot, which is responsible for licensing, refused to allow this year’s hunt to go ahead, citing a potential “adverse impact” on gannet populations according to new modelling.

Wildlife and animal rights organisations have long protested against the killing of the birds, which is part of a tradition some say goes back to the Vikings, when they were hunted for food.

The hunters, known as the Men of Ness, take the chicks from their nests in the nature reserve of Sula Sgeir with a noose on a long pole and kill them with a blow to the head.

The birds are then gutted and salted on the island and eaten as a delicacy in the Western Isles – though the taste has been described as “absolutely revolting”, “between rotten leather and fishy beef” and “without doubt the most disgusting thing”.

In a statement, NatureScot said: “After assessing the application against the legislation and using the most recent scientific evidence, our board’s decision is to refuse a licence.

“We have used the latest information available and commissioned an updated population model to help predict the effect of the guga hunt on the gannet population. As a result, we have concluded an adverse impact is possible, both at the applicants’ requested application limit of 2,000 juvenile gannets, and at a reduced limit of 500.”

However, the organisation, which is part of the Scottish government, criticised some of the anti-hunt activists, saying the police had been called over the “aggression and intimidation tactics of some anti-guga hunt protesters [which] comes at significant personal cost to our expert and dedicated staff, as they try to do their day-to-day jobs”.

Two men dressed in gannet costumes were arrested and charged in March after spending several days on the roof of Great Glen House, NatureScot’s Inverness headquarters. In separate incidents, the building was also subject to graffiti and had windows smashed.

In May, a candidate stood for the Holyrood seat of Edinburgh Central in protest against the hunt.

People from Ness, in the north of Lewis, accused the activists of a campaign of bullying.

Ahead of NatureScot’s board meeting, Murdo MacRitchie, of the Save Our Guga Harvest group, said: “People in Ness will understandably feel that this recommendation risks rewarding a campaign in which members of a small island community have been bullied and abused and publicly owned property has been vandalised.”

A petition to the Scottish government to end the practice attracted more than 100,000 signatures, while a separate petition from the anti-hunting charity Protect the Wild surpassed 250,000.

Devon Docherty, Scottish campaigns manager at Protect the Wild, said the decision was a “victory for compassion, for science and for common sense”.

She added: “Thousands of young seabirds have been spared from a brutal death because NatureScot chose to follow the evidence rather than simply rubber-stamp another licence to kill.”

The decision does not prevent the Men of Ness from getting a licence in future years for the hunt, which is recognised in law under the Wildlife and Countryside Act.

title: Virgin Mary statue becomes beacon of hope after California wildfires, Fox Nation explores
excerpt:
‘Unexplained Mysteries of Faith,’ a new program hosted by Abby Hornacek streams Aug. 3 exclusively on Fox Nation.

The devastating 2025 Los Angeles wildfires reduced thousands of homes to rubble. But ...
body_text:
‘Unexplained Mysteries of Faith,’ a new program hosted by Abby Hornacek streams Aug. 3 exclusively on Fox Nation.

The devastating 2025 Los Angeles wildfires reduced thousands of homes to rubble. But the survival of one family's Virgin Mary statue became a viral sensation, symbolizing the resilience of a community engulfed in flames.

Host Abby Hornacek uncovers the Halpin family's remarkable story in the brand-new, three-part Fox Nation series, 'Unexplained Mysteries of Faith.' In the final episode of the show, she visits Altadena to speak with Peter Halpin and his wife, Jackie, who recount the story of how their Virgin Mary statue survived destruction — and the viral hymn they sang around it.

"It was totally unintended," Halpin said. "As a matter of fact, we all just stood around. We said a family prayer that we say together, and then we decided to sing that song."

WORLD-FAMOUS CATHOLIC SHRINE TORCHED, 'DEVIL IN A SKIRT' SCRAWLED ON VIRGIN MARY STATUE

A statue of The Virgin Mary remained amid ash and rubble after wildfires destroyed a Southern California family's home of 37 years. (Jackie Halpin)

The Halpins reflected on how the comfort of their singing helped them through the initial shock of losing their house, and remarked that the statue's survival also impacted others.

"Being in that kind of state where you just lost your home and [are] in shock," he continued. "I think it gave a lot of people hope, because we believe in God, we are a prayerful family, and we just felt like it was something we should do."

During a January 2026 interview with Angelus News, Jackie echoed a similar sentiment, explaining how she couldn't recover from the emotional toll the wildfires caused without her faith.

"I could not have done it without my faith," she said. "You can be really sad and still be grateful. You can be in pain and believe in redemptive suffering, and that has really sustained me this year. Offering all my sufferings back to Jesus — you just cling to the cross, and I just offer all my sufferings for my children and their needs."

WILLIE ROBERTSON'S FAITH-BASED ADVICE THAT'S KEPT HIS 34-YEAR MARRIAGE TO WIFE KORIE STRONG

A house burns as the Palisades Fire rages on at the Mandeville Canyon, in Los Angeles, California, on January 11, 2025. (Shannon Stapleton/Reuters)

Throughout "Unexplained Mysteries of Faith," Hornacek dives deep into sacred places, odd occurrences and personal stories that some say are shaped by miracles.

In episode one, she travels to Loretto Chapel in New Mexico, which features a mysterious spiral staircase with no visible support, nails or a central column.

Hornacek examines the bizarre disappearance of the carpenter who built it and how the unexplainable led to some citing faith as the reason behind its existence.

During episode two, she investigates the stunning story behind St. Frances Cabrini, the Italian-born nun who became America's first saint. Despite her chronic illnesses, she set sail to New York City to help Italian immigrants facing discrimination and opened 67 educational centers, orphanages and other public institutions during her lifetime.

Her extraordinary strength is cited by her strongest believers as faith in action, with her legacy continuing across generations.

NEW FOX NATION SHOW BLOWS OPEN THE WILD SECRETS INSIDE THE ‘IMPOSSIBLE’ WHITE HOUSE UFC FIGHT

Abby Hornacek hosts the new Fox Nation series, "Unexplained Mysteries of Faith," streaming August 3. (Fox Nation)

Hornacek previously hosted several Fox Nation productions, including 'PARK'D,' in which she explores America's majestic national parks, partnering with local guides and regional experts to showcase the country's incredible beauty.

To uncover more about these fascinating stories of how faith shaped the understanding of inspiring American events, tune in to "Unexplained Mysteries of Faith," now streaming exclusively on Fox Nation.

Fox Nation programs are viewable on demand and from your mobile device app but only for FOX Nation subscribers. Go to Fox Nation to start a free trial and watch the extensive library from your favorite FOX Nation personalities.

Benji Ferraro is a recent University of Maryland grad and new digital production assistant, with a focus on channel coverage and culture stories. He can be reached at benji.ferraro@fox.com for any story tips.

title: Uncertainty on Iranians’ minds as Trump fluctuates on war and talk
excerpt:
Trump pauses ‘massive attack’ on Iran, says new talks to begin

Tehran, Iran – For months now, US President Donald Trump has been making nearly daily proclamations about the war on Iran – from threats...
body_text:
Trump pauses ‘massive attack’ on Iran, says new talks to begin

Tehran, Iran – For months now, US President Donald Trump has been making nearly daily proclamations about the war on Iran – from threats of extensive bombing to claims of renewed negotiations. But Faezeh, a financial firm employee in Iran’s capital, says she has long stopped paying attention.

“His words certainly impact our lives, but I try to escape this toxic environment of uncertainty by focusing on what I can control and protecting myself and my loved ones,” the 27-year-old told Al Jazeera.

As the war approaches its six-month mark, a number of Iranians are opting against chasing the non-stop headlines in an effort to protect their mental health. This week, as the threat of large-scale US military action once again loomed large, the level of expectation and concern among Iranians appeared to be much lower than on April 7, when the US president warned that “a whole civilisation will die tonight”, only to announce a ceasefire shortly afterwards.

“The US used to have presidents who talked less and did more,” asserted Roham, a colleague of Faezeh at the financial company in central Tehran. “But now with the role of social media and other outlets in which Mr Trump is well-versed, he talks more and doesn’t have to do as much,” he told Al Jazeera.

For Roham, what is ultimately missing is not solid decision-making by Trump, but a desire by Iranian authorities to create more space and allow more voices to be heard inside the country. He said he sees no chance of that becoming possible at the moment.

“So we’re up in the air and lack of certainty in our lives has reached a peak,” he added.

Calling Trump’s pronouncements a “repetitive loop” aimed at impacting global markets, Faezeh said any person who makes so many contradictory remarks at such a high pace cannot be considered valid in her eyes.

Looking ahead, she expects economic situations to get considerably worse, including a further depreciation of Iran’s national currency.

Iran’s rial changed hands for about 1.91 million against the US dollar in Tehran’s open market on Monday, hovering near an all-time low. The currency had strengthened to about 1.54 million per greenback in mid-June, in reaction to a now-suspended deal between Iran and the US that was facilitated by regional mediators.

Trump boasted on social media about tanking the rial this week, using a diagram that said he was “destroying Iran’s currency”. It also said there was “massive inflation” in Iran. The Statistical Center of Iran put the inflation rate for the calendar month that ended on July 22 at nearly 90 percent compared to the same month a year earlier.

Ali, a product manager at a technology company in the capital, said the US president mostly cares about stock markets and oil prices, so he also looks at those indicators too when trying to decipher the meaning behind Trump’s statements.

“My view is that Trump won’t undertake any serious action in terms of hitting energy infrastructure or launching a ground attack against Iran at least until the Congress elections,” he said, in reference to November’s polls in the US. “He will keep playing this game and go back and forth”.

Ali said he believes Trump would prefer an agreement that would allow him to declare victory, but that the spectre of war was expected to hang over the country in the coming months.

Following reported threats of a “massive attack” on Iran, Trump on Sunday said talks facilitated by mediators would take place with representatives from Tehran on Monday, while Iran’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs said negotiations over the Strait of Hormuz were in the final stages with Oman, not with the US.

The latest on-again, off-again comments on war and negotiations by the US president also found their way onto state television in Iran.

A hardline war-focused programme asked Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei on Sunday night whether the Trump administration’s claim was true that Tehran had directly or indirectly asked Washington not to attack energy infrastructure and instead focus on negotiations.

“I am sometimes surprised why you put so much stock in comments by US officials that have time and time again proven baseless,” Baghaei said, adding that the Islamic Republic would not back down from its “principled positions”.

Those positions include maintaining a level of control in the Strait of Hormuz, which Iran says will not go back to its pre-war status, as well as resistance towards giving major concessions on the country’s nuclear programme and the “axis of resistance” of armed forces across the region. For any long-term deal, Tehran has also requested an effective lifting of harsh US sanctions that have hit Iran’s economy hard over the past decade.

State TV has urged people to remain prepared for a potentially resumed war, as hardliners refute any negotiated solution with Washington.

Earlier this week, a state TV analyst said the US is likely to attempt a combination of moves to topple the Islamic Republic if the war resumes at scale, including assassinations, infrastructure attacks, propagating internal unrest, border clashes and a ground offensive in southern Iran.

On Monday, Iran’s President, Masoud Pezeshkian, renewed his support for a deal, saying he believes that the memorandum of understanding signed with the US in June will act as “the centre of gravity of our foreign relations in the future”.

“We must strive to compel the enemy to remain committed to what it has signed. The security of the country, the region and our allies will be enhanced by this memorandum,” he posted on social media.

Hours later, it was time for Trump to issue another declaration.

“Nothing gets through to Iran, unless we want it to, and nothing will get through, unless a Deal, or Total Surrender, is accomplished,” he wrote on his Truth Social platform, referring to the US blockade on Iran’s southern ports.

“Whether Iran wants to admit it or not, we are, in fact, talking of a solution to a problem that they have caused, for decades.”

title: Dodgers send Wrobleski against Cubs' Boyd as both teams add arms before the trade deadline
excerpt:
Dan Dakich, Jason Hammer & Dan Zaksheske discuss the upcoming issues that the MLB is facing in their next offseason

The trade deadline is here. I am sure that excites a lot of people, including mysel...
body_text:
Dan Dakich, Jason Hammer & Dan Zaksheske discuss the upcoming issues that the MLB is facing in their next offseason

The trade deadline is here. I am sure that excites a lot of people, including myself. We’ve already seen at least one massive trade, and we’ve seen a few others that have been interesting. There are definitely teams, like the White Sox, who are making a true push for the postseason with their moves. We knew the two teams in today’s game were going to be elite anyway, but both have made a move, and it will be interesting to see what else they do before the first pitch in this one.

The Los Angeles Dodgers made the move to get Tarik Skubal. Not only was he the best pitcher on the market, but he is the best pitcher potentially on the planet. Now a team that has won the past two World Series is more than primed for the third, and they will be getting to show him what it is like to be a Dodger before he hits free agency. Good for them. To be clear, the Dodgers are not bad for baseball. Cheap owners are bad for baseball. The Detroit Tigers organization is owned by people who have multiple billions of dollars in the bank, so they can’t cry poor.

Tarik Skubal #29 of the Detroit Tigers looks on during the game between the Baltimore Orioles and the Detroit Tigers at Comerica Park on Wednesday, July 29, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Izzy Rincon/MLB Photos via Getty Images) (Izzy Rincon/MLB Photos via Getty Images)

Skubal won’t be starting today; that will come tomorrow. Instead, the team turns to Justin Wrobleski, who has been great this season with a 11-2 record, 2.88 ERA, and a 1.02 WHIP. These aren’t numbers he’s put up in a short period of time, either. He has tossed 112.2 innings this season. He did struggle in his most recent outing, going six innings and allowing five earned runs. Four of those came via the long ball, which really hasn’t been an issue for him this season. He faced the Cubs earlier this year, going six scoreless innings and allowing just four hits.

DODGERS REPORTEDLY ACQUIRE ACE TARIK SKUBAL FROM TIGERS IN TRADE THAT STIRS UP MLB WORLD

The Chicago Cubs are a Wild Card team, and that’s likely the best way to describe them overall. We know they are decent – their offense is among the best in the league. However, the team has been decimated by injuries. They had a thin pitching staff coming into the season and despite that being glaringly obvious to even casual followers, they didn’t do much to address it. The good news for Cubs fans is that they’ve fixed that issue a bit with some recent moves. They added Aaron Civale, and yesterday got a former Cy Young winner, Kevin Gausman.

Kevin Gausman pitches for the Toronto Blue Jays during the first inning against the Los Angeles Dodgers at Rogers Centre in Toronto, Ont., on April 7, 2026. (Cole Burston/Getty Images)

He also won’t be making the start today, but it is a good addition to a team that is slowly getting some of their arms back. Matthew Boyd has returned to the rotation and has been a breath of fresh air for the Cubs. Since coming back, Boyd has gone 44 innings and allowed just nine earned runs. We got a really nice outing from him last start when he allowed no runs over seven innings and scattered just four hits. Dodgers hitters are batting just .200 against him in 100 at-bats.

Nico Hoerner of the Chicago Cubs makes a play at second base during a game against the Houston Astros at Wrigley Field in Chicago, Ill., on May 22, 2026. (Matt Dirksen/Chicago Cubs/Getty Images)

This should be a really competitive game, and I think both pitchers are going to see that the opposition gets few opportunities. I think that the better option to take is the Cubs, but I’m not messing with the moneyline. I’m going to back the under 8.5 in this game. I just don’t see either starter giving up a ton of runs.

title: Fired ‘60 Minutes’ correspondents Sharyn Alfonsi and Scott Pelley wash up at Columbia Journalism School
excerpt:
CBS News fired longtime "60 Minutes" correspondent Scott Pelley after his meltdown at a meeting over the new leadership at the company.

Recently fired "60 Minutes" correspondents Sharyn Alfonsi and S...
body_text:
CBS News fired longtime "60 Minutes" correspondent Scott Pelley after his meltdown at a meeting over the new leadership at the company.

Recently fired "60 Minutes" correspondents Sharyn Alfonsi and Scott Pelley have found a safe space, landing at Columbia Journalism School (CJS) for the 2026–27 academic year.

Alfonsi and Pelley, who were shown the door from "60 Minutes" after clashing with CBS News editor-in-chief Bari Weiss and objecting to attempts to tamp down the partisanship at the iconic newsmagazine, will serve at the historically liberal-yet-celebrated home to the Pulitzer Prize as journalists-in-residence, the school announced Monday.

Alfonsi and Pelley will "work closely with students, individually and as a group, through lectures, workshops and special events designed to sharpen their reporting, investigative and sourcing skills," according to CJS. They will also contribute to the Columbia Journalism Review.

SCOTT PELLEY FIRED AT CBS NEWS AFTER BLOWUPS WITH BARI WEISS, NEW '60 MINUTES' PRODUCER

Sharyn Alfonsi and Scott Pelley joined Columbia Journalism School (CJS) for the 2026–27 academic year. (Marla Aufmuth/Getty Images for Texas Conference for Women; Michele Crowe/CBS News via Getty Images)

"This is a critical time for a free press," Pelley said in a statement. "Columbia is leading the way in training the next generation of great journalists, and I am honored to join Sharyn in that vital cause."

The Media Research Center believes "Columbia’s journalism program is not committed to honest journalism" and instead "delivers a one-sided education that celebrates left-wing policies and is overwhelmingly run by liberal journalists."

"The school uses its position as a leading journalism institution to promote a liberal agenda that has sweeping impact on the news Americans consume," the MRC said in a report on higher education.

Meanwhile, Weiss has made several changes to "60 Minutes" during her tenure, which has been marked by sharp criticism from liberal media observers. Pelley was fired from the long-running CBS News show in June after he accused Weiss of "murdering" "60 Minutes" during a tense all-staff meeting that was supposed to be new executive producer Nick Bilton’s introduction to the staff.

"She’s murdering ‘60 Minutes.’ She does not love this place. She was brought in to kill it and is doing exactly that," Pelley told staffers.

SCOTT PELLEY HAS HEATED CONFRONTATION WITH NEW ‘60 MINUTES’ BOSS, ACCUSES BARI WEISS OF ‘MURDERING' SHOW

Bari Weiss, Nick Bilton and Scott Pelley. (Michele Crowe/CBS News ©2025; Michael Kovac/Getty Images for Vanity Fair)

Pelley also told Bilton, who has no linear television experience, that he has "slender qualifications" for his new role. Pelley was fired the next day, with Bilton writing that he "hijacked" the meeting to disparage management.

"Yesterday’s performative display of hostility — enacted in front of the staff instead of in a civil, private conversation — demonstrated that you have no interest in contributing to the future success of the show, or approaching my new tenure with a mind open to collaboration and progress. I am here to deliver first-in-class news programming, not to make headlines about newsroom drama," Bilton wrote to Pelley in a memo obtained by Fox News Digital.

As for Alfonsi, CBS News declined to renew her contract months after she lashed out at Weiss for delaying a segment about allegations of abuses at the El Salvador prison CECOT.

CBS NEWS FIRES ‘60 MINUTES’ CORRESPONDENTS, TOP PRODUCER IN SWEEPING SHAKEUP OF STORIED PROGRAM

Former "60 Minutes" correspondent Sharyn Alfonsi. (Michele Crowe/CBS via Getty Images;)

Last year, Weiss delayed the "Inside CECOT" segment that featured Alfonsi interviewing some released deportees, who described torturous conditions. A CBS spokesperson told Fox News Digital at the time that it was determined the segment needed "additional reporting," seemingly due to concerns about not yet having an on-the-record response from the Trump administration for the newsmagazine segment.

In a stunning note to fellow "60 Minutes" staffers that quickly leaked to the media, Alfonsi said her segment was being held for political reasons, not editorial ones. Alfonsi told colleagues Weiss had "spiked" the story and not given her a chance to discuss it further.

CBS ended up airing the segment in January.

Fox News Digital’s Joseph A. Wulfsohn contributed to this report.

Brian Flood is a media editor/reporter for FOX News Digital. Story tips can be sent to brian.flood@fox.com and on Twitter: @briansflood.

title: 'The Exorcist' star Linda Blair speaks out after home searched in reported 100-dog kennel investigation
excerpt:
Second Chance Rescue NYC founder Jennifer Brooks tells Fox News Digital passionate advocates like Elaine Hendrix are key as she raises concerns about animal overpopulation at NYC gala event.

Linda Bl...
body_text:
Second Chance Rescue NYC founder Jennifer Brooks tells Fox News Digital passionate advocates like Elaine Hendrix are key as she raises concerns about animal overpopulation at NYC gala event.

Linda Blair is speaking out after authorities searched her Southern California property as part of an active investigation into a reported kennel operation allegedly housing more than 100 dogs.

"The Exorcist" star, 67, said she and the animals in her care are "good" after a "surprise" visit from Los Angeles County officials on Friday.

Officials executed an inspection warrant as part of a joint operation between the Los Angeles County Department of Animal Care (DACC) and Control and the Los Angeles County Department of Regional Planning, according to People magazine. Officials told the outlet the operation was intended to evaluate the welfare of the animals and determine whether the property complies with county regulations.

"Checking in, I’m good. The animals are good in lieu of our surprise visit in 105° heat! With as busy as we all are in animal rescue and saving lives from the hot deserts and abandoned animals and shelters, everyone’s emails and social media are overloaded," Blair captioned a video posted to Instagram on July 31.

'EXORCIST' STAR LINDA BLAIR 'UNKNOWINGLY' WALKED AWAY FROM HOLLYWOOD

"The Exorcist" star Linda Blair speaks out after her California home was visited by authorities as part of an active investigation into a reported kennel operation. (Getty Images; Linda Blair Instagram)

"Turns out we just have some paperwork to do and some diagrams but as everybody knows, I’m looking to move so I can be more educational and help more animals. I’d rather move forward," she continued. "And I always say you know a good old-fashioned letter of contact always works. Be safe safe lives support animal rescue cause we’re all fighting to save lives.

The Oscar-nominated actress added that she has been planning to relocate her rescue operation.

The search was conducted after authorities sought to inspect a property "associated with a kennel operation reported to have more than 100 dogs," per People.

Officials alleged the kennel permits expired in 2023 and claimed multiple attempts to contact the property owner had gone unanswered.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

"The warrant allows us to lawfully access the property and verify compliance with County codes," the department said in a statement to People, adding that investigators were assessing "animal care, safety conditions, and overall welfare of the dogs housed on the property."

Blair, who rose to fame in "The Exorcist" in 1973, said the investigation was a mix-up over paperwork. (Getty Images)

"Our priority is the safety and well-being of both the animals on the property and the people who may be working or residing here," the statement continued. "This inspection will help us determine whether conditions meet required standards."

The DACC said the matter remains an active investigation and declined to provide additional details.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"As this is an active and ongoing investigation, DACC is not able to answer specific questions about this case at this time," the department said, adding that it is committed to ensuring kennel operations meet legal requirements and provide humane care.

TMZ, which first reported the search, said Blair was present during the inspection and cooperated with authorities. No dogs were removed from the property, according to the outlet.

Linda Blair "unknowingly" stepped away from acting to launch her Worldheart Foundation in 2003. (Getty Images)

In a video accompanying her Instagram post, Blair reiterated that the visit centered on administrative issues rather than the animals' condition.

"Today we got a really big surprise visit," she said in the video. "And as it turns out, there is nothing but some paperwork and some new diagrams and things."

"Wanted to check in and let you know I am fine. The animals are fine. And we just have some paperwork that has to be dealt with. And that's all this was all about. I don't know why mail isn't used more often to notify somebody. Just saying," she said, while also encouraging supporters to donate to the Linda Blair WorldHeart Foundation — the nonprofit she founded in 2003 to rescue and rehabilitate abused, neglected, and abandoned animals.

She ended her video by reiterating how she and the animals are doing, saying, "I wanna let you know I'm ok and so are the animals. Thank you so much."

Representatives for Blair and the Los Angeles County Department of Animal Care and Control did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

Christina Dugan Ramirez is an entertainment journalist with more than 15 years of experience, including a decade at PEOPLE writing high-profile cover stories, covering Hollywood's biggest events, and interviewing many of the industry's most influential stars before joining Fox News Digital in 2024.

title: Holdouts for Trump’s attorney general pick say they will advance his nomination to the full Senate – US politics live
excerpt:
Republican senators John Cornyn and Thom Tillis say that formal order withdrawing ‘anti-weaponization fund’ has addressed their concerns

Blanche formally rescinds Trump’s $1.8bn ‘anti-weaponization f...
body_text:
Republican senators John Cornyn and Thom Tillis say that formal order withdrawing ‘anti-weaponization fund’ has addressed their concerns

Blanche formally rescinds Trump’s $1.8bn ‘anti-weaponization fund’

Republican senators John Cornyn and Thom Tillis, two key holdouts on Todd Blanche’s attorney general nomination – now say they will vote to advance him to the full Senate.

The outgoing lawmakers, who have repeatedly clashed with Trump over the past year, said their concerns were resolved after “successful negotiation of a legally enforceable document” that formally ends the $1.8bn “anti‑weaponization fund” and makes clear that Trump and his family will not receive indefinite protection from audits of future tax filings. Both issues had been deal‑breakers for Cornyn and Tillis. In the document Blanche released on Sunday, the acting attorney general did say that the sweeping immunity offered to the president and his family for their past conduct does not change.

“We are pleased that the Department of Justice has issued a formal order terminating the anti-weaponization fund. Additionally, the department has acknowledged in a binding written order that the audit settlement is limited to the plaintiffs and the scope does not extend beyond the defendants in the lawsuit, the IRS and the Treasury, addressing concerns that multiple of our Republican colleagues share,” the pair wrote in a statement. “We look forward to voting to advance his nomination out of the Senate judiciary committee soon.”

The panel is set to vote on Blanche’s nomination on Tuesday.

On Truth Social today, Donald Trump has railed against polling which shows his approval rating stuck in the low end. According to a recent survey by AP-Norc, only 33% of Americans said they approved of the president’s job performance – slightly below where he stood at this point in his first term.

“My REAL Polling Numbers, not those made up by the Fake News Media, are the best they have ever been,” he wrote.

“Why wouldn’t they be with the biggest tax cuts and employment numbers EVER, the biggest outside Investment in America in World history, a totally secure Border, a giant Victory in Venezuela, the Denuclearization of Iran, unparalleled respect and success throughout the World, and much more? Don’t believe the Radical Left’s Fake Poll numbers.”

The outgoing lawmakers, who have repeatedly clashed with Trump over the past year, said their concerns were resolved after “successful negotiation of a legally enforceable document” that formally ends the $1.8bn “anti‑weaponization fund” and makes clear that Trump and his family will not receive indefinite protection from audits of future tax filings. Both issues had been deal‑breakers for Cornyn and Tillis. In the document Blanche released on Sunday, the acting attorney general did say that the sweeping immunity offered to the president and his family for their past conduct does not change.

“We are pleased that the Department of Justice has issued a formal order terminating the anti-weaponization fund. Additionally, the department has acknowledged in a binding written order that the audit settlement is limited to the plaintiffs and the scope does not extend beyond the defendants in the lawsuit, the IRS and the Treasury, addressing concerns that multiple of our Republican colleagues share,” the pair wrote in a statement. “We look forward to voting to advance his nomination out of the Senate judiciary committee soon.”

The panel is set to vote on Blanche’s nomination on Tuesday.

On Tuesday, we’ll bring you the latest from Michigan where voters will head to the polls for competitive primaries in Senate and House races.

The most closely watched competition is the Democratic primary for the US Senate, where congresswoman Haley Stevens is up against former public health official Abdul El-Sayed. They’re vying to ultimately win the seat of outgoing senator Gary Peters in November. The race has now turned into a proxy battle for the future of the Democratic party. Establishment-backed Stevens has received support from party leaders and her race has been buoyed by millions from the pro-Israel lobby. Meanwhile the insurgent El-Sayed has built a strong grassroots movement and is endorsed by progressives lawmakers in the Democratic caucus.

There are also several competitive House primaries tomorrow –mirroring the same choice in the Senate race – where more moderate Democratic candidates will face off against progressives who reflect the changing face of the party.

Kay Granger, a former Republican representative, who was the first woman to win a US House seat from Texas, has died at age 83.

Granger served in the house from 1997-2025, and was the first female chair of the House appropriations committee. Before her role in federal office, she was the first woman elected mayor of Fort Worth, Texas.

In a tribute on social media, Republican House speaker Mike Johnson said that Granger “broke barriers for women in public service”.

My colleague Ramon Antonio Vargas previously reported that Granger largely disappeared from the public eye after she announced her plans to retire when her term ended in early 2025.

Granger’s son later reportedly told the Dallas Morning News that Granger was “having some dementia issues” and had moved into an independent senior living center with a memory care community on the same property. However, he disputed that she was being treated at the memory care community and said she was a resident of the independent living side of the property.

Homeland security officials under the Trump administration have quietly attempted to subject at least 10 hunger strikers in US immigrant detention to involuntary medical procedures, including force-feeding, a Guardian investigation has found.

In 2025 and 2026, officials had definitely performed the procedures on at least three detained immigrants and probably subjected two more to the forced treatment – widely considered torture by human rights groups. The other five people gave in and broke their hunger strike at the last minute as force-feeding procedures loomed.

The government has not publicly acknowledged the practice of involuntary medical procedures on striking detainees, as the number of people detained by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) increases nationwide.

More people have gone on hunger strike in ICE detention centers to protest against conditions and demand resolutions to legal cases.

The investigation, based on hundreds of pages of court records and interviews with multiple sources, reveals a clearer picture of the federal government’s response to hunger strikes within secretive ICE facilities.

In the cases reviewed by the Guardian, the involuntary procedures included force-feeding, where medical staff coercively insert a tube through a hunger striker’s nose and down their throat then pump in nutritional shakes – an agonizing and traumatizing procedure that experts say can cause significant harm to the nose, esophagus and body organs. Other procedures included intravenous forced hydration, involuntary blood draws and the collection of urine samples.

Read the breakdown of the Guardian’s investigation here:

A reminder that my colleagues are covering the latest out of the Middle East at our dedicated live blog. This includes the latest drop in oil prices, since Trump walked back his threats to strike Iran on Sunday.

Brent crude, the international benchmark, was trading 5% lower at $83.50 a barrel by mid-morning, after falling as low as $81.55 a barrel.

As we reported earlier, Republican senator Bernie Moreno has now publicly called for Representative Max Miller, his ex-son-in-law, to step down from Congress amid allegations of domestic and child abuse.

Trump, when asked about the allegations on Sunday on Air Force One, said he was “looking at” the claims against Miller.

“I’m gonna look at it. I mean, so far, it’s accusations,” the president added.

Miller and Emily Moreno, were in the middle of an acrimonious custody battle this year, when Miller filed a defamation against his former wife earlier this year.

On Sunday, Miller posted a video on social media, and continued to deny the allegations.

“I categorically deny abusing my former wife,” the Republican congressman said.

Donald Trump will be in Washington today. He’ll spend most of the day in meetings, but we’ll hear from him at 1.30pm ET when he signs an executive order in the Oval Office.

We’ll bring you the latest lines as that gets under way.

President Donald Trump said new talks to wind down the war in Iran will start Monday afternoon, after announcing he is holding off on new massive strikes he had threatened to unleash on the country.

The talks will seek to end the conflict and revive stalled cargo traffic through the strait of Hormuz, a crucial waterway through which about a fifth of all traded oil and natural gas passed before the war.

Iranian state media quoted the country’s foreign ministry as saying Tehran was not currently holding negotiations with the United States.

Robert F Kennedy Jr, the US health secretary, on Sunday told American parents that they should get their children vaccinated against measles, as the surge in infections has reached numbers not seen in the past 35 years.

Kennedy, a leading vaccination skeptic who has spent years amplifying misinformation about vaccines, including the shot that protects against measles, mumps and rubella (MMR), made his call in the course of a contentious interview with CNN’s State of the Union on Sunday morning.

His remark came as the incidence of measles crossed a milestone – the US has now officially recorded 2,371 confirmed infections so far this year, surpassing the total tally in 2025 of 2,289.

Taken together, the past two years have seen more measles infections in the US than the rest of the 21st century combined. The last time a greater number of measles cases were recorded in a single year was in 1991.

Kennedy’s statement was extracted from him by Dana Bash, CNN’s host, who invited him to use his “bully pulpit” to talk directly to parents as the new school year approached. She urged him to tell families that they should vaccinate for measles “because it is safe and it will help them save their children’s lives”.

The pastor of a historically Black church on St Louis’s north side, Rodrick Burton has watched with bewilderment as the congressional race in his district has drawn national attention not about the bloodshed in his community, but rather in Gaza.

“As a pastor who’s had eight members murdered, violence over there is terrible,” Burton said of the conflict in the Middle East.

“We have to deal with the problems right in our metropolitan area,” Burton added. “While there’s kinship and stuff … you’re talking about blood overseas, blood on the TV. We got blood right here in our metropolitan area.”

In Tuesday’s Democratic congressional primary, voters in Missouri’s deep-blue first congressional district will decide whether to give pro-Israel incumbent Wesley Bell a second term, or replace him with Cori Bush, a former progressive congresswoman who accuses Israel of perpetrating genocide in Gaza. Along with a heated primary in Michigan, the contest has become a proxy battle over the Democratic party’s role in supporting Israel’s military before the November midterm elections, which will determine which party holds the majority in both chambers of Congress.

After losing to Bell two years ago, Bush is vying for her seat back, and a Super Pac linked to the American Israel Public Affairs Committee (Aipac) has so far spent more than $3m to try to keep her out.

In recent weeks, Democratic voters in New York City and Denver ousted incumbents in favor of candidates who promised they would take a hard line against support for Israel. In Congress, large shares of Democrats have voted for unsuccessful efforts to block arms sales to the country’s security forces, and progressives hope that a win by Bush will underscore their movement’s momentum.

Hello and welcome to the US politics live blog.

Acting US attorney general Todd Blanche issued a formal order late on Sunday terminating Donald Trump’s $1.8bn “anti-weaponization fund” to compensate his political allies.

The move follows weeks of negotiations with two Republican senators who were blocking his nomination to become attorney general.

While Blanche has repeatedly said publicly that the fund was dead, the justice department had resisted formally confirming that in writing. That had drawn concern from lawmakers that it could be revived in some form, especially after Trump expressed continued support for the idea.

A spokesperson for Texas Senator John Cornyn, one of the senators holding up Blanche’s nomination, confirmed the agreement. The other GOP senator, North Carolina Senator Thom Tillis, did not have immediate comment.

The announcement comes ahead of a Senate judiciary committee vote on Blanche, which is scheduled for Tuesday.

“My team and I have met with committee members and Senators over the past several weeks and addressed any concerns or outstanding questions,” Blanche said in a post on X. “We have enjoyed good faith discussions, and as a result issue the following order.”

The order says that “although the acting attorney general has repeatedly advised Congress through testimony, including under oath, as well as in written responses, that the Fund is not moving forward, and the Department has repeatedly represented to district courts that the Fund is not moving forward, today’s Order officially rescinds the May 18, 2026 Order.”

The document released by Blanche on Sunday night also limits the scope of another provision of the settlement that provided broad immunity for Trump and members of his family from tax audits. It clarifies that the tax audit immunity agreement “applies only retroactively” to claims open at the time of the settlement and does not protect the president from examination of future tax filings.

Kennedy, a leading vaccination skeptic who has spent years amplifying misinformation about vaccines, including the shot that protects against measles, mumps and rubella (MMR), made his call in the course of a contentious interview with CNN’s State of the Union on Sunday morning.

Donald Trump has said he cancelled planned military strikes against Iran on the basis of “rapidly” reaching a deal on its nuclear programme and the full reopening of the strait of Hormuz. The president paused the strikes in expectation of a breakthrough and in response to requests from Iran and other countries in the region, he claimed on his Truth Social platform on Saturday.

Marcy Kaptur is being treated ⁠for non-life-threatening injuries after a car crash in Toledo, ⁠Ohio, on Sunday, ⁠the ​Democratic US representative’s office said. Kaptur, 80, was a passenger ⁠in the vehicle and on her way to church, her office ⁠said. Toledo police did not ​respond to ‌a request from Reuters for ‌comment.

Republican senator Bernie Moreno on Sunday publicly called for Representative Max Miller, his ex son-in-law, to step down from Congress amid allegations of domestic and child abuse. As recently as Friday, the Ohio senator had avoided giving his opinion directly on accusations made by his daughter, Emily Moreno, against the congressman.

The family of a Haitian immigrant who froze to death in early March at a bus shelter in Pittsburgh after she was dropped off in the city by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) is poised to file a lawsuit this month against the United States and “multiple other governmental and non-governmental entities”, the Guardian has learned.

title: 49ers betting preview suggests Rams and Seahawks could overtake San Francisco for playoffs
excerpt:
The "NFL on FOX" crew broke down the San Francisco 49ers' 23-19 win over he Philadelphia Eagles in the Wild Card Round.

Technology is fun. I wrote this article once already, and something happened wh...
body_text:
The "NFL on FOX" crew broke down the San Francisco 49ers' 23-19 win over he Philadelphia Eagles in the Wild Card Round.

Technology is fun. I wrote this article once already, and something happened where it disappeared altogether. I really don’t know what the issue is or was, but maybe the second time I dissect the San Francisco 49ers' upcoming season will be even more exciting than the first time.

This was a team that I struggled to bet on or against last season. When I was betting they would lose, they came out with some miracle game. When I bet they would win, they looked like they had never played football before. I can still admit that the squad was impressive despite navigating a wide range of injuries. They were 12-5 for the season and got a 5-3 record from their backup quarterback, Mac Jones. Every loss they took in the regular season was against a postseason team, with the exception of Tampa Bay. They did win the first game of the postseason, taking out the reigning Super Bowl champion Eagles. Then disaster struck against the Seahawks. They gave up a game-opening kickoff return for a touchdown. Then turned the ball over on downs, leading to a Seattle field goal. A fumble and another Seattle touchdown put them down 17-0 after the first quarter. The second half was even worse in many ways. They turned the ball over on downs, then had an interception, turnover on downs, fumble, punt, and then ran three meaningless plays to end the game.

49ERS BRING BACK DEEBO SAMUEL TO FILL VOID LEFT BY RICKY PEARSALL'S KNEE INJURY: REPORT

San Francisco 49ers tight end George Kittle (85) greets his wife Claire Kittle before a preseason game against the Las Vegas Raiders at Allegiant Stadium on Aug. 23, 2024 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Chris Unger/Getty Images)

The team that deals with many injuries at many positions took a shot with someone uber talented, but also coming off of an injury-marred season. Mike Evans, who played only eight games last season, is now their primary receiver. If he is healthy, which he has been most of his career, he will be a difference-maker. They also added Christian Kirk, providing quarterback Brock Purdy with some solid options. It seems like they assumed offense was the priority, considering they also drafted a wide receiver in the second round. Their main addition on defense was Osa Odighizuwa; if he can replicate his season from last year, this should be an even tougher defense.

Brock Purdy #13 of the San Francisco 49ers looks to pass against the Dallas Cowboys during the first quarter in the NFC Divisional Playoff game at Levi's Stadium on January 22, 2023 in Santa Clara, California. (Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images)

49ERS HAVE SUCCEEDED WITH TALENT ACQUISITIONS BUT FAILED AT ADDITION BY SUBTRACTION OF BRANDON AIYUK

The biggest issue I have with the 49ers is that they don’t ever seem to be healthy. There is a ton of talent on this roster, but if you look at the names on paper and those who are actually available, there is a large gap. Christian McCaffrey is one of the best backs in the league, but he misses games fairly regularly. Brock Purdy consistently misses games. Nick Bosa and Fred Warner both played fewer than 10 games last season. George Kittle is on the PUP list to start the year. Ricky Pearsall has some issues with his knee again as well. Healthy, they are elite, but that’s going to be a major question mark for this team all season.

San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan watches from the sideline during the second half of an NFL football game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Tampa, Florida, on Oct. 12, 2025. (AP Photo/Chris O'Meara)

Their head coach, Kyle Shanahan, has been great at getting the most out of his team regardless of who is on the field. However, I have some concerns that as these players age, they may not be able to go as far as long. No team will be healthy the whole season, but some of these guys are more consistently off the field than they are on the field. At 9.5 games, I don’t love taking the over – even though I think it hits, but you’re playing it at -145 or higher. Instead, I think we bet that there are going to be pieces missing and the Rams and Seahawks will still be better. I’ll take San Francisco to miss the playoffs at +122 if I had to take anything. Most likely I’ll just stay away.
