Got a tech question? Get Kurt’s free CyberGuy Newsletter, share your voice, a story idea or comment at CyberGuy.com.

title: Cheryl Reeve sends clear message to Sophie Cunningham with ‘Trans Kids Belong’ shirt during Fever-Lynx game
excerpt:
A pro-trans athlete protester waves a fan with a slur on it toward supporters of Indiana Fever star Sophie Cunningham. (Credit: Dustin Grage/Townhall columnist)

Minnesota Lynx head coach Cheryl Reeve...
body_text:
A pro-trans athlete protester waves a fan with a slur on it toward supporters of Indiana Fever star Sophie Cunningham. (Credit: Dustin Grage/Townhall columnist)

Minnesota Lynx head coach Cheryl Reeve made her position clear Sunday afternoon.

Reeve wore a shirt reading "Trans Kids Belong" underneath her blazer while coaching against Sophie Cunningham's Indiana Fever at Target Center. There’s no reason to pretend the timing was coincidental.

TRANS ACTIVISTS HARASS, HURL SLURS AT SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM SUPPORTERS BEFORE FEVER GAME IN MINNESOTA

Reeve had already addressed the transgender-athlete debate before the game, saying she comes from "a space of inclusion," that "we need to protect trans kids" and that "every kid has a right to sports." Her comments came with another rally supporting Cunningham’s position taking place outside the arena before the Fever-Lynx matchup. Then, Reeve carried the message onto the sideline.

Of course, she has every right to wear the shirt. The Lynx have every right to support her. But it was also an unmistakable response to Cunningham, who has spent the past two weeks taking heavy criticism for saying girls and women shouldn’t have to compete against biological men or share locker rooms with them.

Minnesota Lynx head coach Cheryl Reeve wore a ‘Trans Kids Belong’ shirt as the Lynx faced Sophie Cunningham’s Fever, adding new fuel to the WNBA’s trans-athlete debate. (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect)

Why anyone feels the need to argue against Cunningham's common-sense take is another matter. But it's also important to note that Cunningham never said transgender kids don’t belong in sports, society or anywhere else. In fact, she said she had "never once" expressed hatred toward transgender people and argued that there is room for everyone. Her position was more specific: "I want to protect young girls in a locker room, or young girls in sport who shouldn’t have to go against biological men."

Reeve’s shirt collapsed that distinction into a progressive slogan.

By wearing "Trans Kids Belong" while coaching against Cunningham, Reeve implied that Cunningham’s position is about excluding transgender children entirely. It isn’t. Cunningham drew a line at participation in girls’ and women’s sports and access to female locker rooms.

That position is not only reasonable, but the position the majority of Americans hold.

FEVER SHUT DOWN SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM QUESTIONS, ABRUPTLY END PRESS CONFERENCE

To Reeve’s credit, she acknowledged before the game that the issue becomes more complicated after puberty and when Olympic spots or scholarships are involved. She argued that people should find common ground rather than make exclusion the answer. That is a more nuanced argument than the shirt conveyed.

Still, Cunningham didn’t say trans kids don’t belong. So, Reeve answered the argument she wanted Cunningham to make rather than the one Cunningham actually made.

Minnesota Lynx coach Cheryl Reeve wore a 'Trans Kids Belong' shirt while coaching against Sophie Cunningham and the Indiana Fever during a marquee WNBA matchup. (Getty Images)

That would have been an obvious subject to ask Reeve about after the game. Fox News Digital and OutKick tried to be there to ask those questions, but the Lynx denied our credential request.

The request was submitted July 30 for an Aug. 2 game. The Lynx’s stated deadline was 5 p.m. on Aug. 1, meaning the application arrived more than two days before the game and well before the deadline. The denial didn’t cite timing, capacity or any other specific reason.

After I posted about the denial on social media, several WNBA reporters and fans celebrated it. Some argued that local beat writers should receive priority. Others suggested that outlets should only receive access if their reporters regularly attend practices and ask questions about basketball.

The first point is reasonable. Local reporters who cover a team every day should be prioritized.

But "prioritized" and "exclusively credentialed" aren’t the same thing. Fox News Digital and OutKick regularly cover the WNBA, and I was credentialed for both the 2026 NBA Finals and the 2026 Final Four despite not working as a full-time beat reporter for the NBA or college basketball.

So, are regular-season WNBA games really a more exclusive media credential than the NBA Finals or Final Four?

More importantly, the "stick to basketball" defense completely fell apart the moment Reeve walked onto the sideline wearing that shirt. If reporters are only supposed to ask about basketball, why is the head coach using a WNBA game to make a statement about one of the country’s most contentious social debates?

WNBA SUDDENLY WANTS TO STICK TO BASKETBALL AFTER YEARS OF MAKING POLITICS PART OF THE PRODUCT

Reeve didn’t wear a shirt about transition defense. She didn’t promote rebounding or ball movement. She used the sideline to send a message about transgender children while coaching against the player at the center of the league’s transgender-athlete controversy.

Again, that’s her right. But once she makes the statement during the game, questions about that statement become relevant to the game.

The Lynx were asked whether Reeve’s shirt was intended as a response to Cunningham’s comments and whether the organization approved or coordinated the decision and endorsed the message. The team didn’t respond before publication.

Minnesota Lynx head coach Cheryl Reeve looks on in the third quarter of their game against the Las Vegas Aces at Michelob Ultra Arena on Aug. 2, 2025. (Candice Ward/ Imagn Images)

Perhaps Reeve would have said the shirt had nothing to do with Cunningham. That would be difficult to believe given the opponent, her comments before the game and the controversy surrounding the Fever’s road trip, but she deserved the opportunity to explain it.

Instead, WNBA defenders celebrated a credential denial while insisting reporters should focus on basketball, then watched a head coach turn the sideline into a platform for a social message. The league and its teams routinely promote inclusion, open dialogue and the importance of athletes and coaches using their platforms. Those principles seem to become much less important when the questions might challenge the preferred position.

Reeve was free to wear the shirt. The Lynx were free to deny the credential. And WNBA reporters were free to cheer that decision.

But taken together, the message was clear: approved social statements belong on the sideline.

title: Burnham to be ‘relentless’ on small boat crossings after Ceuta crisis
excerpt:
Prime minister says UK needs to ‘bring back that control’ and safe routes for refugees are necessary to tackle trafficking

Andy Burnham has pledged to be “relentless” in tackling small boat crossings...
body_text:
Prime minister says UK needs to ‘bring back that control’ and safe routes for refugees are necessary to tackle trafficking

Andy Burnham has pledged to be “relentless” in tackling small boat crossings after tens of thousands of migrants entered the Spanish territory of Ceuta, and he said “safe routes” for refugees were necessary to tackle trafficking gangs.

Speaking during a visit to Dover, the prime minister said he had been assured by the Spanish prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, that approximately 98% of the estimated 50,000 people who entered Spain’s north African territory of Ceuta last week had now been returned to Morocco.

But while that dealt “substantially” with the immediate issue, “of course there’s a broader issue about the Schengen area and our relationship with it”, he said, adding: “I would want to be in regular dialogue with the EU on those issues”.

Asked if he wanted to change the tone of the debate on the issue by stressing the need for safe routes, he said the UK had to “deal with the issue rather than play politics with the issue” and make changes that would reassure the public.

“The public don’t like the idea that the border looks like it’s not controlled. We need to bring back that control, but also we need to offer support for people who genuinely need it,” he said. “It’s about changing the whole approach, and slowly but surely we are putting in place those building blocks of a very different approach to this issue.”

Last Wednesday was the busiest day for small boat crossings across the Channel so far this year, with 752 people arriving in the UK. Official provisional figures suggest 14,526 have entered the UK so far this year. This is 43% lower than the number recorded by this time last year (25,436) and down 14% on the same period in 2024 (16,903).

“Progress is being made but we’re not complacent,” Burnham said. He said the number of National Crime Agency officers tackling organised immigration crime had more than doubled since the start of 2025, from 376 to almost 800.

On Sunday the latest figures showed that more than 2,000 people had crossed the Channel in small boats since Burnham became prime minister. Home Office numbers showed 326 people arrived on Saturday in four boats, bringing the number up to 2,057 since he took over from Keir Starmer on 20 July. There were 1,962 crossings in the same period last year.

On a separate visit to the National Crime Agency headquarters in Stratford, Shabana Mahmood said the government’s work to tackle small boat crossings were beginning to “bear fruit”.

The home secretary has faced fierce opposition within the ranks of the Labour party over proposed immigration measures including doubling the time it takes to qualify for indefinite leave to remain from five to 10 years. But she said reform was needed “to address the pull factors that draw people into boats in the Channel”, adding: “I want to change the calculus. I want them to change their mind about whether they get on the boat in the first place.”

She rejected calls to copy Spain’s response to the influx into Ceuta, in which tens of thousands of people have been returned to Morocco without processing any asylum claims. That was possible because Morocco and Spain share a land border and have an agreement in place. Mahmood said people smuggling and the shared waters of the Channel made things “trickier in many ways”.

At least 72 people died trying to reach Ceuta, some of them drowning and others being crushed when attempting to climb the border fence.

Sánchez called the huge influx “a violation of Spain’s territorial integrity”. The surge of people, which took place over the course of just 24 hours from Thursday, overwhelmed the city of 85,000 people, triggered a political crisis for Madrid and led to an angry reaction from some EU countries, including calls for Spain to be suspended from the Schengen free-movement zone.

On Saturday, Spanish police installed a 500-metre (1,640ft) floating barrier off its border ‌with Morocco to prevent others from making their way around the border. But Spain’s leftwing government has continued to come under pressure from right and centre-right governments already angry at its plan to regularise about 500,000 immigrants living in Spain.

EU ministers have convened emergency talks for Tuesday. The leaders of 22 EU countries have demanded an emergency response, citing the need to prevent further uncontrolled crossings. The summit was called during a “sobering” meeting of officials representing EU member states and Frontex border agency experts on Saturday, as EU leaders sought to heal divisions in the bloc and restore a unified approach to migration.

title: Republican calls for Max Miller to resign from Congress amid abuse allegations
excerpt:
Senator Bernie Moreno says congressman and former son-in-law should step down after ex-wife’s allegations

Republican senator Bernie Moreno on Sunday publicly called for Representative Max Miller, his...
body_text:
Senator Bernie Moreno says congressman and former son-in-law should step down after ex-wife’s allegations

Republican senator Bernie Moreno on Sunday publicly called for Representative Max Miller, his ex son-in-law, to step down from Congress amid allegations of domestic and child abuse.

As recently as Friday, the Ohio senator had avoided giving his opinion directly on accusations made by his daughter, Emily Moreno, against the congressman.

“If there are any basic standards of character required to hold elected office, Max Miller fails them. He should not serve in the House of Representatives,” the Ohio senator wrote in a post on X on Sunday. “I believe Max Miller needs to seek professional help to end the clear pattern of abuse he has left in his wake. I believe he should not be free to continue endangering others until he does.”

Moreno also said he had hoped the situation would remain private but added that Miller’s “increasingly erratic and dangerous behavior has made that impossible”.

The senator’s statement came hours after Miller released a livestream Sunday morning denying allegations of domestic and child abuse and insisting he would remain in the race for re-election. The public appearance came ahead of Wednesday’s deadline to replace him on the ballot.

“Just want to be clear: no court, no agency has ever substantiated any allegation of abuse against me. No criminal charge has ever been filed against me,” Miller said on the livestream. “Every single one of these allegations were already investigated, and I cooperated fully every single time because I had nothing to hide and I have nothing to hide now.”

The statement follows allegations that Miller poured hot water on Emily Moreno, held a gun to her head and broke their toddler daughter’s collarbone. The accusations have intensified scrutiny of Ohio’s seventh congressional district race, with Democrats viewing the seat as a possible pickup while Republicans have largely remained silent so far.

When asked on Friday by NOTUS whether Miller should continue his re-election campaign, Moreno responded, “I don’t know,” according to the outlet.

Miller, 37, has denied allegations made by both his ex-wife, Emily Moreno, and former girlfriend Stephanie Grisham, the former White House press secretary, as he continues his re-election campaign.

Emily Moreno, a conservative policy adviser, shares a two-year-old daughter with Miller. The former couple has been involved in a custody dispute over their child since 2024. In his Sunday statement, Bernie Moreno said it had been “horrific” to witness the situation unfold in view of the public “all while knowing an innocent two-year-old girl is caught in the middle.”

Among the allegations, Emily Moreno testified earlier this year in connection with a defamation lawsuit filed against her by Miller that he “took hot water from a pan he had just cooked eggs in and threw it at me”. She has also accused Miller of holding a gun to her head, according to the New York Times. The couple married in 2022.

title: Bill Maher warns that the Democratic Party is being 'colonized' by socialists, says his 'vote is in play'
excerpt: Comedian Bill Maher argued on Friday's episode of HBO's "Real Time" that the Democratic Party is being "colonized" by socialist ideology, saying the influence of the Democratic Socialists of America h...
body_text:
Comedian Bill Maher argued on Friday's episode of HBO's "Real Time" that the Democratic Party is being "colonized" by socialist ideology, saying the influence of the Democratic Socialists of America has left his "vote in play."

Comedian and talk show host Bill Maher doubled down on his previous comments suggesting his "vote is in play" in coming elections, as he expressed his discontent over the Democratic Party being "colonized" by radical, socialist views.

During Friday night’s episode of HBO’s "Real Time," Maher blasted the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) agenda that appears to be taking hold within the mainstream Democratic Party.

"People gotta realize this is going on," Maher said. "Yes, my vote is in play. I'm not voting for anyone who thinks the wrong side won the Cold War or cheers for the intifada like it's the World Cup."

MAHER SHAMES CLINTONS, KAMALA, DEMS, SAYING THEY WON'T GO ON HIS SHOW OR ANYWHERE THEY AREN'T 'PRE-ADORED'

"Real Time" host Bill Maher on July 31st warned his fellow liberals that the Democratic Party is being "colonized" by extreme socialists.  (HBO)

Maher went on to poke fun at the sheer irony of the apparent political takeover within a party that has platformed against such views.

"It's so ironic from the people who obsess about colonization," Maher said. "You know what's being colonized now? The Democratic Party."

He then pointed to two congressional Democrats — Rep. Tom Suozzi, D-N.Y., and Rep. Adam Gray, D-Calif.— after the pair launched a pledge to moderate the party amid the internal rise in DSA views.

RAHM EMANUEL WARNS DSA AGENDA DOESN'T PLAY WELL OUTSIDE 'UPPER WEST SIDE OF MANHATTAN'

Members of the Democratic Socialists of America gather outside a Trump-owned building on May Day, May 1, 2019, in New York City. (Getty Images)

"Last month, two Democratic congressmen released an open pledge," Maher told the audience. "They wanted their fellow Democratic members to sign. It said, ‘We are capitalists, not socialists. We want safety, not lawlessness. We are proud, not ashamed of America.’ These should not be hard words for a congressional Democrat to sign onto."

"You know how many did?" Maher continued. "Eight [members]. Eight, out of 212."

He added that while the DSA platform may appear to be making waves throughout the party, most mainstream politicians do not align themselves with the radical-left views.

SEN MARK KELLY WARNS FAR-LEFT POLICIES THAT ‘DON’T MAKE SENSE’ COULD COST DEMOCRATS SEATS

Bill Maher attends the 27th Annual Mark Twain Prize for American Humor gala at The Kennedy Center on June 28, 2026, in Washington, D.C. (Shannon Finney/WireImage)

"And, no, this nonsense is not where most Democratic politicians are right now," Maher said. "But it's also becoming a raging fire festival in the party that neither is anyone putting out."

"People are actually getting elected now who literally don't think we should have police or prisons or borders," he added.

Maher’s comments come after Fox News Digital previously reported he told ABC News "This Week" co-anchor Jonathan Karl that his "vote is in play" due to his unhappiness with the direction the Democratic party is heading.

"My vote is in play because it can’t be Trump running, so I’m not living in communist America," Maher said last month.

"I mean, I know the talking point is that it’s not communism, it’s socialism. OK, I’ve read the quotes from the DSA platform from their own mouths. Don’t tell me I’m not seeing what I am seeing," he added at the time.

The sentiment was echoed by former state attorney Dave Aronberg, who told Fox News Digital the DSA's platform could be what brings an end to the Democrats' short-lived momentum in the polls.

"History and current polling trends point to a blue wave in November, and the DSA is the only thing that can stop it," Aronberg said. "Outside of concentrated blue enclaves in places like New York and Denver, general elections aren't won on the far-left fringes. If the Democratic Party lets the DSA drive the bus, they’re driving straight off an electoral cliff."

"Bill Maher is voicing what millions of voters are thinking: The Democratic Party must not surrender to extremists who despise classic American principles," he added.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

Maher concluded his show Friday by referencing former Alaska governor Sarah Palin, suggesting he would rather vote for the longstanding Republican over DSA candidates running within his own party.

"Get your head out of your a–, I would vote for Sarah Palin before this s—," Maher said. "She's a bimbo, but if you asked her to come up with something she likes about America, she could do it. You betcha."

Fox News Digital reached out to the Democratic National Committee and the Democratic Socialists of America for comment.

Julia Bonavita is a media and culture writer for Fox News Digital, and a Fox Flight Team drone pilot. You can follow her at @juliabonavita13 on all platforms and send story tips to julia.bonavita@fox.com.

title: 'American Idol' winner says husband 'put his badge up' to support her music career
excerpt:
"American Idol" 2026 champion Hannah Harper tells Fox News Digital about her husband's career sacrifice, why he traded his badge for the road and how it changed their marriage.

Hannah Harper says her...
body_text:
"American Idol" 2026 champion Hannah Harper tells Fox News Digital about her husband's career sacrifice, why he traded his badge for the road and how it changed their marriage.

Hannah Harper says her husband made the ultimate career sacrifice to help launch her country music dreams.

The "American Idol" Season 24 winner exclusively revealed to Fox News Digital that her husband walked away from a nearly decade long career in law enforcement, "put his badge up" and joined her full-time on the road as her tour manager.

"It has definitely strengthened our marriage in ways that I didn't even know those muscles worked, if that makes sense," Harper said.

CARRIE UNDERWOOD SURPRISES 'AMERICAN IDOL' CONTESTANT WITH TIFFANY JEWELRY AND HANDWRITTEN NOTE

"American Idol" winner Hannah Harper says her husband left law enforcement and put his police badge up to become her tour manager as her country music career took off. (Eric McCandless / Disney)

"My husband was in law enforcement for eight years and put his badge up just so that I could pursue this. And he was doing insurance there for a little while. We were going to try to just do, like, a work-on-the-road kind of thing. And then music just got too busy. And he was like, 'You know what? I think I want to be tour manager.' And I was like, 'That's perfect. I think you should do that.'"

The career pivot came as Harper's schedule exploded following her "American Idol" victory, leaving the couple searching for a way to keep their family together while managing an increasingly busy tour calendar.

Harper is currently on her first national tour and recently landed her first major brand partnership with Sargento after her original song, "String Cheese," went viral during her "American Idol" run. The cheese company is sponsoring her tour with a custom-wrapped bus stocked with snacks for Harper, her band, crew and family.

"American Idol" champion Hannah Harper is on her first national tour and recently landed her first major brand partnership with Sargento. (Sargento / Hannah Harper)

However, working side by side with her husband has sometimes come with its own growing pains, Harper pointed out.

CARRIE UNDERWOOD WARNS HOLLYWOOD IS A 'SELF-SERVING BUSINESS,' CREDITS FAITH FOR KEEPING HER GROUNDED

"I think the biggest challenge now is because we're both working is, ‘OK, when are off hours?' You know, like when normal people go home, they're done working for the day, but our work is at home. And so, it's hard for us to be able to turn it off. But it's so much fun for both of us to be building this together."

WATCH: ‘AMERICAN IDOL’ WINNER SAYS HUSBAND TRADED POLICE BADGE FOR MUSIC TOUR LIFE

Before being crowned the winner of "American Idol" Season 24, Harper was already building a life with her husband, Devon Mendenhall. The couple, who married in April 2018, welcomed their first son the following year and have since grown their family to include three boys.

Hannah Harper was crowned the winner of "American Idol" Season 24. (Eric McCandless / Disney)

Harper said the family's all-in approach has become one of the most rewarding parts of her success.

"My entire family is on the road with me, both of my brothers, my parents, my kids. And I think it's so special that everyone has a role and a job, and everyone feels included."

Sargento is sponsoring Harper's tour after her original song, "String Cheese," went viral during her "American Idol" run. (Sargento / Hannah Harper)

The singer became emotional, reflecting on her husband's sacrifice.

"But more than anything, I feel honored that he was willing to step down from his position. A lot of men wouldn't do that. I think their pride would get in the way, and that man would bend over backwards for anything that I asked him to do."

WATCH: 'AMERICAN IDOL' WINNER CREDITS CARRIE UNDERWOOD FOR HELPING HER NAVIGATE FAME

As Harper adjusts to her rapid rise in country music, she said fellow "American Idol" winner, Carrie Underwood, offered advice that has helped her navigate the pressures of fame without losing herself.

LIKE WHAT YOU’RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"Carrie, just saying like social media, the stage presence that one has to have, it's like a character basically, and you have to separate that character from reality, which is hard for me because I want them to be the same."

Carrie Underwood gave Hannah Harper some advice after she won "American Idol." ( Eric McCandless/Disney via Getty Images)

"I want everyone to feel connected to me and know that I'm real and authentic, but there definitely has to be a separation on my stage mask and mom, if that makes sense. And so, I'm learning that very quickly and how important it is to be able to take it off and still be Mom and still be the Hannah I was before 'American Idol.'"

Harper said one of the biggest surprises following her "American Idol" win was watching "String Cheese" take on a life of its own.

WATCH: 'AMERICAN IDOL' WINNER REVEALS HOW VIRAL SONG KEEPS REOPENING HER DEEPEST WOUNDS

The deeply personal song, inspired by her experience with motherhood and postpartum depression, has become an anthem for parents who see themselves in its message.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

"I am so emotionally connected to the people who are going through it," Harper said.

Hannah Harper performing on "American Idol" earlier this year. (Frank Micelotta/Disney)

"In meet-and-greet lines... there are at least 50 of those are women who walked the exact same path as I did when it came to postpartum depression or just being in the trenches of motherhood. And getting to connect with them during their hardships... I relive all of those same emotions while talking to them and it still feels fresh."

Harper believes the song's impact extends beyond music.

"And I think that it's a song that continues to give, and I didn't write it on my own. I think the Lord just kind of like laid it in my lap, and He's used it to minister to people as well as me."Harper will remain on the road through November for her first national tour, with upcoming stops across the country and appearances alongside Brad Paisley and Lauren Alaina.

Stephanie Giang-Paunon is an entertainment reporter for Fox News Digital.

title: US reporter fighting back after border patrol seized his cell phones
excerpt:
Max Blumenthal says he was singled out at airport after Trump ally Laura Loomer targeted him in online posts

When reporter Max Blumenthal went to a cafe in Tehran one night a few weeks ago to upload ...
body_text:
Max Blumenthal says he was singled out at airport after Trump ally Laura Loomer targeted him in online posts

When reporter Max Blumenthal went to a cafe in Tehran one night a few weeks ago to upload videos from his reporting on the funeral of Iran’s supreme leader Ali Khamenei, he began seeing social media posts from Trump ally Laura Loomer targeting him, including one that suggested he should be “taken off the plane by US Marshalls when he lands back in the US … [and] detained”.

“I began to prepare myself for being harassed on my return,” Blumenthal said.

Effectively, that’s what happened, sparking a legal fight that freedom-of-the-press advocates say shows the determination of the Trump administration to crack down on members of the media whose reporting it disagrees with.

On 10 July, border batrol agents at Virginia’s Dulles airport flagged Blumenthal, founder of the independent outlet the Grayzone, for a “secondary inspection”. Agents asked him how he had paid for his trip to Iran, whether he knew the people who had hosted him and whether he had plans to return.

They asked to see his two phones. He declined to give them the passwords. They seized the phones, but not his laptop or digital cameras.

The federal agency returned the cell phones a week later – less than 24 hours after the American-Arab Anti-Discrimination Committee filed an emergency motion in district court seeking their return.

The US federal government said they couldn’t get into the phones and returned them, and that therefore the motion was moot. But Blumenthal went back to court on Wednesday and got a judge to agree that the government must prove it – by supplying evidence of who had his phones, when they had them and what they did to them. Federal judge Leonie M Brinkema gave the government 14 days to respond.

Blumenthal’s treatment and case pose “serious constitutional problems”, said Seth Stern, chief of advocacy at the Freedom of the Press Foundation. “The Trump administration is finding any excuse it can to target journalists it dislikes, and border searches are one more play in the playbook.”

It is the second case concerning cell phone seizures at US airports to hit federal courts in recent weeks, after another involving an activist against the Atlanta police-training center known as “Cop City” had its first evidentiary hearing.

Brinkema cited a recent fourth district ruling that distinguished a basic cellphone search – as in, the phone’s owner allows an agent to open the phone – from an “advanced” search, where “equipment, wired or wireless, [is used] to copy and/or analyze the contents of an electronic device”.

This is what federal agents sought to do with Blumenthal’s phones. “I believe now under fourth circuit case law, a search warrant would be required for that degree of intrusion into a cell phone,” Brinkema said, according to a transcript of the proceedings. No such warrant was produced for Blumenthal.

The incident is also the second recent case involving the federal government apparently seeking to discover the sources of journalists, after its failed attempt to subpoena New York Times reporters.

Jenin Younes, president of the American-Arab Anti-Discrimination Committee, noted that the border patrol agents seized only Blumenthal’s phones. “They didn’t take his laptop or digital camera,” she said. “That suggests they’re interested in contacts, sources, personal communications – maybe even tracking data.”

Brinkema mentioned the Times case in Wednesday’s hearing. “[G]iven the fact that this plaintiff is a reporter, this case has particular concern to the court because there’s been so much recently in the ether about attempts by the government to intrude upon a reporter’s right to report,” she said.

“And, you know, just recently in New York, we had the issue of the subpoenas that were issued to the New York Times reporters,” she continued. “I don’t think that can be overlooked.”

“We want to know what they did with [Blumenthal’s] phones,” Younes said. “We want to make sure the administration recognizes the serious privacy interests at stake in taking anyone’s phones – especially journalists.”

The judge suggested that Blumenthal could “probably have an expert take a look at his phones to see if there’s any indication […] they were somehow tampered with or accessed in some way”. Blumenthal said he’s “working on that – but it costs a lot”.

Younes pointed out that many other US journalists were in Iran to cover Khamenei’s funeral, including mainstream outlets like CNN and the Times – but there’s been no public disclosure of any other reporter being detained upon returning.

The posts by Loomer “raise the specter he’s being targeted for his views, for his journalism. This strengthens the first amendment aspect of his case.”

Blumenthal said the views that make him a target include him being a “Jewish anti-Zionist”.

Wednesday’s hearing, he said, was positive not just for him. “It has positive consequences for other journalists who have faced or will face this kind of repression, from an administration that isn’t responsive to the rule of law,” he said.

At the same time, the information he is seeking may turn into what Younes called “a protracted battle”, since the government’s attorney raised the issue that some of what was done with his phones may be “law enforcement privileged information”.

“You explain how this is done, and the individuals who we are trying to get information from are able to ‘beat it’,” he said.

title: ‘Agony and despair’: Nancy Guthrie’s family issues new plea for information on her whereabouts
excerpt:
Police also released notes received from presumed abductors of mother of Today anchor Savannah Guthrie

The family of Nancy Guthrie issued a new appeal on Saturday for information on the whereabouts o...
body_text:
Police also released notes received from presumed abductors of mother of Today anchor Savannah Guthrie

The family of Nancy Guthrie issued a new appeal on Saturday for information on the whereabouts of their missing grandmother, six months after she disappeared from her home in Tucson, Arizona, and a day after local investigators released two purported ransom notes.

“Six months ago, someone took her out of her bed in the dead of night. We have lived every moment, every breath, and every heartbeat in agony and despair ever since,” a post on Instagram said.

“Every day, we wake up and try to be strong and go on – because that’s what our joyful and resilient Mom taught us to do. But make no mistake – our hearts are in ruins,” the Guthrie family added.

Eighty-four-year-old Nancy Guthrie, mother of Today show anchor Savannah Guthrie, disappeared from her home on 1 February. But despite intense national attention and the involvement of the FBI, no suspects have been arrested in connection with her disappearance.

On Thursday, NBC News reported that two men who were detained and questioned in the days immediately after Nancy Guthrie vanished had issued a “notice of claim” against the Pima county sheriff, Chris Nanos, and a detective on the case.

The Pima county sheriff’s department posted a message saying, “The Guthrie investigation remains active and ongoing,” and later released notes received by news outlets soon after Guthrie disappeared.

The first note came from someone who claimed they had Guthrie – and that “she is safe but scared” and would not be released until payment in the form of $4m in bitcoin was received.

The second said that she had “perished shortly after she was taken. We believe it was heart related. She is buried in nature now.” The presumed abductors added: “Nothing you could have done could have changed the outcome. We want your family to know this and hope you all can find peace. We are truly sorry.”

On Saturday, the family issued a new appeal for information leading to Guthrie’s recovery.

“We are begging for help. We are desperate. We need someone to come forward. Someone knows something. Someone suspects something. Someone recognizes the writing in the ransom demand notes,” it read.

“Please. Bring her home,” the appeal concluded.

title: Exclusive: Israeli President Herzog blasts Mamdani, praises Trump, sounds alarm on Iran
excerpt: Just hours before President Trump announced that Hamas had agreed to a roadmap that includes disarmament, Israel's president discussed the U.S.-Israel alliance, Iran, Mamdani and much more. (Video: Yo...
body_text:
Just hours before President Trump announced that Hamas had agreed to a roadmap that includes disarmament, Israel's president discussed the U.S.-Israel alliance, Iran, Mamdani and much more. (Video: Yoav Dudkevitch for Fox News Digitial.)

JERUSALEM, Israel: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani is spreading hateful and antisemitic rhetoric and endangering the lives of New Yorkers, Israeli President Isaac Herzog told Fox News Digital in an exclusive interview at his Jerusalem residence.

"Mamdani does not respect my nation's right for self-determination… the Jewish people's inherent right to have a nation of their own. And he's basically spreading blasphemy, hate, antisemitic rhetoric. He should understand that he's risking his own citizens, he’s risking their safety, well-being and life," Herzog said.

In an incident that drew global attention, Mamdani posted a video on social media on July 21 in which he called Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu "a war criminal" and "the architect of a horrific genocide against the Palestinian people."

HUCKABEE WARNS OF 'BIBLICAL IGNORANCE' AS HE DEFENDS CONSERVATIVE SUPPORT FOR ISRAEL

President Isaac Herzog of Israel Mayor Mamdani, Israel's relationship with the U.S. in an interview with Fox News Digital in Jerusalem, Israel. (Yoav Dudkevitch/TPS-IL for Fox News Digital)

"This cannot be accepted in New York, which is a city which is dear to our heart, dear to the Israelis, and dear to me personally," Herzog said.

"I think New York will continue way after Mamdani. And I hope he won't create an irreversible damage," he added.

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani. (Adam Gray/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

On Iran, Herzog said the regime has for decades posed a strategic threat to global stability, and not only to Israel and the Middle East.

"They take their people's food and money and spend it on terror all over the world. It's a given fact," he said. "You ask yourself why a nation of this nature wants to have so much terror activity around the world, and that is because of ideology… The ideology does not accommodate any other religion or moderate Islam, for that matter. That is why it is so dangerous," he added.

The United States and Israel launched a joint military campaign against the Islamic Republic on Feb. 28, dubbed Operation Epic Fury by the Trump administration and codenamed Operation Roaring Lion by Israel, before Trump announced a ceasefire on April 7.

Herzog said Tehran’s missile program, activities around the Strait of Hormuz, nuclear ambitions, domestic repression and support for regional terror proxies as evidence of the regime’s major threat to U.S. national security interests. He added that many Americans had been killed by the Islamic Republic.

A billboard depicting Iran's supreme leaders since 1979: (L to R) Ayatollahs Ruhollah Khomeini (until 1989), Ali Khamenei (until 2026), and Mojtaba Khamenei (incumbent) is displayed above a highway in Tehran on March 10, 2026. Iran marked the appointment of Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei to replace his father as its supreme leader on March 9, 2026.  (AFP/Via Getty Images)

As some leading political voices in the U.S. have questioned the relationship with the Jewish state, the president stressed the important ties that have made the relationship so important.

"We both drink from this set of values which was commanded to all of us by these historic spiritual books given to us by the Almighty," he said.

The Israeli president highlighted what he described as Trump’s deep support for the Jewish state, demonstrated through both words and actions.

He pointed to Trump’s 2018 decision, during his first term, to relocate the U.S. embassy to Jerusalem, as well as his subsequent recognition of Israeli sovereignty over the Golan Heights.

ISAAC HERZOG ELECTED ISRAEL'S PRESIDENT, FOLLOWING IN FATHER'S FOOTSTEPS

Herzog praised Trump’s "endless" backing of Israeli positions "in so many issues" and his "immense support and friendship with Israel," adding that the two countries still more often than not see "eye to eye."

Herzog credited Trump with helping secure the return of 255 hostages held by Hamas following the Oct. 7, 2023, massacre. While acknowledging the efforts of many officials involved, he said Trump "put his foot down" and "pushed and negotiated brilliantly" to bring them home, adding that he had "huge respect" for the American leader.

That admiration among Israelis has not been diminished by any perceived political disagreements, Herzog said, adding that he believes the U.S.-Israel relationship transcends shifting attitudes and growing criticism of the Jewish state.

U.S. President Donald Trump enters the Knesset, Israel's parliament, with Israel's President Isaac Herzog and Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu (R) before he speaks on Oct. 13, 2025 in Jerusalem.  (Evan Vucci - Pool/Getty Images)

"I believe that there is something biblical and prophetic in the way our nations work together. And I truly believe that Israel should be a bipartisan issue of friendship and support," he added.

Herzog linked the reported decline in American support for Israel, particularly among younger people, to campaigns of well-funded disinformation on social media.

"It's very easy to smear Israel on TikTok, but that doesn't say the real truth. And I invite every young American to set foot in this country," he told Fox News Digital.

Herzog described Israel as a place where innovators flourish and great ideas are shared with the world, contributing enormously across fields including health, energy, science, agriculture and food security.

A NEW CHAPTER FOR AMERICA’S 250TH: 'J250' INITIATIVE PUTS JEWISH CONTRIBUTIONS IN THE SPOTLIGHT

Beachgoers on a beach in Tel Aviv, Israel, on Sunday, Aug. 6, 2023.  (Getty Images)

"There's a reason why Americans who visit our country, young Americans, fall in love with this country. And my aim in this interview is to … take off the terrible mask which was placed on our face by terrible forces, some of them, of course, forces which work on it all the time to tell a distorted story."

"We're a nation seeking peace, we're a nation seeking innovation, we are a nation bringing ideas which will save humanity, and we are [a] nation trying to do good," he continued. "And I hope and pray that we will have peace with our neighbors in the entire region, with our Palestinian neighbors as well. But that requires that Israel will be accepted and people will understand that we have security needs."

Herzog addressed the House's recent passage of a $1.15 trillion annual defense policy bill, which largely split along party lines, with the fiscal year 2027 National Defense Authorization Act receiving only six Democratic votes.

He described the development as a "red light," but said it does not signal the end of relations between the American and Israeli public or of bipartisan dialogue and support.

THE BEDROCK OF AMERICAN LIBERTY WAS LAID IN JERUSALEM

Israeli President Isaac Herzog speaks to a joint session of Congress, Wednesday, July 19, 2023, at the Capitol in Washington. (AP Photo/Jacquelyn Martin)

"Exactly three years ago, I spoke in the American Congress in front of a joint session of the House, marking 75 years of Israel's independence, and I had almost 30 standing ovations," he said.

"I'm aware … of the criticism, and aware of a huge campaign on campuses, and of huge money which was funneled to attack Israel, and also aware of our mistakes," he added.

Herzog said Israeli society is undergoing an evolution following Oct. 7, making it legitimate to ask difficult questions about the country’s future security after such a "horrendous, aggressive, cruel" attack.

At the same time, he said Americans are right to examine the bilateral relationship and Israel’s role in advancing U.S. national security interests.

Earlier this week, Prime Minister Netanyahu traveled to Washington, D.C., to meet with Trump and attend the memorial service for the late Republican Sen. Lindsey Graham of South Carolina.

U.S. Sen. Lindsey Graham, R-S.C., speaks to members of the media as the Trump Cabinet briefs members of Congress on Iran at the U.S. Capitol on March 3, 2026. in Washington, D.C., Trump administration Cabinet officials will be briefing all lawmakers in the House and Senate on U.S. and Israeli attacks on Iran. (Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images)

"Lindsey was ever active, always coming with new ideas, brilliant, understood world affairs like no one else, and understood Israel's role in protecting Western values and values of the free world," Herzog told Fox News Digital.

He said Graham also knew how to voice criticism, which is legitimate between friends, and enjoyed support across the Israeli political spectrum.

"[Graham] knew how to fight empires and nations of evil, and to stand up to them without fear. I will always remember him, Israel will always remember him. The Jewish people will always cherish his memory," Herzog added.

EXCLUSIVE: MEET THE MAN ISRAEL CHOSE TO BE ITS FIRST-EVER AMBASSADOR TO THE CHRISTIAN WORLD

Herzog also raised the importance of how Israel values Christian communities in the Holy Land and is committed to strengthening interfaith dialogue. He added that these communities are a top priority.

According to Israel's Central Bureau of Statistics, as of December 2025, Israel’s Christian population stood at approximately 184,200, representing 1.9% of the country’s total population. The community grew by 0.7% over the previous year.

"I myself met the Pope and spoke to him several times and went to the Holy See. I speak to all the heads of churches. I recently had the Greek Orthodox Patriarch and this morning the Cardinal of Jerusalem," Herzog said.

A delegation of 1,000 evangelical Christian pastors and influencers ever brought to Israel meets with former Hamas captives at the site of the Supernova music festival on Wednesday as part of the Friends of Zion Ambassador Program. (Shlomi Amsalem)

He continued, "I believe in real dialogue with our brothers and sisters from the Evangelical world in the United States and elsewhere. So, the Christian communities are a top priority in Israel and we are doing our best that they will flourish and grow."

Herzog spoke of a zero tolerance of anti-Christian behavior. "I know of cases where there was tension and we're dealing with it aggressively and there's a major reduction in moments of friction. Now we have to work hard throughout the region. Christian communities will be strong and will flourish because there is a movement to shun out Christian communities, especially in some of the Muslim world, in Palestinian communities and elsewhere. And we are dealing with it as well. And I'm here for any Christian community that needs support of any kind. People know it. And I speak to their leaders all the time."

EXCLUSIVE: SERBIAN PRESIDENT VUČIĆ SAYS SUPPORT FOR US 'SURGED' UNDER TRUMP, INVITES HIM TO VISIT BELGRADE

Herzog weighed in on the controversy surrounding the dismissal of the International Criminal Court’s Chief Prosecutor Karim Khan, who issued the arrest warrants against Netanyahu, after member states voted to remove him over sexual misconduct allegations.

Herzog said Khan "absolutely" pushed forward with the arrest warrants to try to distract attention from the sexual assault allegations against him. He added that Khan had wanted to come to Israel to meet with various experts and leaders, including the Israeli president himself.

"Everybody got ready to talk to him and present the real story and the real truth," Herzog told Fox News Digital. "His staff were on their way to the airport and all of a sudden he issued these orders and writs against Prime Minister Netanyahu, [then] Defense Minister [Yoav] Gallant and others. And only in hindsight now we know clearly that it was in order to divert attention from the sexual allegations.

Karim Khan is the ICC's chief prosecutor. (Getty Images)

"The case has to be dropped and the ICC should ... not fall into the trap of hate and lies that Karim Khan presented simply to cover for himself," said Herzog.

Lawyers for Karim Khan have said they "will challenge the lawfulness and fairness of the decision through all available legal mechanisms."

Just hours before President Trump’s announcement that Hamas had agreed to a roadmap that includes disarmament on Thursday, Herzog praised the "enormous efforts" by the U.S. administration to advance the next phase of the Gaza ceasefire.

"This is something that can be a major breakthrough if it happens. Let's remember, the 20-point plan of President Trump was approved by the [United Nations] Security Council, and the next phase is disarming of Hamas," Herzog told Fox News Digital.

President Donald Trump speaks during a summit to support ending the more than two-year Israel-Hamas war in Gaza after a breakthrough ceasefire deal, Monday, Oct. 13, 2025, in Sharm El Sheikh, Egypt. (AP Photo/Evan Vucci) (AP)

"The people of Gaza deserve a better life. And there is a real viable plan, including budget and efforts, how to change the course of the future," he added.

But one thing has to be made clear, he concluded: "Hamas cannot control Gaza and cannot turn it into a launching pad for terror and hate anymore."

Amelie Botbol is a freelance field reporter based in Tel Aviv, Israel, who reports on Israel-related news.

title: Fauci's Fifth fuels vow to haul him into court 'every day' despite Biden pardon
excerpt: Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis discusses Dr. Anthony Fauci's Senate hearing, reacting to the key moments from the testimony and sharing his perspective on Fauci's handling of the COVID-19 pandemic on 'Jess...
body_text:
Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis discusses Dr. Anthony Fauci's Senate hearing, reacting to the key moments from the testimony and sharing his perspective on Fauci's handling of the COVID-19 pandemic on 'Jesse Watters Primetime.'

Former National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases Director Dr. Anthony Fauci may be spending more time in the Deep South than he envisioned after officials in Alabama and Florida announced plans to investigate whether he can be held accountable under state law for maladministration of the COVID-19 response.

Fauci invoked his Fifth Amendment right against self-incrimination 111 times during a Senate hearing Wednesday.

Sen. Josh Hawley, R-Mo., argued that former President Joe Biden’s blanket pardon eliminated Fauci’s federal criminal exposure for covered conduct and undercut his basis for refusing to answer.

Sen. Tommy Tuberville, R-Ala., alluded to that detail and told Fox News Digital that same pardon cannot prevent prosecution at the state level under the Constitution — which says presidential pardons cover "offenses (sic) against the United States."

CAN FAUCI HIDE BEHIND THE FIFTH? GAME-CHANGING BIDEN PARDON MAY NOT PROVIDE COMPLETE COVER, EXPERTS SAY

Sen. Tommy Tuberville, R-Ala., left; Anthony Fauci, center; Florida AG James Uthmeier, right. (Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images; Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images; Joe Burbank/Getty Images)

"Anthony Fauci is responsible for the deaths of millions of Americans and tens of thousands of Alabamians," Tuberville told Fox News Digital. "The ‘pardon’ signed by Joe Biden’s autopen doesn’t apply to state-level crimes."

"When I’m governor of Alabama, I will look into ways we can hold Fauci accountable for all of the Alabamians who died under his watch," the former Auburn football icon said.

TOP 5 MOMENTS FROM FAUCI'S HEARING: PAUL BOOTS LAWYER, MORENO ERUPTS AS CONTEMPT VOTE LOOMS

Republican Alabama Senator and former college football coach Tommy Tuberville. (Office of Senator Tommy Tuberville)

Tuberville — who is favored to succeed term-limited Republican Gov. Kay Ivey in November — indicated he would order Fauci to Montgomery, Alabama, as many times as he could to face state charges, and encouraged Alabamians to bring their own civil claims against the 85-year-old immunologist.

Speaking to Newsmax from the Capitol, Tuberville separately fumed that Fauci "should be locked up before he leaves this building today."

FAUCI PRIVATELY TOOK CREDIT FOR COVID-19 LOCKDOWNS DESPITE PUBLIC DENIAL, NEWLY EXPOSED DIARY ENTRIES REVEAL

Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier announces during a press conference that his office is offering to send a team of additional prosecutors to the Ninth Circuit to assist Orange/Osceola State Attorney Monique Worrell with a backlog of cases, April 14, 2025. (Joe Burbank/Orlando Sentinel/Tribune News Service via Getty Images)

"We lost 20-30,000 (people) in Alabama alone, and I hope every damn one of them sues Fauci."

Tuberville said that if state prosecutors can't imprison Fauci, he would support voluminous litigation to "put him in court for the rest of his life where he can listen to the death he caused.

He told Fox Business that when he regularly heard from Fauci during COVID on the HELP Committee, and now believes he "lied … and knew he was lying" due in part to revelations in the doctor’s diary.

"He's going to court every day of his life for the rest of his life. And he's going (to) have to look these people in the face, these families, because the pardon does not cover state government."

Fox News Digital reached out to Ivey for comment on whether she would pursue similar action in the final months of her administration.

Florida also is investigating Fauci’s COVID-era tenure. Attorney General James Uthmeier confirmed to Fox News Digital that "any and all potential violations of Florida law" are on the table.

"Our inquiry will focus on what Fauci knew, when he knew it, and how he misled the American people. We will examine the physical and monetary harms to Floridians that may have resulted from his deceptions and determine whether his conduct exposes him to liability under state law," said Uthmeier press secretary Jae Williams.

Lt. Gov. Jay Collins — who is running for governor to succeed boss Gov. Ron DeSantis — fully backed Uthmeier’s probe in an interview Thursday with Fox News Digital.

"There has to be accountability ... between families getting threatened and our kids not being able to potentially go to school because of the risks coming from Fauci," he said.

Collins noted he is a 100%-disabled retired amputee veteran, and said he couldn’t get care from Veterans Affairs unless he had a COVID-19 shot.

Republican gubernatorial candidate Steve Hilton speaks to supporters at his primary night watch party, in Huntington Beach, California on June 2, 2026 (Paul Steinhauser/Fox News)

"I had to make a choice of getting my prosthetic care and having a leg to walk on versus taking an immunization that I didn't want or believe in," he said, blaming Fauci's prescriptions for "generational loss" of businesses nationwide.

Asked about Fauci criticizing DeSantis in his diary, Collins said it was a badge of honor to be the state on the receiving end of "pejoratives."

DeSantis "became America's governor. Greatest governor in our state's history, largely because of what he did in COVID. When our president, our federal government, other world leaders were attacking him, he stood there and took it over and over and over."

"We protected America," he said of Tallahassee’s government. "We pushed back on the Fauci-Ouchie and all the nonsense that came from it … I’m glad (Fauci) was offended."

DeSantis similarly called Fauci the "most destructive bureaucrat in the history of the United States of America," when asked on Fox News to respond to the diary entries that called him a "jerk" and more.

While California’s current leadership complied with and welcomed Fauci’s prescriptions, the state’s Republican gubernatorial nominee said after watching Fauci plead the Fifth, he drafted a plan similar to his Deep South compatriots to bring the bureaucrat to justice.

"What an absolute disgrace — when will there be any accountability for this guy," Hilton said in a statement.

"I tell you, when I'm governor of California we will have a COVID Accountability Commission," he said on Facebook, Hilton said the panel would examine Fauci and California officials over policies "who caused so much pain and suffering and cruelty in this absolute disaster of public policy."

Fox News Digital reached out to Fauci via counsel for comment. DeSantis' office directed Fox News Digital to his quoted comments.

Born and raised in Allentown, Pennsylvania, worked in both the New York and Washington bureaus for Fox News since 2013.

title: Trump vows to push $1.8bn slush fund as Senate committee set to reconsider AG nomination
excerpt:
After declaring ‘anti-weaponization’ fund ‘dead’, Trump reverses and says he’ll revive it despite Senate opposition

The US Senate judiciary committee has scheduled a meeting early next week to consid...
body_text:
After declaring ‘anti-weaponization’ fund ‘dead’, Trump reverses and says he’ll revive it despite Senate opposition

The US Senate judiciary committee has scheduled a meeting early next week to consider Todd Blanche’s nomination for attorney general, as Donald Trump promised to revive the controversial $1.8bn “anti-weaponization” fund.

The meeting, set for Tuesday, comes as Blanche’s confirmation ​has stalled over a dispute between the president and outgoing Republican senators John Cornyn and Thom Tillis, who are seeking written confirmation that the justice department would not establish the proposed fund.

A spokesperson for the committee said in a statement that Chuck Grassley, committee chair and Iowa Republican, “wants Todd Blanche’s nomination to be successful”.

“Grassley would like to see Blanche confirmed before the August recess as he has an excellent record restoring law and order and keeping Americans safe,” the statement added.

Opponents of the president consider it a slush fund to compensate political allies for political lawfare; supporters say it is a vehicle to compensate individuals who claim they were wrongfully targeted by the government more broadly.

“It is dead, but I wish ⁠it weren’t, to be honest with you. I think people were horribly treated, horribly abused,” Trump had said during a cabinet meeting on Friday. “I’d like to ⁠see them compensated for the pain.”

At the cabinet meeting on Friday, Trump urged Republican senators to confirm Blanche and warned that they “will never get anybody like him” and repeated a claim that ​Cornyn was blocking Blanche because Trump had endorsed Cornyn’s Republican primary challenger Ken Paxton.

“I’d be upset also,” ‌Trump said. “I fully understand it. He shouldn’t be that way. I shouldn’t be that way.“

Trump then slammed Cornyn and Tillis in a post on Truth Social on Saturday, claiming that both were upset because he had not endorsed them. Trump threatened to withdraw Blanche’s nomination, keep him on as acting attorney general and “push hard” for anti-weaponization bill.

“Todd Blanche was a voice of reason!” Trump wrote. “It will immediately be back on the table, and I will get it done.”

Blanche, Trump’s former personal attorney, has told senators that the fund was dead, but has so far not agreed to put that in writing. The “anti-weaponization” fund was crafted as part of a ⁠legal settlement between Trump and the justice department to resolve his $10bn lawsuit against the IRS over allegedly mishandling ​his tax records.

Trump wrote that the fund “will not benefit me, but rather the great American Patriots who were hunted down like dogs and whose lives were unfairly and illegally destroyed”.

Tillis has said those who attacked law enforcement during the 6 January 2021 riots should still be in prison and should not get a check from the federal government.

Cornyn and Tillis also object to ​an IRS deal that would prevent tax audits of Trump and his associates.

Tillis responded on Saturday, saying that despite Trump’s comments that the fund is dead, the president “clearly intends to resurrect the payout pot for punks either by inappropriately establishing another bogus fund or pushing Congress to vote for a bill that the majority of Republicans in the Senate would be against”.

“It’s unfortunate that Todd Blanche, who I consider qualified for the job, will not be confirmed because of this reversal,” he said on X. “Hopefully, we can resolve this by Tuesday.”

The back-and-forth over Blanche’s nomination, which is vigorously opposed by victims of Jeffrey Epstein over his handling of investigative files related to the late sex trafficker, now likely lies with backroom negotiations over the weekend. The same controversy dogged Trump’s original second-term attorney general, Pam Bondi, before she resigned.

Cornyn and Tillis were reported to be close to backing Blanche as recently as Thursday. But with just more than two years left in Trump’s second term, Blanche may not need formal Senate confirmation to serve so long as his nomination is pending and not formally rejected or withdrawn.

– X-Canuck checks in: I just returned from vacation in London, then Paris and thought I would give your readers some tips and info if they ever plan on going over there. London was great, they speak the language, you can watch TV, have a variety of different foods, tons of great sights to see, wheeling around in my wheelchair was easy-peasy with the black cabs. What was interesting is that after work, pretty much everyone goes down to the pub and drinks beers for a couple of hours before heading home. Also interesting is they still have remote work on Fridays as a carryover from COVID, so the pubs are pretty much empty because no one comes into the city!

* afternoon tea at the Wolseley with the missus, that was a hit! She absolutely loved it

* British museum incredible, Natural History museum great

* pubs serve great food - shepherds pie, fish and chips, Sunday roast all pretty tasty

The drawback was the crowds. Joe, it was packed almost everywhere you went. Hoards of tour buses from foreign lands, kids on school trips, people everywhere! I recommend avoiding the month of June and pick another time to go.

Took the bullet train down to Paris, which was a wonderful experience (that thing rolls at speeds of up to 180 mph!) Discounted tickets, fees, abound if you are in a wheelchair! Paris is a beautiful city although not as easy to get around and the people are not as nice. Downright rude when driving, scooters and bikes weaving in and out, people opening their windows and yelling all the time.

* The Arc de Triomphe is larger than expected

* Lots of shopping and sprung for a LV for the missus

* The food was pretty standard at every cafe and after a while got old. I ended up at Benihana Paris one night to get some variety.

Again, the crowds were insane! Just not fun no matter where you went. We were there with the heat dome and it was 107 in Paris and, according to my buddies back home, it was 108 in Phoenix. They are all green there so there is very little air conditioning, no paper plates, no plastic cutlery, no plastic bags . . . even the fries at McDonald's came in a hard plastic container that you returned to be washed and reused. The Filet-O-Fish with yellow curry was amazing by the way. Interesting that the Mayor of Paris came out condemning the US for all of its greenhouse gases and why they don't have any air conditioning, but not a peep was mentioned about China or India. Oh, and over 6,000 people died during the heat dome. Guess being green is better than people's lives.

This leads me to my final point . . . the influencers were EVERYWHERE! Joe, they are horrible. As the missus and I are waiting for our chance to see the Mona Lisa, there was a crowd waiting to move up to the roped off area to get a closer look. There was a young couple that were clearly influencers from a foreign land that HAD THEIR BACKS TO THE MONA LISA, had the camera up high and were posing for repeated pics with pursed lips, peace signs, turn the other cheek, smile, tongues out, I could go on and on. Talk about being unaware. When they finally had all their snaps, they pushed through the crowd to go find the next place to generate likes. No appreciation that they were standing in front of one of the most priceless paintings in history.

Since OutKick is always on the cutting edge of cultural changes, here is the next one that is going to hit. People are going to start banning influencers everywhere. There is a restaurant in Nantucket I just read about that has banned all influencers. Fox had an article about a bakery owner here in Phoenix that went viral when an influencer tried to scam him by leaving bad reviews if he didn't pay up. He turned the tables on her good. See it here:

BAKERY OWNER WHO WENT VIRAL WITH RESPONSE TO CRITICAL INFLUENCER SPEAKS OUT ON WHY SHE DEFENDED HER BUSINESS

So, you are going to start seeing more and more of this and I can't wait. We all need to rally around this effort. It continues to amaze me the continually stupid things people will do for the likes and hearts . . . where is the sanity in this world.

You guys get me. The Bee gets me. The travel ball loyalists will say its their way to spend time with their kids. Meanwhile, my kids played rec ball and I just spent a week swimming with them in waterfalls, watched them paddle board through a Pure Michigan sunset, got to pick Petoskey stones with them and watch the Golden Girls with them.

And we didn't step foot in a Hampton Inn the entire time.

My time is up this morning. We'll get cranking for real on Monday as we enter the first week of the football season. Yes, the Hall of Fame game is next week. It's here. The grind all the way to the Super Bowl begins now.

Go have a great weekend. Respect Summer® and let's get down to football business on Monday.
