Jesse Watters hosts Chris Fischer, founder of OCEARCH, to discuss the early surge in shark attacks this summer.

Americans heading to the Bahamas are being reminded to exercise increased caution after the U.S. State Department renewed its travel advisory for the island nation.

The Bahamas remains under a Level 2: "Exercise Increased Caution" advisory, the State Department's second-lowest of four travel advisory levels.

The advisory, renewed this week, cited violent crime, burglaries, sexual assaults and armed robberies — reminding Americans that they can occur "anywhere in The Bahamas."

TRAVEL WARNING ESCALATES FOR POPULAR GETAWAY AS DANGERS AND SECURITY THREATS MOUNT

"Most crime occurs in Nassau and Freeport on New Providence and Grand Bahama islands," the State Department said.

"Stay alert in the 'Over the Hill"'area in Nassau, south of Shirley Street, where gangs have killed residents."

Officials recommend that visitors never swim alone and remain aware of nearby watercraft while enjoying the beaches in the Bahamas.  (iStock)

The State Department also urged travelers to remain alert when staying at vacation rental properties, particularly those without private security.

VACATION HOT SPOT FACES NEW CDC TRAVEL WARNING AS OUTBREAK CASES CONTINUE CLIMBING

Officials also warned that boating in the Bahamas is not well regulated, noting that accidents have resulted in injuries and deaths.

"Due to safety risks, U.S. government employees are not allowed to use or rent jet skis and personal watercraft from independent operators on New Providence and Paradise Islands," the advisory read.

"Lock doors and windows and use other security features, especially on balcony doors."

"Watercraft may not be safe, and some operators are not licensed or insured."

AMERICANS WARNED POPULAR TRAVEL ROUTES THIS SUMMER COULD CARRY CRIME AND KIDNAPPING RISKS

Officials are also urging visitors to stay alert on shore, citing reports of sexual assaults on and near downtown Nassau beaches.

"Never swim alone and beware of jet skis or other watercraft operating close to shore," the alert added.

The State Department renewed its Level 2 travel advisory for the Bahamas, reminding Americans to exercise increased caution while visiting the island nation. (iStock)

"Stay alert for sharks. Shark attacks have led to serious injury and death."

The advisory also offers several personal safety recommendations for travelers, stating, "Do not answer your door at your hotel or residence unless you know who it is."

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

"Lock doors and windows and use other security features, especially on balcony doors," the warning added.

"Do not physically resist any robbery attempt."

The updated advisory reminds travelers to use caution on and around the water because boating accidents have resulted in injuries and deaths. (iStock)

Fox News Digital reached out to the State Department for further details.

The renewed advisory comes as U.S. officials continue to warn travelers about crime at other tropical island destinations.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Earlier this summer, the State Department renewed its Level 2 "Exercise Increased Caution" travel advisory for Turks and Caicos, due to reports of assaults, petty crime and scams targeting tourists.

Americans planning trips to the Bahamas are encouraged to review the latest State Department guidance before traveling. (iStock)

Recently, U.S. officials elevated Saint Lucia's travel advisory to Level 2, citing concerns about violent crime on the Caribbean island.

Andrea Margolis is a lifestyle reporter for Fox News Digital and Fox Business. Readers can follow her on X at @andreamargs or send story tips to andrea.margolis@fox.com.

title: UK petrol price hits Iran war high, adding to pressure on households
excerpt:
Average pump price reaches 160p a litre, while diesel is up 14.5p to 179p and forecast to go to 185p soon

The price of petrol has hit a new Iran War high at UK forecourts, adding to the financial pre...
body_text:
Average pump price reaches 160p a litre, while diesel is up 14.5p to 179p and forecast to go to 185p soon

The price of petrol has hit a new Iran War high at UK forecourts, adding to the financial pressure on millions of households about to embark on their annual holiday.

The RAC said that in “very unwelcome news for drivers” the average pump price had reached 160p a litre, reversing the drop down to 151p in early July that followed the announcement of a fragile Middle East ceasefire.

That is the highest level since November 2022, when prices were soaring in the aftermath of Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

Diesel is up 14.5p to 179p but the price remains below the high of 192p seen back in April, the motoring body said.

“This means the cost of filling a family-size car with unleaded has gone up to £88, while a tank of diesel is £10 more,” said the RAC’s head of policy, Simon Williams. “The wholesale price of petrol eased very slightly this week but is not enough to make a difference at the pumps.”

Williams added that diesel “looks set to keep on rising” and would probably reach 185p a litre in the next few weeks, barring any major oil price reduction.

Fuel prices had declined after the US reached a memorandum of understanding in mid-June with Iran that appeared to be a precursor to peace talks. However, Donald Trump has in recent weeks appeared to tire of the peace efforts, and the US has struck Iran several times in recent days, prompting retaliation against US allies in the Middle East.

On Friday the Brent crude benchmark rose more than 1% to above $90 a barrel as Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said they had struck two tankers trying to pass through the strait of Hormuz under a US “air escort” and turned four other ships around.

The reversal in forecourt fortunes had come “at a very bad time” said Luke Bosdet, the AA spokesperson on pump prices. “AA polling indicates that 20.5 million UK drivers will take to the road in the third week of the holiday season. Among them, 2.2 million will cover 100 to 200 miles, 1.5 million will travel 200 to 300 miles and 1.3 million will go even further.”

However, Bosdet said that fuel prices appeared to be following wholesale prices more closely since May, when the government introduced a new fuel finder scheme that forces all petrol stations to report prices publicly.

In the past fuel retailers have faced accusations of “rocket and feather” pricing – when rapid price increases are followed by slower price cuts.

“In early May when wholesale costs shot up 3p to 6p for more than a fortnight, average petrol prices put on less than 2p,” Bosdet said. “Fuel Finder compliance started to be enforced at the beginning of the month and that likely had an impact.

“When costs plummeted from late May onwards, pump prices followed rapidly, which was unlike previous years of ‘rocket and feather’ pump pricing.”

title: Inside Barcelona’s most sweltering neighbourhood: El Raval
excerpt:
Barcelona, Spain – The sky glows with the pink, orange and blue hues that commonly appear when the sun slips below the horizon – but the heat and humidity remain suffocating.

A group of Pakistani wom...
body_text:
Barcelona, Spain – The sky glows with the pink, orange and blue hues that commonly appear when the sun slips below the horizon – but the heat and humidity remain suffocating.

A group of Pakistani women take refuge from the scorching heat at the water’s edge on Barcelona’s beach in colourful, breezy cotton clothing, some letting the water wash over them as they lie on the wet sand. Others are dancing in the shallows to music from home blasting from a speaker, or cooling off under showers on the beach.

The Spanish city broke its heat record on July 8 , with temperatures reaching 40.7C (105F) during the European heatwave and the wider Barcelona province has recorded an estimated 205 heat-related deaths since the start of the month.

A study last year published by Nature Medicine projected that, in a worst-case scenario, the city could see more than 246,000 heat-attributable deaths between 2015 and 2099 – more than any other European city, mostly because of its Mediterranean location and urban density. Then there is the heat-island effect, in which densely built-up areas, pollution, asphalt and a lack of green spaces trap heat and drive temperatures up.

But within Barcelona itself, the risk of dying from the high temperatures is not evenly shared. El Raval, in the city’s old town, ranks as the most “heat-vulnerable” neighbourhood, especially at night, according to the Climate Vulnerability Index (IVAC), a tool created in 2022 to map which areas would be hit hardest

In the years before it was developed, “there were an increasing number of heatwave episodes”, Elena Domene, the index’s coordinator and coauthor told Al Jazeera – hence the need to find out “where people would suffer most”.

In Barcelona, a heatwave is defined as three or more consecutive days with maximum temperatures above 33.1C (91.6F).

But El Raval is especially vulnerable to several risk factors: it is among the city’s 15 most densely populated neighbourhoods, it has Barcelona’s second-lowest median annual income at 15,050 euros, according to the Spanish National Statistics Institute, and is one of the neighbourhoods with the least green space, according to the Public Health Agency of Catalonia. Indoors, there is little relief. A map designed by the Architecture, Energy and Environment Research Group at the Polytechnic University of Catalonia (UPC), shows that a high percentage of homes lack thermal insulation and cross-ventilation, trapping heat and creating an increasingly suffocating environment as temperatures soar.

The neighbourhood is also one of the migrant hearts of the city. With 67 percent of its residents born abroad – mainly Pakistan, the Philippines and India – it is home to the second-highest share of foreign-born residents, according to city council data.

Tucked down one of El Raval’s narrow streets, the Cultural, Educational and Social Association of Pakistani Women (ACESOP) offers some refuge from the heat. With fans whirring in the society’s hall, migrant women share a meal and support one another here each Friday.

ACESOP’s founder, Huma Jamshed Bashir, tells Al Jazeera that during hot afternoons and nights, many people in the community walk 20 minutes outside of the neighbourhood to find some respite in an air-conditioned shopping centre, or to the beach to escape their suffocating, overcrowded flats.

They usually stay until sleep overcomes them, she says. Those who struggle to walk that far sit instead along the Rambla del Raval, one of the few tree-lined spaces in the neighbourhood.

The lack of relief from the heat at night is measurable. By July 20 , Barcelona had already recorded 25 tropical nights – lows of 20-24.9C (68-77F) – and 25 “torridas” (translating to “torrid” in English, or “extremely hot”) nights with lows of 25-29.9C (77-86C), already catching up to the 36 nights of extreme heat that the city experienced during the whole of 2025.

Reena Mazhar who visits the organisation some Fridays arrived in Barcelona from her native Lahore in Pakistan six months ago. Neither she nor her husband have found work yet. The couple share one room in a flat in El Raval, with four other people living in the next room. They don’t even have a fan.

“All I can do is keep wetting myself down, taking showers, or leaving the house in search of somewhere I can breathe,” the 40-year-old tells Al Jazeera, as she sits on a sofa in ACESOP’s living room. The other women remain at the table, chatting after lunch, sheltering from the heat outside.

Close to ACESOP, in a square with less than half its area shaded by trees, Adam Halui, a 16-year-old local, tilts his head back to stop a nosebleed – a condition triggered whenever the temperature spikes, he says. He washes his face in a public fountain in front of the Josep Trueta municipal centre for elderly people, an air-conditioned “climate shelter”.

Barcelona operates around 500 similar shelters – 15 in El Raval – including libraries, museums and parks. They are open to all who need them, however, they have limitations.

Blanca Arellano Ramos, an architect specialising in urbanism and a professor at UPC, co-authored a 2023 study on the effectiveness of the shelters for over-65s, one of the most vulnerable groups to high temperatures. Her findings show that at night, only 15 percent of the elderly population has access to one of the centres within a 10-minute walk, since many close after dark. Other centres, such as schoolyards designated as shelters, are closed during the summer months.

Furthermore, Arellano Ramos says, “quality matters – not just anything can be a shelter,” referring to the limited opening hours. “There has to be a place to sit, where you can drink water, or wash up,” she adds.

Inside the municipal senior centre, Margarita Medina, 70, is sitting at one of the tables. The lifelong Raval resident lives alone and suffers from fibromyalgia – a chronic condition causing widespread body pain and persistent fatigue. She has air conditioning at home but can’t use it because it irritates her condition.

“I don’t have enough oxygen in my lungs, so I really do suffer in the heat,” she said, as she collects her walker at the door of the senior centre.

A recent study by the Barcelona Urban Research Institute (IDRA) emphasises the risk elderly people like Medina are facing. According to its findings, older, low-income women living alone in poorly insulated housing are at the highest risk of death during heatwaves.

Ramos tells Al Jazeera that urban design needs to start focusing on the “renaturalisation of the city” by introducing more green spaces, although that would require significant water supply and enough space for trees to grow. While water is not scarce for now, it was restricted to essential uses only during the 2023 drought.

Barcelona City Council is aiming to introduce warm-climate trees and ultimately wants them to make up 36 percent of trees in the Ciutat Vella district, where El Raval is located, as part of its climate adaptation plans.

However, Pere de Mas, the council’s urban trees coordinator, says that besides the economic and logistical obstacles, erratic winter cold snaps make it hard for such species to thrive and European nurseries remain heavily specialised in cold-climate trees.

“There are few producers of warm-climate trees,” de Mas told Al Jazeera.

Within the sweltering neighbourhood, an oasis that offers relief is facing the threat of closure.

A purely voluntary, self-managed community “green area”, it is a sheltered area built and maintained by the residents themselves.

In 2014, dozens of citizens occupied an apparently abandoned corner plot – previously an overgrown patch of wasteland – near where police had killed a man and established a community space named after him: Agora Juan Andres Benitez.

Six officers from the Mossos d’Esquadra, Catalonia’s regional police force, were convicted of manslaughter and sentenced to two years in prison for restraining Benitez. The 50-year-old was detained following a street fight, according to Spanish media. Police were found to have used disproportionate force against him for 12 minutes, which resulted in his death hours later in hospital.

The area has since become a “free space” with lush plants to cool the environment, purify the air and nurture biodiversity. But there has been pushback from the authorities and, now, a court has set an eviction date for 8 October.

“This is a community space that fosters social cohesion. We are in need of these kinds of spaces in the neighbourhood,” says Margarita Hernandez, an El Raval resident and member of the Agora – a term that refers to a meeting point, a discussion forum.

It isn’t just a free space to take refuge from the heat. Some 16,000 free or low-cost meals are served here annually,   It also functions as an informal community-led care network where local families share caregiving responsibilities. It also hosts school visits, runs free educational workshops, provides health information and, ultimately, functions as a safe haven for El Raval’s most marginalised residents, including undocumented migrants, homeless people, sex workers and low-income families.

Users of the space fear there will soon be nowhere to escape the heat at all.

Isa Fernandez is sitting at a table under the lush greenery of the community space and worries about its loss.

“They don’t understand why we insist the Agora has to continue. They don’t realise what it means, how it affects the whole neighbourhood,” Fernandez says. “It’s become a place of welcome for a lot of people. It’s nice to come here – not like sitting on a bench in the street in the heat.”

Additional reporting by Diego Arredondo and Serena Lordache. Reporting for this article was supported by a 2025 Montserrat Roig Journalism Research Grant.

title: Cocky Curt Cignetti called out the SEC, but he should Google Indiana's laughable schedule first
excerpt:
Joel Klatt reacted to Indiana and Curt Cignetti winning the National Championship in Cignetti's second season as head coach.

The cocky Curt Cignetti train rolled on through Big Ten Media Days this we...
body_text:
Joel Klatt reacted to Indiana and Curt Cignetti winning the National Championship in Cignetti's second season as head coach.

The cocky Curt Cignetti train rolled on through Big Ten Media Days this week, and it doesn't seem like it's slowing down any time soon.

Nor should it, by the way. Indiana is the defending national champs. Cignetti has earned the right to be cocky. He's earned the right to pick fights with the SEC, and any other conference he chooses.

BUT, it will come to a halt at some point, and fans of a certain conference are already foaming at the mouth.

For those who missed it, Cignetti took a nasty little shot at the SEC on Thursday, calling out some unnamed teams — unofficially, of course — for making excuses.

INDIANA'S CURT CIGNETTI ROASTS THE SEC AS ESPN STARTS THEIR PROMOTIONAL CAMPAIGN ALREADY: 'WE DON'T WHINE'

Indiana Hoosiers head coach Curt Cignetti looks on before the 2025 Big Ten Championship Game against the Ohio State Buckeyes at Lucas Oil Stadium on Dec. 6, 2025. (Robert Goddin/Imagn Images)

"I mean we don’t run a hype machine up here in the Midwest," Cignetti said. "We believe everything’s earned, not given. And when we fall short, we say, ‘We fell short.’ We don’t cry a river, whine and complain. All right? And that’s why we’re the best."

Lordy. Just a vicious shot at the SEC. Again, Cignetti has earned the right to make it. The Hoosiers were dominant last year. But ...

Let's not get crazy. All these things tend to come out in the wash, and Indiana's schedule this upcoming season ain't exactly murderer's row.

SEC fans, of course, were QUICK to point that out yesterday:

I could go on and on. It's a war zone over on Elon's app formerly known as Twitter. Just a war zone. Which is great, because that means college football is almost back.

Less than 30 days, folks. Hang tight for just a bit longer!

Look, I'm an SEC guy. I'm biased. I'll happily admit that. OutKick's Ian Miller is not an SEC guy. He hates us. I get it.

Indiana head coach Curt Cignetti speaks during media day ahead of the College Football Playoff national championship game between the Miami Hurricanes and Indiana. The game will be played Monday, Jan. 19, 2026, in Miami, Florida, on Jan. 17, 2026. (AP Photo/Chris Carlson)

I'm also a Florida Gators fan, and I'm man enough to admit the Hoosiers would probably crush us. They crushed just about everyone they faced last year, so it's safe to assume they'd do the same to us.

Now, they had a bunch of 30-year-old players on their team, but that's neither here nor there.

But, let's not act like Indiana is about to face the toughest schedule in the world. I mean, just look at that thing! It's hilariously bad.

That's a pathetic first six weeks. Come on. Let's be fair here. In that same span, LSU plays Clemson, Texas A&M and Ole Miss.

Texas plays Ohio State (!!!), Tennessee and Oklahoma.

Oklahoma plays Michigan, Georgia and Texas.

Texas Longhorns head coach Steve Sarkisian walks into Camping World Stadium ahead of the Citrus Bowl against the Michigan Wolverines in Orlando, Fla., on Dec. 31, 2025. (aAustin American-Statesman via Getty Images)

Do we see the difference? Again, Cignetti can say what he wants and be as cocky as his heart desires. He's earned it. Indiana has earned it.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

But calling out the SEC for whining and complaining, while also knowing you have six straight bye weeks to open the season, is a ballsy move.

title: KARR Bluetooth flaw exposes 2.2M cars to theft risk
excerpt:
Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

Could a small device hidden beneath your dashboard make your car easier to break into? Nancy from Newtown, Pennsylvani...
body_text:
Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

Could a small device hidden beneath your dashboard make your car easier to break into? Nancy from Newtown, Pennsylvania, asked me where she should look for the KARR or SWDS "code" in her 2025 Cadillac XT5 and 2024 Hyundai Tucson Limited Hybrid.

Here is the first thing you need to know. There is no code to find in your vehicle's settings. KARR and SWDS refer to aftermarket security hardware that a dealership may have installed before selling the car. SWDS stands for Southwest Dealer Services, the company associated with several KARR-branded vehicle protection products.

The device usually sits beneath the dashboard on the driver's side. You may also find a KARR or SWDS sticker on the driver-side window.

So, before you start searching through menus or calling the automaker, here is how to find out whether your vehicle has one of these devices and what to do next.

15 SECURITY ESSENTIALS TO KEEP YOUR VALUABLES SAFE FOR SUMMER TRAVEL

A Bluetooth flaw in dealer-installed KARR and SWDS security devices could expose about 2.2 million vehicles to unauthorized access. (David Baillot/University of California San Diego/Jacobs School of Engineering)

CyberGuy Live: Missed "Sick of Spam?" Get the replay and checklist

Our free CyberGuy Live class "Sick of Spam?" has ended, but you can still watch the full replay and download our spam-stopping checklist. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you step by step through simple ways to reduce robocalls, spam texts, junk email and unwanted messages. You’ll also learn how to curb political texts, clean up your inbox and spot messages that could put your personal information at risk.

Get the free replay and checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.

Computer security researchers at the University of California San Diego uncovered a Bluetooth vulnerability affecting at least 2.2 million vehicles. The flaw involves dealer-installed KARR and SWDS security devices. A person standing within about five yards of a vulnerable vehicle could connect to the device through Bluetooth.

From there, an attacker could lock or unlock the doors. The same flaw could silence the alarm, sound the horn or flash the headlights. An attacker could also prevent a parked vehicle from starting. However, the researchers did not report that the flaw could start the engine or shut down a vehicle that was already running. That distinction is important. The Bluetooth flaw alone does not let someone drive away. However, it could quietly unlock the doors. A thief could then use separate tools to create or program a key.

KARR systems are aftermarket vehicle security products sold through participating dealerships. They may include an alarm, GPS tracking, remote vehicle controls or an ignition-disabling feature. Southwest Dealer Services uses several product names, including KARR Security, KARR Fusion, KARR BT, KARR S.W.A.T. and S.W.A.T. Dealer. The features vary by product and vehicle.

These devices do not come from Cadillac, Hyundai, Ford or another automaker's factory. A dealership or one of its vendors adds the hardware after the vehicle arrives. Dealers may use the system to protect inventory sitting on the lot. When someone buys the vehicle, the dealer may offer the system as an additional security package. The problem is that some dealers left the hardware connected even when buyers declined the service. As a result, a driver might have a vulnerable device without an active KARR account or any idea that the equipment is inside the car.

The KARR device communicates with a smartphone app through Bluetooth Low Energy. Researchers found that the affected devices relied on the same secret authentication key. Once they recovered that key, they could send commands that vulnerable KARR devices accepted.

Think of it as giving a huge group of devices the same unchangeable password. Once that password becomes known, each device becomes easier to approach. The researchers also found that the devices broadcast recognizable Bluetooth signals. Historical databases containing those signals could reveal where a particular device had appeared. That creates a privacy concern beyond car theft. Someone could potentially use the data to study where a vehicle regularly parks or travels.

UC San Diego researchers found the devices most often in vehicles sold through Honda, Toyota, Mazda, Ford and Jeep dealerships in Southern California since 2017. However, that list does not mean other brands are safe.

KARR works with more than 3,000 dealerships nationwide. Vehicles also move around the country through used-car sales, auctions and dealership trades. Therefore, the vehicle's make and model cannot confirm whether it has the equipment. The dealership that prepared the vehicle for sale matters more than the badge on the grille. A Cadillac, Hyundai or Chevrolet could have a KARR system if the selling dealer installed one. A Honda from another dealership might never have received it.

Start with the easy clues before you remove any trim or crawl too far beneath the dashboard.

Look at the lower corners and edges of the driver-side window.

A sticker strongly suggests that the dealership installed a related device. However, the absence of a sticker cannot completely clear your vehicle. A dealer or previous owner may have removed the label while leaving the hardware connected. UC San Diego says many affected vehicles have the sticker, rather than every affected vehicle.

Park the vehicle and shut off the engine. Move the driver's seat back and use a flashlight to look beneath the lower dashboard. Researchers say the device is usually installed underneath the dashboard on the driver's side.

You may see a small button or indicator light attached to the bottom edge of the dash. Wiring may run from the button behind the dashboard panels. The button shown by UC San Diego is small and easy to miss. It can look like a basic aftermarket alarm switch rather than a modern connected device. Do not pull on the wires or disconnect anything. The module may connect to the ignition system and other vehicle electronics.

Check the purchase agreement, dealer addendum, finance documents and service records.

The charge may appear as part of a larger dealer protection package. You may also find the product listed with no separate price if the dealer installed it for inventory control.

TESLA HELPED SAVE A DRIVER; IS YOUR CAR READY?

Some Jeep, Ram and Chrysler drivers previously saw promotional messages on infotainment screens through Stellantis’ Uconnect system. (Kurt "Cyberguy" Knutsson)

Call the dealership that originally sold the vehicle. This step can help even when you bought the car used from another business. Your VIN appears near the bottom of the windshield on the driver's side. You can also find it on the registration, insurance card and driver-side door frame.

Ask the dealer: "Can you check this VIN and confirm whether your dealership or inventory vendor installed a KARR, SWDS, KARR BT, S.W.A.T. or other aftermarket security module?"

Then ask these follow-up questions: "Is the device still connected?" "Has it received the firmware update released on July 20, 2026?" "Can you provide the device model and firmware status in writing?"

A vague answer such as "Your factory alarm is fine" does not address the question. You are asking about dealer-installed aftermarket equipment.

KARR says people who never activated the security service can still use the official KARR Security app to check their VIN. Download the app only through the official Apple App Store, Google Play Store or KARR website. Do not use an app link from an unexpected text message, email or online advertisement.

After opening the app near the vehicle, tap the customer service link at the bottom of the screen. The app should guide you through the VIN check and available firmware update. KARR also lists customer support at 800-395-5277.

Nancy's 2025 Cadillac XT5 and 2024 Hyundai Tucson Limited Hybrid were not among the specific brands UC San Diego researchers said appeared most often. However, that does not rule them out. The device comes from the dealership rather than Cadillac or Hyundai.

Nancy should check each SUV separately. First, she should look for a KARR or SWDS sticker on the driver-side window. Next, she should use a flashlight to inspect the lower edge of the dashboard near the driver's knees.

She should also review the paperwork from each dealership. If the vehicles came from different dealers, one could have the equipment while the other does not. Finally, Nancy should call both selling dealers with the VINs. She should ask whether either dealership installed a KARR, SWDS or S.W.A.T. module before delivery. If the dealers cannot provide a definite answer, she can use the official KARR app or call KARR support.

Acrisure released a firmware patch on July 20, 2026, one day before UC San Diego publicly announced the vulnerability. The vehicle owner must deliver the update to the KARR device through the official KARR Security app. Updating your phone or vehicle infotainment system will not patch the separate module.

An activated system means you purchased or activated KARR service through the dealership.

KARR says no additional action is necessary after the app confirms that the latest firmware is installed.

You can still check and update a device that remained in the vehicle after you declined the service.

Call KARR support when the app cannot find the vehicle or complete the update.

WAYMO RECALLS ROBOTAXIS OVER CONSTRUCTION-ZONE RISK

Drivers can check for a KARR or SWDS device by inspecting the driver-side window, dashboard area and vehicle sales paperwork. (David Baillot/University of California San Diego/Jacobs School of Engineering)

You can ask to have the system deactivated or removed. However, I would not turn this into a weekend do-it-yourself project. Researchers warn that removal may require opening the dashboard, cutting wires and restoring connections involving the ignition system or vehicle computers. Disconnecting the wrong wire could stop the car from starting. It might also affect the factory alarm, remote start or another electrical feature. Southwest Dealer Services says an owner can request removal, transfer or deactivation by calling 800-395-5277 and confirming the account information.

Ask the original dealership or a qualified automotive electrical technician to handle the work. Before approving removal, ask the technician how the factory wiring will be restored. Afterward, request written confirmation that the module was removed and the vehicle's original security functions still work.

We reached out to KARR Security, and a representative from the company provided CyberGuy with the following statement:

"KARR Security maintains rigorous standards to help protect customers’ vehicles. Researchers at UC San Diego identified a vulnerability affecting BLE-based auto theft devices, including a small percentage of KARR devices with certain Bluetooth-related components. The vulnerability described in the research is highly complex and presents a low risk to customers under real-world conditions. Nevertheless, we responded promptly and developed a firmware update to address the issue. We launched this app/firmware update on July 20, 2026. Active customers may apply the update directly from their phone after securely logging in to the KARR Security app. Vehicle owners of non-active systems can still update via the app using their VIN (last 8 digits) as a validation step. Consumers can find detailed instructions and tutorials for assistance with this firmware on the Customer FAQ section of our website at www.KARRSecurity.com."

KARR Security added, "To our knowledge, we have not seen this vulnerability used in the real world to break into or steal a vehicle."

Turning off Bluetooth on your phone will not disable the Bluetooth radio inside the KARR module. Deleting the app will not remove the device. Removing the vehicle from your phone's normal Bluetooth menu will not patch it either.

The KARR module communicates separately from the Cadillac, Hyundai or other factory infotainment system. A Faraday pouch also will not fix this particular problem. Faraday pouches can help block relay attacks involving a key fob. They cannot update or disable hardware installed beneath the dashboard. You need to update the KARR device itself or have a professional remove it.

Car thieves use different methods, so protecting your vehicle requires more than one piece of technology.

When your vehicle has a KARR or SWDS device, install the firmware update as soon as possible. This directly addresses the Bluetooth flaw identified by the researchers. A steering wheel lock or tracker can add protection, but neither one repairs vulnerable software.

Signal jammers can sometimes block the command sent by a key fob. After pressing the lock button, listen for the normal confirmation sound. Look for the lights and pull a door handle before walking away. Also, close every window and take the keys with you. NHTSA recommends checking the doors whenever you leave a parked vehicle.

A steering wheel lock creates an obvious barrier inside the car. It will not stop every determined thief. However, it adds time and makes the vehicle harder to steer. NHTSA includes steering wheel locks among visible devices that can discourage vehicle theft. You can find more ideas in my CyberGuy guide on how to help prevent your car from getting stolen.

Store key fobs away from exterior doors, windows and attached garages. A tested signal-blocking pouch can help reduce the risk of a relay attack. In that type of theft, criminals extend the signal from a key inside the house to a vehicle outside. Test the pouch regularly. Put the key inside, close the pouch and stand next to the car. The doors should remain locked when you touch the handle. Remember that a key-fob pouch protects against a different attack. It will not patch a KARR module.

A hidden GPS tracker or Bluetooth tracker may help locate a stolen vehicle. However, do not confront anyone or attempt to recover the car yourself. Give tracking information to law enforcement. An Apple AirTag can provide a backup location signal, although Apple's anti-stalking alerts may eventually warn a thief that an unknown AirTag is traveling with the vehicle. Read my CyberGuy guide on using an AirTag in a vehicle and understanding its limits.

Use a locked garage when one is available. Otherwise, park in a visible area with lighting, foot traffic or a security camera. Avoid isolated corners where someone can work around the vehicle without attracting attention. NHTSA also recommends parking in well-lit areas whenever possible.

A thief may break into a car without planning to steal the entire vehicle. Take phones, laptops, wallets and bags with you. Do not leave a spare key or garage remote inside the car. NHTSA warns that thieves commonly target electronics and other items they can quickly resell.

Nancy's question highlights the biggest problem with this vulnerability. Many drivers have no idea that a KARR or SWDS device may be hiding in their vehicle. You will not find a KARR code inside your vehicle's settings. Look for a sticker on the driver-side window and a small aftermarket button below the dashboard. Then check your paperwork and ask the selling dealer to search your VIN. The flaw can unlock a vulnerable vehicle and interfere with its security features from nearby. It cannot start the engine by itself or shut down a moving car. Still, unlocking the doors may give a thief the access needed to try another method. Fortunately, KARR has released a firmware update. Install it through the official KARR Security app. When you no longer want the system, arrange professional removal rather than pulling wires yourself.

Should dealerships have to tell you about every connected device installed in your car, even when you decline to purchase the service? Let us know by writing to us at CyberGuy.com.

title: Hull funeral director who left bodies to rot in mortuary jailed for 20 years
excerpt:
More than 80 loved ones spoke of horrors of learning about Robert Bush’s crimes, including mother of a miscarried baby

A funeral director has been jailed for 20 years for leaving dozens of bodies – i...
body_text:
More than 80 loved ones spoke of horrors of learning about Robert Bush’s crimes, including mother of a miscarried baby

A funeral director has been jailed for 20 years for leaving dozens of bodies – including a miscarried baby – “rotting” in his mortuary and giving bereaved families the wrong ashes.

Robert Bush, the owner of Legacy Independent Funeral Services in Hull, pleaded guilty to 67 offences spanning 12 years and affecting hundreds of families, including 30 counts of preventing a lawful and decent burial.

Over a five-day sentencing hearing at Hull crown court, more than 80 victims recounted their horror at learning their loved ones had been left “rotting away” inside his funeral parlour. Many broke down sobbing during their statements.

Sentencing Bush, the judge, Mr Justice Hilliard, said: “The defendant was so preoccupied with his own enrichment that he behaved in a shocking and disgraceful way towards the deceased.
 “The awful truth is that anyone whose loved one went through Legacy at any time when it was operating can now have no confidence as to how they were treated or whose ashes they have. Unless of course, they were one of the 30 bodies recovered in March 2024.
 “Culpability is of course high because of the gross breach of trust in respect of people who were vulnerable as they were bereaved.”

Bush, 48, from Otley, West Yorkshire, showed little visible emotion while listening to the statements in the dock, but hung his head lower and lower as the week went on.

Gasps and sobbing could be heard from the public gallery when prosecutors revealed the grim condition of the deceased.

Hull crown court heard bodies had been found uncovered and laying on racks in varying states of decomposition. Damp and mould had spread to the coffins and ash boxes, while dried body fluids and faeces had been left on the floor.

During the search, PC Jason Sutcliffe spotted a brown paper bag on the floor. He initially thought the item inside was a baby bird, before noticing two hospital wristbands wrapped around the waist, identifying the body as the “baby of Jasmine Beverley”.

The baby, Sunny Beverley-Conlin, was miscarried at 18 weeks in May 2022. His parents believed he had been given a funeral and cremated. Instead, Bush had left his remains inside Legacy for almost two years.

Sunny’s mother, Jasmine, sobbed as she faced Bush in court. “I trusted Rob with the most precious and important person in my life,” she said. “The reality I now live with is that my baby boy Sunny has spent more time in your possession than he ever did with his own family.”

In a statement, Sutcliffe described finding Sunny’s remains as “the worst experience of my career” and said it would “never leave my thoughts”.

The ashes presented to Beverley and her family had been “consistent with baby remains in volume but had larger pieces of coarse bones” expected from an adult’s body, according to evidence heard in court.

Some of the ashes presented to Lucy Ness, who lost her child just before 12 weeks, were said to have resembled “animal remains” in terms of size and texture, which prompted cries in the courtroom.

The body of 94-year-old Norman Bridger was recovered at the Legacy premises 323 days after his death. “My lovely dad lay in a cardboard coffin for almost 11 months,” said his daughter Karen King “It’s beyond belief. I’ll never know why. It feels like he was just forgotten.”

Bush was arrested on 10 March while returning from a holiday in Arizona, US, a £3,000 trip funded by his funeral fraud. Arrest footage showed Humberside and Met police officers escorting a shocked Bush off a plane at Heathrow airport.

Soon after his arrest, Bush told officers: “I fucked it all up, everything, my whole world.”

Police officers found more than 35 bodies and more than 100 sets of ashes during a search of Legacy premises at Hessle Road in March 2024.

Several families had had the wrong ashes turned into jewellery, and in one instance planned to incorporate some into a tattoo.

David Gorbutt told the court he felt “abused” after learning that Bush had given him a stranger’s ashes rather than those of his late wife, Susan Gorbutt. He had scattered those ashes at the same site as her son’s, as per Susan’s wishes.

“I have had the uncertainty of not knowing who or what I have scattered over the ashes of Susan’s son,” Gorbutt said. “Who was that? One person? More than one?”

The state of Bush’s premises “did not meet industry standards” and represented a “wholly inadequate approach to care for the deceased”, according to evidence from Dr Richard Lloyd, a human anatomy centre manager at the University of Cambridge and Cranfield University. “Bodies were simply abandoned in the Hessle Road mortuary for nature to take its course,” his report stated.

Containers of ashes were “stored in an undignified manner” across the premises, stacked “chaotically on shelves” or left on the floor, where “damp had caused mould to grow on the boxes”. Ash was also found on desk surfaces and, in one room, strewn across the floor. Officers found jewellery that ought to have been returned to families and a large number of photographs that should have been placed inside coffins.

Bush stole money from funeral services intended for 12 separate charities, including Macmillan Cancer Support, Salvation Army and a local hospice. In addition, he sold false funeral plans to 226 people over nearly 12 years, totalling in value to £562,117.

In the time he spent defrauding bereaved families, Bush spent more than £42,000 on holidays, including his trip to Arizona, £21,000 on motorcycle racing and £17,400 on home improvements between 2017 and 2024. He spent more than £9,000 on camping expenses in 2022 – the same year he failed to cremate baby Sunny Beverley-Conlin.

Bush’s barrister, Richard Wright KC, said his client wished to apologise to the families and accepted this was “likely to be rejected” by them. Wright added: “He is treated, completely understandably, as a pariah – hated and despised.”

title: Michigan Senate candidate endorsed by AOC and Bernie Sanders insists he's not a socialist
excerpt: Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed said during an interview that he was "simply not a socialist" when pressed on his association with prominent left-wing leaders such as Bernie Sanders and Rep. ...
body_text:
Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed said during an interview that he was "simply not a socialist" when pressed on his association with prominent left-wing leaders such as Bernie Sanders and Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez.

Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed insisted during an interview on Tuesday that he was "simply not a socialist," when pressed on his close relationship with socialist figures such as Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-VT., or Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y.

"Let me ask you about democratic socialism because you have a new ad with AOC in the ad," MS NOW's Jen Psaki asked. "You've been — you're very close to Bernie Sanders. You've had a number of these very popular officials come out and campaign for you. You've also said that you're not a democratic socialist. You describe yourself as a capitalist who understands capitalism."

"But what is the difference? What are they getting wrong?" she continued. "I think this is confusing to a lot of people. What are they getting wrong about capitalism, or why don't you consider yourself a member of the democratic socialist movement? Given your proximity in your relationship to all of these officials."

"Because I'm simply not a socialist," El-Sayed said. "I believe in science. For me, you got to bring results. I've studied a lot of the solutions that I fight for, things like Medicare for All, things like rethinking the way that our financial system implies that corporate CEOs are more interested in a quarterly bottom line than they are in the long-term sustainability of their business."

SOCIALISM'S WAR ON SUCCESS HAS A NEW CHAMPION — AND HE’S RUNNING FOR SENATE IN MICHIGAN

Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., speaks during a news conference at the U.S. Capitol on May 20, 2026, in Washington, D.C. Abdul El-Sayed, Democratic Senate candidate from Michigan, speaks during a community meetup at Rouge Park in Detroit, Michigan, on July 26, 2026. Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez speaks at TU Berlin on February 15, 2026. (Alex Wong/Getty Images; Sarah Rice/Bloomberg via Getty Images; Annette Riedl/picture alliance via Getty Images)

El-Sayed is running in the Michigan Democratic Senate primary against U.S. Rep. Haley Stevens on August 4. The pair debated on Wednesday night and clashed on several issues.

He said that the U.S. operates in a monopoly or oligopoly when it comes to markets people are "forced" to participate in, adding, "I know that capitalism works, I just know that it does not work when you have monopolies or oligopolies."

"So, at the end of the day, it's just a philosophical difference," he continued. "I'm not an ideologue. I'm a lot more interested in empirical results. So, when it comes to Medicare for All, I think that's the best single way to provide folks healthcare in this country."

"And by the way, public healthcare, the public part would be the insurance," El-Sayed added. "The healthcare itself stays private. When it comes to investing in our schools or investing in good infrastructure, these are the shared resources that we need so that every single person can actually participate in the economy."

DEM CIVIL WAR HITS PRIMARY DEBATE STAGE IN FIERY BATTLEGROUND SHOWDOWN: 'WHAT ARE YOU HIDING?'

Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed poses for a portrait in Grand Rapids, Michigan, on Saturday, Feb. 21, 2026. (Evan Cobb for The Washington Post via Getty Images)

Psaki pressed him again and noted that socialists would say that they believe in science as well, saying, "If you're the nominee, Mike Rogers and the Republicans are going to try to label you as a democratic socialist. You're going to say you're not. But I'm saying, help us understand what's the difference between your version of capitalism and their version of democratic socialism."

El-Sayed then criticized Rogers, the presumptive Republican nominee for the Michigan Senate race.

"We're so concerned about what they're going to say about us that we forget that we also have mouths and can talk about that," El-Sayed said. "Let's talk about Mike Rogers. Mike Rogers is the worst kind of corporatist."

RAHM EMANUEL WARNS DSA AGENDA DOESN'T PLAY WELL OUTSIDE 'UPPER WEST SIDE OF MANHATTAN'

Michigan Democratic candidate for Senate Abdul El-Sayed speaks at The People V. The Powerful rally at the Detroit Opera House on July 18, 2026, in Detroit, Michigan. (Sarah Rice/Getty Images)

Alyssa Brouillet, the communications director for Rogers campaign, told Fox News Digital in a statement, "We all know that if it walks like a duck, and quacks like a duck, it’s a duck. This election is about crazy versus common sense. Mike Rogers will hold the line against the Left’s socialist takeover and ensure common sense prevails this November."

"It’s no surprise that the same guy who lied about being a physician is lying about everything else," the statement continued. "But while Abdul offers lip-service, Mike Rogers delivers results. Just today, Mike Rogers released a plan to fix our broken healthcare system by improving affordability, accessibility, and transparency of healthcare for working families."

"This is only one of the many examples of Mike Rogers cleaning up the mess Democrats — like Abdul — created during their 32-year monopoly over Michigan’s two Senate seats," Brouillet added.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

Rep. Rashida Tlaib, a Democrat from Michigan, during a House Financial Services Committee hearing in Washington, D.C., on March 6, 2024.  (Getty)

El-Sayed has attended Democratic Socialist of America (DSA) events over the years.

Between 2017 and 2020, El-Sayed attended and spoke at six events held by the DSA, including a 2019 fundraiser which he headlined. El-Sayed has distanced himself from the DSA in interviews and has previously outright rejected being labeled as a "socialist."

"I'm not technically or practically DSA," El-Sayed told The Wall Street Journal earlier this month. In an interview with CNN, he similarly stated that "I am not somebody who is a socialist. I believe in capitalism, I just believe that capitalism has to be regulated."

At the 2019 event, which raised $10,000 for the organization, El-Sayed was described by DSA organizers as "a longtime friend of Detroit DSA." He was photographed smiling next to far-left Michigan Rep. Rashida Tlaib, a self-described socialist, behind a table with a poster on it depicting a hand labeled "DSA" choking a snake labeled "capitalism."

El-Sayed’s first recorded appearance at a DSA event was during his run for Michigan governor in 2017. Other DSA events he spoke at focused on Medicare for All and the Green New Deal.

Fox News' Robert Schmad contributed to this report.

Hanna Panreck is an associate editor at Fox News.

title: Top Democrats accuse Republicans of becoming ‘gelatinous blobs’ on Iran war | First Thing
excerpt:
Senators Warren and Van Hollen attack Republican ‘rubber stamps’ in Congress for surrendering authority to Trump. Plus, could AI take your job? Some workers in China already know the answer

Senior De...
body_text:
Senators Warren and Van Hollen attack Republican ‘rubber stamps’ in Congress for surrendering authority to Trump. Plus, could AI take your job? Some workers in China already know the answer

Senior Democrats accused Republicans in the US Congress of becoming “gelatinous blobs” who will not stand up to Donald Trump and “rubber stamps” for his war on Iran.

The Massachusetts senator Elizabeth Warren and the Maryland senator Chris Van Hollen argued that the Republican-controlled Congress had surrendered its constitutional authority to the president.

In interviews with the Guardian, the senators urged their Republican colleagues to stand with Democrats and assert Congress’s authority as a separate branch of the federal government – with power over declaring war.

What else is happening in Washington? Trump has said a deal has been reached for Hamas to disarm and for Israel to withdraw its forces from Gaza. However, briefings from both sides exposed disputes over its implementation that could prove difficult to overcome.

Donald Trump said yesterday he may “temporarily” pull the nomination of Todd Blanche to serve as attorney general, but would keep him in the role in an acting capacity until two Republican senators objecting to his confirmation leave office next year – an extraordinary escalation of an intra-party fight over an agreement to create a $1.8bn slush fund and give the president tax immunity.

Two Republican senators – John Cornyn of Texas and Thom Tillis of North Carolina – have refused to back Blanche’s nomination until they receive written confirmation from the justice department that it is not moving forward with a widely criticized agreement creating a $1.8bn fund to compensate people claiming they were targets of political weaponization and granting the president, his family and business entities broad immunity from past tax investigations.

What has Blanche said? Blanche has already said publicly that the payout fund to compensate victims of so-called government weaponization is not moving forward amid bipartisan backlash. But Cornyn and Tillis had sought assurances in writing, something Blanche has refused to do. Cornyn also sought to clarify the terms of the tax immunity portion of the agreement.

At least 34 people have died trying to reach the Spanish enclave of Ceuta, after about 49,000 migrants breached the border with Morocco and poured into the tiny territory.

Spain sent ​military and police reinforcements to Ceuta on Thursday after people crossed by land and sea. Spain’s prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, was expected to join the interior minister, Fernando Grande-Marlaska, on a visit to Ceuta on Friday.

Rachid Sbihi, who leads a local workers’ association representing civil guard officers, described the situation as a “serious humanitarian crisis”. He said: “People are still entering. The reinforcements that have arrived are only helping the injured and other humanitarian efforts.”

How did the people die? Many drowned but some were killed in a crush to cross the breakwater fence at Tarajal beach, Sbihi said.

Why have so many breached the border at the same time? It was not immediately clear what prompted so many people to cross to Ceuta.

Seattle’s police chief has resigned amid criticism of the city’s response to a fatal shootout at a food festival last weekend, Katie Wilson, the mayor, said last night. The announcement followed hours of speculation about whether Shon Barnes would step down.

Anthropic ⁠said on Thursday its AI Claude model hacked ⁠systems of ⁠three ​organizations during testing, days after its rival OpenAI ⁠revealed a rogue agent had gone on a days-long ⁠hacking spree at another AI ​firm, Hugging ‌Face.

George and Amal Clooney have been forced to evacuate their home in south-eastern France as a wildfire burned nearby, the actor’s agent confirmed to Associated Press on Thursday. In a letter to the local mayor, the actor said that “whatever happens, they remain fully part of this community” and would “contribute to its rebuilding”.

In the new instalment of the Spider-Man franchise, Peter is back where he started, adored by New Yorkers for crime-fighting as Spider-Man, living in a scuzzy single room with all his screens and tech gear, his secret identity a secret once more, but pining for the people he loves. And he’s not getting any younger. How much of a “brand new day” is this?

European countries have agreed to boycott all Fifa competitions if Gianni Infantino pushes forward with his proposals to sell chunks of the World Cup to US-based private investment. In an extraordinary development, all 55 Uefa members resolved not to participate in future World Cups or other Fifa-run events, saying in a statement that they “unanimously and unequivocally reject” the proposals.

In China, the deployment of AI is being encouraged at a scale unseen in the west. Across the country, workers are fearful about the impact of AI on their livelihoods as the technology is rolled out at a staggering rate in an increasingly precarious labour market.

“Are we understanding it yet?,” writes Alexander Hurst for Guardian Opinion “As Europe burns in the west, the south and the north, are we grasping the fact that our economies, food systems, political stability and even our ability to plan for the future, will all be charred in a world on fire? Meanwhile, the White House seems committed to ecocide.”

First Thing is delivered to thousands of inboxes every weekday. If you’re not already signed up, subscribe now.

If you have any questions or comments about any of our newsletters please email newsletters@theguardian.com

title: 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' Review: Tom Holland, Zendaya return for action-packed, emotional sequel
excerpt:
The trailer for Sony Pictures and Marvel Studios' "Spider-Man: Brand New Day" starring Tom Holland, Zendeya, Jacob Batalon, Sadie Fink, Jon Bernthal and Mark Ruffalo.

Your friendly neighbor Spider-Ma...
body_text:
The trailer for Sony Pictures and Marvel Studios' "Spider-Man: Brand New Day" starring Tom Holland, Zendeya, Jacob Batalon, Sadie Fink, Jon Bernthal and Mark Ruffalo.

Your friendly neighbor Spider-Man… is going through some hard times.

In "Spider-Man Brand New Day," Peter Parker (Tom Holland) is adapting to life in complete isolation in New York City. As you may or may not recall (based on the events of the film's 2021 predecessor "No Way Home"), Peter had everyone's memories erased after his identity had been exposed to the world, putting those he loved the most in danger.

After having lost his Aunt May (Marisa Tomei), Peter vowed he wouldn't let what happened to her happen to the love of his life, MJ (Zendaya), nor his best friend, Ned (Jacob Batalon). So their memories of him are gone and his only connection to them is him stalking Ned's Instagram videos showing him and MJ living their best lives as students at MIT, something they talked about doing in high school.

AS ‘THE ODYSSEY’ THRIVES AT THE BOX OFFICE, FRANCHISE FATIGURE HITS SUMMER WITH BOMBS LIKE ‘SUPERGIRL,’ ‘MOANA’

Tom Holland stars as Spider-Man in Columbia Pictures' "Spider-Man: Brand New Day." ( Courtesy of Sony Pictures)

Meanwhile, a mysterious, telepathic villain is wreaking havoc in the Big Apple, jumping from body to body in the search for something dubbed "V-Max." This foe can take over anyone's mind, but meets its match with Spider-Man, of course.

"Brand New Day" has a cast filled with familiar faces from the Marvel Cinematic Universe, like Bruce Banner aka The Incredible Hulk (Mark Ruffalo) and Frank Castle aka The Punisher (Jon Bernthal) as well as new ones like Detective Jean DeWolff (Liza Colón-Zayas of "The Bear" fame), who forms a partnership with Spider-Man — think a Batman/James Gordon dynamic — iconic Spider-Man foe Scorpion (Michael Mando) and Bill Metzger ("Severance" star Tramell Tillman), the chief of the U.S. Department of Damage Control created to repair the damage done from superhero fighting and contain whatever dangers that are left behind.

I would be remiss if I didn't mention "Stranger Things" breakout Sadie Sink, whose involvement in "Brand New Day" has been kept under wraps — and for good reason, since her role is a bit of a game changer. Sink continues to be a rising star based on her string of compelling performances.

'THE ODYSSEY' REVIEW: CHRISTOPHER NOLAN GOES EPIC WITH HIS MOST AMBITIOUS FILM TO DATE

Scorpian (Michael Mando) in Columbia Pictures' "Spider-Man: Brand New Day." (Jay Maidment/Sony Pictures Entertainment Inc. ©2026 CTMG)

The tone of "Brand New Day" is a bold departure from its three predecessors because of how Peter Parker grapples with loneliness, which is taking a toll on him physically — even affecting his superpowers. Tom Holland, fresh off the blockbuster hit "The Odyssey," will be web-slinging into another box office smash — but giving his strongest performance yet as Spider-Man, balancing the agony that his own isolation has brought him with the geeky charm audiences have grown to love over the years.

‘MOANA’ REVIEW: DWAYNE JOHNSON RETURNS FOR DISNEY'S LAZY LIVE-ACTION REMAKE THAT RESEMBLES AI SLOP

Zendaya — newly-married to Holland in real life, has plenty of on-screen chemistry with him for obvious reasons. And despite having her memory of Peter Parker erased in the last film, MJ has enough to work with (the same can't be said for Batalon's Ned, who's sadly sidelined here). Bernthal's The Punisher is a nice addition to the Spideyverse as the brute antihero has some comical exchanges with the lighthearted Spider-Man.

Jon Bernthal is The Punisher in Columbia Pictures' "Spider-Man: Brand New Day." (Jay Maidment/Sony Pictures Entertainment Inc. ©2026 CTMG)

Destin Daniel Cretton, who previously directed Marvel's "Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings," takes over the director's chair from Jon Watts, who spearheaded the previous Holland "Spider-Man" films, though the screenwriting duo Chris McKenna and Erik Sommers, return for the fourth installment.

There's a lot to balance in "Brand New Day" and Cretton handles it with care, particularly when it comes to the emotional elements to it — relying on a skill set he previously showcased in his highly underrated 2013 indie drama "Short Term 12."

'THE INVITE' REVIEW: SETH ROGEN, OLIVIA WILDE HOST ONE HILARIOUS DINNER PARTY YOU WON'T REGRET ATTENDING

Peter Parker (Tom Holland) in Columbia Pictures' "Spider-Man: Brand New Day." (Jay Maidment/Sony Pictures Entertainment Inc. ©2026 CTMG)

"Brand New Day" is more visually striking than its predecessors with well-choreographed action sequences. And Oscar-winning composer Michael Giacchino ("Up," "The Batman") delivers yet another fun score.

With a nearly two-and-a-half hour running time, "Brand New Day" does drag a bit. And like many of the Marvel films, it doesn't present us with a truly great villain that superhero movies deserve (see Heath Ledger's Joker, Willem Dafoe's Green Goblin and Alfred Molina's Doc Ock in the Tobey Maguire "Spider-Man" trilogy, etc.)

For the super Marvel fans out there, there is one post-credit scene at the end — offering a very mild teaser of what's to come for the beloved hero.

‘TOY STORY 5’ REVIEW: TOM HANKS, TIM ALLEN RETURN FOR TIMELY INSTALLMENT AS PIXAR GANG BATTLES RISE OF TECH

MJ (Zendaya) swings through the city with Spider-Man (Tom Holland) in Columbia Pictures' "Spider-Man: Brand New Day." ( Jay Maidment/Sony Pictures Entertainment Inc. ©2025 CTMG)

As the Marvel Cinematic Universe has broadly struggled in recent years, "Spider-Man: Brand New Day" gives it new life, thanks in large part to Holland at the helm. While it doesn't reinvent the wheel, this heartfelt superhero sequel will certainly satisfy fans and entertain audiences young and old.

"Spider-Man: Brand New Day" is rated PG-13 for sequences of action/violence and some language. Running time: 2 hours, 25 minutes. In theaters now.

Joseph A. Wulfsohn is a media reporter for Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to joseph.wulfsohn@fox.com and on Twitter: @JosephWulfsohn.

title: Huge great white spotted traveling up US and Canada as shark sightings surge
excerpt:
Contender, largest tagged male great white, heading north as overheating oceans alter range of several shark species

The largest tagged male great white shark in the Atlantic Ocean has been identifie...
body_text:
Contender, largest tagged male great white, heading north as overheating oceans alter range of several shark species

The largest tagged male great white shark in the Atlantic Ocean has been identified traveling up the US and Canada coastline amid a surge in sightings of sharks that are increasingly shifting their movement patterns due to the overheating of the oceans.

The great white shark, named Contender, is nearly 14ft long and weighs more than 1,650lbs. The hulking fish has been pinged in several locations off North Carolina and Maine as he headed north for the summer, with Contender’s last known location located off Nova Scotia in Canada on 11 July.

Contender is the largest male ever tagged in the Atlantic by Ocearch, a shark research organization, which first attached a satellite tag to his dorsal fin in January last year. The giant predator, thought to be 30 years old, shuttles between Florida and Canada in his seasonal migrations. Ocearch said it is confident that Contender, named after a research boat, is now summering in Canada.

The identification of Contender’s movements comes as shark sightings have surged in locations including New York and California. There have been 16 sightings of sharks just in July off Rockaway Beach in New York City, a situation that has spurred some nervousness. “It’s a little scary,” one beachgoer told NBC.

But scientists point out that while the chances of being attacked by a shark remains very small, rising ocean temperatures, caused by the human-driven climate crisis, are altering the range of several shark species, sometimes bringing them closer to where people are swimming or surfing.

“We are seeing evidence of a northward movement because of the warming waters and that means for there’s more chances to see sharks,” said Shannon Barry, a researcher at the Florida Institute of Technology who led recent research finding that bull sharks have moved up the US’s east coast.

“Bull sharks are definitely going to be more near shore – they can go into low-salinity environments such as estuaries and near rivers, so that is something to keep in mind,” she said. “There is a potential increase in human-shark interactions as they are moving into places where people go to swim and fish.”

This prospect does concern some people, Barry acknowledged, but she added that it was more striking that the morphing composition of the oceans was causing such a change.

The global water surface temperature hit a new record high last month, the latest in the string of remarkable recent heat records as the ocean, which soaks up 90% of the excess heat caused by the burning of fossil fuels, rapidly warms up and acidifies. A developing El Niño, a periodic climatic event, is also driving up ocean temperatures.

Most sharks do not like the cold and so are able to venture northwards as the oceans warm up and prey species distribution changes, although the extra heat may soon become so extreme that great white sharks face the risk of fatally overheating, researchers recently warned.

“The reaction should be concerning because we can see sharks are the canary in the coalmine to this problem,” Barry said. “Bull sharks generally hang out in south Florida and the Bahamas and now we are seeing them moving. That is something that people can see and think, ‘Oh, I can see the effect of climate change there.’”

This month, a man visiting a beach in Florida said he was bitten on the foot by a shark, causing the release of a “whole lot of blood” as he attempted to get his pregnant fiancee to safety. But there is little evidence of an increase in such incidents and attacks on people remain rare, with only 65 unprovoked shark bites on humans recorded worldwide in all of last year, with 25 of these in the US.

By contrast, humans kill about 100 million sharks a year by accidentally tangling them in fishing nets or actively catching them for sport, food or the shark fin trade. Removing sharks can damage whole marine ecosystems, Barry said. “Seeing a lot of sharks is usually a good thing; it means the surrounding food web is healthy,” she said.

Conservation measures and increased surveillance means that some shark numbers are recovering and they are being spotted more easily, according to Neil Hammerschlag, executive director of the Shark Research Foundation, but global heating is pushing them into places where they haven’t been seen before.

“We are seeing tiger sharks, for example, moving north of Cape Cod, and previously that would be very, very rare,” he said. “Still, fear of sharks shouldn’t deter anyone from enjoying the ocean. Sharks generally don’t want to be around people; they try to avoid us. We are like aliens to them.”

Hammerschlag added, though, that humans are “just visitors to the ocean and we should be shark aware”. This includes avoiding wearing shiny jewellery in the water, which can resemble the scales of a fish, or swimming at dusk or when there’s an unusual amount of fish activity.

“We have to be aware we are not the only ones in the ocean,” he said. “Sharks aren’t lurking in the water, they are living in the water. We are in their territory.”
